body:
Fixes the pip-audit failures in the vulnerability-scan workflow.

- `dnspython` GHSA-vvf4-9x63-8xvv: override to `>=2.9.2`, with marker `python_version >= '3.11'` (2.9.2 doesn't support 3.10, so no fix exists there).

## Verification
Ran `pip-audit` on `dnspython` and `opentelemetry-api` as pinned in `uv.lock` (not the full-environment audit that CI runs):

| | dnspython | opentelemetry-api | pip-audit |

| this PR | 2.9.2 | 1.45.2 | No known vulnerabilities found |

No unit test is added: this is a dependency bump, and the pip-audit job in the vulnerability-scan workflow is the regression check.

Mirrors the approach from #9451.
Closes #9452

title: fix(cli): read and write .env as UTF-8
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #9444

## Summary

`fetch_and_json_env_file`, `load_env_vars` and `write_env_file` opened `.env` without an encoding, so they used the platform default (cp1252 on Windows). A UTF-8 `.env` with non-ASCII text then made `fetch_and_json_env_file` return `{}` (deploy sends no variables) and `load_env_vars` raise `UnicodeDecodeError`, and `write_env_file` could not write a non-ASCII value. They now read and write UTF-8, matching `python-dotenv` and the `pyproject.toml` fix in #9414. Nothing else changes.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

- 4 new tests in `lib/cli/tests/test_utils.py`, using a fixture that makes text files default to ASCII (as on Windows or a C locale), so they behave the same on every OS: `load_env_vars` and `fetch_and_json_env_file` read a UTF-8 file, `write_env_file` writes UTF-8, and a non-ASCII value round-trips. All 4 fail on `main` and pass with this change.
- Reproduction from the issue: `{}` and two exceptions on `main`, the parsed values and a clean write with this change.
- `uv run ruff check lib/cli`, `uv run ruff format --check`, `uv run mypy lib/cli/src/crewai_cli/utils.py`: clean.
- `uv run pytest lib/cli/tests`: 2263 passed

## Additional context

Prepared with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude Code), so this should carry the `llm-generated` label. I reproduced the bug and reviewed and ran everything above.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow change to local .env I/O encoding; no auth or deploy protocol changes, only more predictable Unicode handling.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`.env` handling on Windows and C-locale machines** where the platform default encoding (e.g. cp1252) could not read or write UTF-8 content.
> 
> **`fetch_and_json_env_file`**, **`load_env_vars`**, and **`write_env_file`** now open `.env` with **`encoding="utf-8"`** instead of relying on the system default. That stops deploy flows from getting an empty dict when parsing non-ASCII UTF-8 files, avoids **`UnicodeDecodeError`** on load, and allows writing values like accented or CJK text.
> 
> Tests add an **`ascii_default_encoding`** fixture (simulates ASCII-default **`open`** / **`os.fdopen`**) plus four cases: UTF-8 read via load and fetch, UTF-8 write, and a non-ASCII round-trip.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ca5004d26a4d5a8a6036cf35b457f8bbb781759c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

body:
## Related issue

Fixes #9431

## Summary

The "Serve your agent over AG-UI" step in `docs/edge/en/guides/frontend/overview.mdx` shows two alternative FastAPI snippets. The `Flow` tab registers `path="/recipe"`, but the `Crew` tab registered `path="/research"`, while everything after that step — the CopilotKit runtime (`CrewAIAgent({ url: "http://localhost:8000/recipe" })`), `<CopilotKit agent="recipe">`, and the `CopilotSidebar` / `CopilotPopup` / `CopilotChat` options — targets the `recipe` agent on `/recipe`. A reader who follows the `Crew` tab ends up with a server and a frontend that never connect.

This PR registers the Crew example on `/recipe` too, and applies the same edit to the `ar`, `ko`, and `pt-BR` translations so the code blocks stay in parity, as the documentation section of CONTRIBUTING.md asks.

Only the endpoint string changes. `path` is arbitrary for `add_crewai_crew_fastapi_endpoint`, so the example stays valid, and `ResearchCrew` itself is untouched.

This also supersedes the first version of this PR, which was closed by the first-time contributor issue gate.

## Verification

- [ ] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior — not applicable, docs-only change with no runtime code
- [ ] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally — nothing to run; no Python or JavaScript sources touched

Checked instead:

- `git diff origin/main --stat` shows exactly 4 files with 1 line changed each: `docs/edge/{en,ar,ko,pt-BR}/guides/frontend/overview.mdx`.
- `grep -rn '"/research"\|localhost:8000/research'` over those four files returns no matches after the change.
- The changed line is identical in all four code blocks, so the translations stay in parity.

title: fix(deps): raise soupsieve floor to 4.0 for CVE-2026-126190
body:
## Related issue

pip-audit on main fails with:

```
Error: Found vulnerabilities in 1 package(s)
  - soupsieve==2.9.2: GHSA-4j63-6c4x-wfg4
  - soupsieve==2.9.2: GHSA-mmhr-3c5m-f64f
```

## Summary

- Raise the soupsieve floor to **4.0** on Python ≥3.11.5 (lock resolves 4.1). GHSA-mmhr-3c5m-f64f / CVE-2026-126190 (high) is fixed in 4.0.
- Raise the floor to **2.10** on Python <3.11.5. GHSA-4j63-6c4x-wfg4 / CVE-2026-126192 (medium) is fixed in 2.10, which is published on PyPI with Python >=3.10.
- Declare the same split floors in `lib/crewai-tools/pyproject.toml`, so consumers installing crewai-tools get them.
- Python 3.10 and 3.11.0–3.11.4 cannot install 4.x, so they remain exposed to GHSA-mmhr-3c5m-f64f until 3.10 support is dropped.

## Verification

- [x] `uv lock` (uv 0.13.4) resolves soupsieve 2.10 below Python 3.11.5 and 4.1 at 3.11.5+.
- [ ] Vulnerability scan on this PR reports no soupsieve findings
- [ ] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior — dependency floor only

## Additional context

soupsieve 4.0 changes selector behavior that Beautiful Soup inherits: the contents of an HTML `template` are no longer part of the surrounding document, and the contents of an `iframe` are no longer a separate document. Results for ordinary selectors are otherwise unchanged. Since crewAI uses BS4/unstructured for document parsing (not DOM rendering), this should not cause behavioral changes.

Based on the work in #9422 by @Vidit-Ostwal.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Dependency-only security bump with documented Python-version splits; main residual risk is unchanged exposure on Python <3.11.5 and possible subtle BS4 selector semantics on soupsieve 4.x for template/iframe handling.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR **raises the minimum `soupsieve` version** to address pip-audit findings (GHSA-4j63-6c4x-wfg4 and GHSA-mmhr-3c5m-f64f) that blocked the previous `>=2.9.2` floor.
> 
> On **Python ≥3.11.5**, dependencies and uv overrides now require **`soupsieve>=4.0`** (lock resolves 4.1). On **Python <3.11.5**, the floor is **`soupsieve>=2.10`** because 4.x needs Python ≥3.11.5. The same split is declared in **`crewai-tools`** so direct installs inherit it, not only workspace uv overrides.
> 
> **`uv.lock`** is refreshed: resolution markers distinguish 3.11.0–3.11.4 from 3.11.5+, and `beautifulsoup4` pulls the matching `soupsieve` pin. Python 3.10 and early 3.11 remain on 2.10 and stay partially exposed to the high-severity descendant-combinator issue until those Python versions are dropped.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9bb6f652ae493194e89d6c33f9e36efe87e3a76f. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(project): accept an llm mapping in agents.yaml
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #9420

## Summary

`@CrewBase` checked every `llm` and `function_calling_llm` value in `agents.yaml` against the crew's `@llm` methods with `llms.get(value)`. A mapping of LLM settings (`model`, `temperature`, ...), which `Agent` itself accepts through `create_llm()`, is a `dict` and can't be used as a key. So the crew failed with `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'` before any agent was built.

The lookup now runs only for strings. Any other value is passed through to the agent, as a model name that isn't an `@llm` method already was. `AgentConfig` now types the two fields as `str | dict[str, Any]`.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

- New `test_agent_llm_given_as_a_mapping_in_yaml` in `lib/crewai/tests/test_project.py` loads an `agents.yaml` whose `llm` and `function_calling_llm` are mappings, and checks that the agent's LLMs carry the configured temperatures. It fails on main with `TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'` and passes with this change. No LLM call is made.
- `pytest lib/crewai/tests/test_project.py` (Windows 11, Python 3.13): 14 passed, 11 failed. The same 11 tests fail on main on this machine (async-decorator, kickoff-hook and MCP tests).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on `crew_base.py`: clean. `mypy` on `crew_base.py`: no new errors. Its one error is the missing `crewai_tools` package in this environment, and main shows it too.

## Additional context

Written with an AI coding agent (Claude Opus 5.5 in OpenCode). CONTRIBUTING asks for the `llm-generated` label on AI-assisted PRs; I can't add labels, so could a maintainer add it?

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow, backward-compatible change to YAML agent config resolution with a focused regression test; string-based `@llm` references behave as before.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes crew initialization when `agents.yaml` specifies **`llm`** or **`function_calling_llm`** as inline settings (e.g. `model`, `temperature`) instead of a string reference to an `@llm` factory method.
> 
> `@CrewBase` previously always used `llms.get(value)` on those fields, which raised **`TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict'`** before agents were built. Resolution now runs the factory lookup **only for strings**; dict values are left on the agent config so **`Agent` / `create_llm()`** can build the LLM as before. **`AgentConfig`** types for both fields are widened to **`str | dict[str, Any]`**.
> 
> A new test loads YAML with mapping-style LLMs and asserts the resulting agent LLMs have the configured temperatures (no network call).
>

title: Add SincorSettlementTool (escrowed CNP auction settlement)
body:
## Description

Crews that delegate work to other agents have no native way to bid the work out, escrow the payment, or see what the platform took. This PR adds a `crewai-tools` integration for the SINCOR agent marketplace:

- **`SincorSettlementTool`** (headline import) — post a CNP (Contract Net Protocol) auction task, list bids, accept one, and settle. Settlement returns the gross amount, the **5% platform fee**, and the net to worker — the fee is explicit, never hidden.
- **`SincorAuctionTool`** — the auction tool `SincorSettlementTool` aliases.
- **`SincorEscrowTool`** — create escrowed tasks, check status, release, refund, fetch a settlement record.

All three are backed by a small typed client for the SINCOR platform API, bundled inside the tool directory (standard library only, no new hard dependency). Tests inject a client with a custom transport, matching the repo's mocking conventions.

**What is live vs. pilot — stated plainly.** CNP auctions, escrowed task creation, pool settlement (5% fee), and KYA telemetry are live on https://getsincor.com today, and the AP2 discovery document is served at https://getsincor.com/.well-known/ap2.json. SEAL (EIP-712 settlement authorization) and SIGIL (state-commitment verification) are integration-pilot framing — designed interfaces, not settled mainnet primitives. **No SINCOR settlement contract is deployed on Base mainnet**, and this tool does not claim otherwise; the tool README carries the same disclosure. The SINCOR token is platform access, not an investment.

The verified-payment companion package is declared as an optional extra pinned to the published release:

```toml
sincor-x402 = ["sincor-x402==0.1.0"]   # https://pypi.org/project/sincor-x402/
```

so `pip install "crewai-tools[sincor-x402]"` version-matches the x402 verified-payment surface with these tools.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Changes

- New tool directory `lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/tools/sincor_settlement_tool/` (`sincor_settlement_tool.py`, `sincor_client.py`, `README.md`)
- Registered `SincorAuctionTool`, `SincorEscrowTool`, `SincorSettlementTool` in both `crewai_tools/__init__.py` and `crewai_tools/tools/__init__.py` (+ `__all__`)
- `sincor-x402` optional-dependency extra in `lib/crewai-tools/pyproject.toml`
- Tests: `lib/crewai-tools/tests/tools/sincor_settlement_tool_test.py`

## Test report (run by the author pre-submission)

Environment: Python 3.12 venv with `crewai 1.15.40` (matching this repo's current version) installed from PyPI; the tools package imported from this tree.

- New tests: **3 passed** — full loop (post → bid → accept → settle) asserting gross 100 / fee 5.0 / rate 0.05 / net 95.0; escrow create + refund; alias subclass check
- `import crewai_tools` smoke: all three tool names present in `crewai_tools.__all__` and importable from the top level
- Note: the repo's root pytest `addopts` reference a `--block-network` plugin flag that is not published on PyPI under that name; the run above used `-o addopts=""`. The tests are in-memory (mock transport) and touch no network either way. Repo CI, which has the full dev environment, is the authoritative run.

Not included, deliberately: a docs MDX page under `docs/edge/en/` — left out to keep this diff minimal per the repo's contribution guidelines; the in-directory README follows the per-tool README precedent (e.g. Exa). Happy to add the docs page in this PR or a follow-up if maintainers prefer.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> New external API integration (default `https://getsincor.com`) can move real escrow/settlement funds when used in production; core package stays stdlib-only but payment flows warrant careful review.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **SINCOR marketplace integration** to `crewai-tools` so agents can escrow payments, run CNP auctions, and settle with an explicit **5% platform fee** breakdown instead of opaque paid calls.
> 
> The new `sincor_settlement_tool` package bundles a stdlib-only `SincorClient` plus three `BaseTool` exports — **`SincorSettlementTool`** (alias of auction flow), **`SincorAuctionTool`**, and **`SincorEscrowTool`** — with action-based JSON responses for create/post, bids, accept, settle/release, refund, and status. Tools are registered in both package `__init__` modules, documented via an in-directory README (live vs pilot disclosures), and covered by in-memory mock transport tests.
> 
> Also adds the optional extra **`sincor-x402==0.1.0`** in `pyproject.toml` for verified x402 payments alongside these tools.
>

title: fix(core): read pyproject.toml as utf-8 in project helpers
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #9413

## Summary

`_get_project_attribute()`, behind `get_project_name()`, `get_project_version()` and `get_project_description()`, opened `pyproject.toml` without an encoding. On Windows the file was decoded with the ANSI code page (cp1252) instead of UTF-8. A `pyproject.toml` with CJK text, or a letter such as "č" or "Ł", made `crewai deploy` and `crewai tool publish` stop with "Unable to read 'project.name'". title: fix(flow): keep earlier step outputs across a human-feedback resume
body:
## Summary

A flow that pauses for human review lost the outputs of earlier steps when it resumed. Approving still worked. Rejecting reruns the reviewed step, and when that step read an earlier output through `outputs.<step>`, the resume failed:

`failed to evaluate CEL expression 'outputs.compare_versions.raw': ("no such member in mapping: 'compare_versions'", KeyError)`

On pause, `crewai` saved the flow state but not the step outputs, which live only in memory. `from_pending()` then started with an empty list. Flows that keep data in `self.state` were not affected. Declared flows that read `outputs.<step>` were. 

The fix saves the outputs in `PendingFeedbackContext.method_outputs` at both pause sites and restores them in `from_pending()`. The field round-trips through `to_dict` / `from_dict`, so any persistence backend keeps it. Rows saved before this change load with `None` and behave as before.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

- New test `test_rejected_review_rerun_reads_outputs_of_steps_before_the_pause` uses real `SQLiteFlowPersistence` to pause, reject, pause again, then approve. It fails on `main` with the error above and passes with this change.

## Additional context

- Flows already paused before this ships have no saved outputs, so them will still fail.
- After a resume, rich step outputs (for example Pydantic models) come back as JSON-safe dicts. CEL already reads them that way.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches HITL persistence and resume semantics for declared flows using `outputs.*`; backward-compatible for new pauses but pre-existing pending rows still lack saved outputs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes human-in-the-loop pause/resume dropping in-memory step outputs so **`outputs.<step>`** CEL expressions still work after **`Flow.from_pending()`**, especially when a rejected review reruns a step that references an earlier step.
> 
> **`PendingFeedbackContext`** now carries **`method_outputs`**, serialized through **`to_dict` / `from_dict`** like other resume metadata. On every HITL pause (kickoff and resume), the runtime copies **`self._method_outputs`** into the context before **`save_pending_feedback`**, and **`from_pending()`** restores them onto the new instance. Older pending rows without the field stay **`None`** and behave as before.
> 
> Adds an integration test that pauses, rejects (re-pause), then approves via SQLite persistence and asserts **`outputs.compare_versions`** resolves through the full cycle.
>

title: fix(llm): strip cache_breakpoint marker on the LiteLLM path (OSS-272)
body:
Fixes OSS-272.

## Problem

Since 1.14.5, Groq requests fail on every run:

```
litellm.BadRequestError: GroqException - 'messages.0': for 'role:system' the following must be satisfied [('messages.0': property 'cache_breakpoint' is unsupported)]
```

`AgentExecutor._setup_messages` tags messages with an internal `cache_breakpoint` flag (`crewai/llms/cache.py`). Native providers drop it in `BaseLLM._format_messages` (Anthropic translates it to `cache_control` first). The LiteLLM fallback `LLM` never goes through that method, so the flag was forwarded to the provider. Strict APIs such as Groq reject the whole request. Any model routed through LiteLLM (Cohere, SambaNova, ...) is exposed.

## Changes

**1. `fix(llm): strip cache_breakpoint marker on the LiteLLM path`** (`llm.py`)
- `LLM._prepare_completion_params` now copies each message that carries the flag and pops the key from the copy.
- The copy matters: the executor reuses one message buffer across tool-loop iterations, so mutating in place would erase the markers after the first call and defeat Anthropic caching.
- All `litellm.completion` / `acompletion` call sites build their params here, so sync, async and streaming are covered.
- Non-dict messages are passed through unchanged, so the existing `TypeError` in `_format_messages_for_provider` still fires.
- Unit tests in `tests/llms/test_prompt_cache.py`: the flag is absent from the outgoing params, and the input list keeps its markers across repeated calls.

**2. `test(llm): add Groq cassette test ...` and `test(llm): drop Groq cassette test`**
- I first added a VCR cassette test (real `Agent.kickoff` through OpenRouter, pinned to Groq), but the recorded cassette was ~14 MB, so the follow-up commit removes it again. Net effect on the diff: none.
- Coverage comes from the unit tests in commit 1.

**3. `refactor(llm): type cleaned messages as list[LLMMessage]`**
- Types the cleaned message list as `list[LLMMessage]` (with a `cast` on the copied dict) so it matches `messages`. No behavior change.

## Verification

Ran against the real Groq API with the model from the ticket repro (`groq/openai/gpt-oss-20b`), via `Agent(...).kickoff("Say hi in one word.")`, spying on what is handed to `litellm.completion`:

| `llm.py` | Payload to LiteLLM | Live Groq call |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | `cache_breakpoint` leaked on `system` and `user` | `400`: `GroqException - 'messages.0': for 'role:system' ... property 'cache_breakpoint' is unsupported` |
| This PR | no `cache_breakpoint` | `OK` (got a response) |

Also checked through OpenRouter (Llama 3.3 70B, pinned to Groq upstream): same result.

Other checks:
- LiteLLM-related suites (`tests/llms/litellm`, `test_base_llm.py`, `test_llm.py`, streaming/usage-event tests, `test_prompt_cache.py`): 149 passed, 12 skipped.
- ruff, ruff format and mypy pass via pre-commit.

## Notes

LiteLLM-routed Anthropic models still don't get prompt caching from this marker (LiteLLM never understood it). Translating it to `cache_control` there would be a separate feature.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(mcp): report non-timeout MCP errors with their own type instead of as a timeout
body:
Fixes #9438

## What the user sees

When an MCP server rejects a request (for example HTTP 401 or 404), the error is raised inside the MCP client's task group. `MCPToolWrapper._execute_tool` treated any exception that had a `__cause__`, or whose text contained "TaskGroup" / "unhandled errors", as `asyncio.TimeoutError`. The wrapper then retried the call 3 times and told the model "Connection timed out after 60 seconds": the agent retried a request that can never succeed, and the real reason was lost.

## Fix

Classify by exception type, not by text. `_execute_tool` flattens (nested) exception groups into their leaf exceptions:

- if any leaf is a `TimeoutError`, it is a timeout and is retried as before;
- otherwise the leaves are reported as "MCP execution error: <Type>: <message>" and the call is not retried.

A plain exception that is not a group is re-raised unchanged and goes through the existing handling.

## Test

`lib/crewai/tests/mcp/test_tool_wrapper_errors.py` stubs the MCP client and session so `call_tool` raises an exception group:

- a group containing an HTTP 401-like error: the message names the error type and "401", does not say "timed out", and `call_tool` is awaited once (before the fix: 3 attempts and "Connection timed out");
- a group containing a `TimeoutError`: still reported as a timeout and retried 3 times.

Both pass with the change; the first fails without it. `ruff check` is clean.

Written with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code) and reviewed and run before submitting, hence the `llm-generated` label.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized error-classification change in MCP tool execution with targeted tests; retry behavior for true timeouts is preserved.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **misclassified MCP failures** where HTTP errors and other non-timeout problems from the client's task group were surfaced as connection timeouts, triggering useless retries and hiding the real error.
> 
> `MCPToolWrapper` now **flattens nested exception groups** via `_leaf_exceptions`: only leaves that are `asyncio.TimeoutError` still map to timeout handling and **exponential retry**; other grouped failures become **`MCPExecutionError`** with typed leaf messages and **no retry**. `_execute_single_attempt` catches `MCPExecutionError` and returns an `MCP execution error: …` string.
> 
> Adds **`test_tool_wrapper_errors.py`** with mocked MCP sessions to assert HTTP 401-like groups report the actual error once, while timeout groups still retry three times.

title: fix(llm): run after_llm_call hooks on async calls
body:
Fixes #9355

## Summary

`LLM.call()` runs the global `after_llm_call` hooks on string responses, but `LLM.acall()` returned straight from `_ahandle_streaming_response` / `_ahandle_non_streaming_response`. A hook that rewrites responses — redacting secrets, enforcing formatting, appending citations — applied to `llm.call(...)` and was silently skipped for `await llm.acall(...)`. The native provider classes invoke the hooks on both paths; only the LiteLLM-backed `LLM` class was missing the async side.

The async path now captures the handler result and passes string responses through the same helper as the sync path:

```python
if self._effective_stream():
    result = await self._ahandle_streaming_response(...)
else:
    result = await self._ahandle_non_streaming_response(...)

if isinstance(result, str):
    result = self._invoke_after_llm_call_hooks(messages, result, from_agent)

return result

title: fix(cli): exit with the uv status when crewai install fails
body:

## Summary

`crewai install` printed a failed `uv sync` and exited `0`. `install_crew()` only re-raises when the caller opts in with `raise_on_error=True`, and the CLI command used the default, unlike the `deploy` and `run` paths which already translate the failure into `SystemExit(e.returncode)`. title: feat(cli): pick tools for standalone agents and add them later
body:
Resolves [OSS-270](https://linear.app/crewai/issue/OSS-270/extend-tool-setup-to-single-agent-flow-and-standalone-commands).

## What

- **`crewai create agent`** (JSON/YAML, interactive terminal) now opens the same tool picker and CrewAI Platform setup as `crewai create crew`: accordion picker, per-app action selection, and AMP sign-in plus integration validation. Picking and auth run before any files are written, so a cancelled sign-in leaves no partial project.
- **`crewai tool add [TOOLS...]`** adds tools to an existing agent project. With no arguments it opens the picker; otherwise it takes references such as `SerperDevTool`, `platform:gmail/send-email` or `custom:my_tool`. Platform app and action names are checked against the catalog, and new platform apps are validated on AMP before the definition changes.
- **`crewai tool setup`** reads the `platform:` tools already in the agent definition, validates them on AMP and saves `CREWAI_ENTERPRISE_ACTION_AUTH_TOKEN` to `.env` (for example after cloning a project).
- Docs: `concepts/cli.mdx` and `guides/agents/standalone-agent-projects.mdx`, synced to `ar`, `ko` and `pt-BR`.

## How

The new `crewai_cli/agent_tools.py` reuses the existing onboarding helpers from `create_json_crew.py` (`_select_tools`, `_select_platform_actions`, `_setup_platform_auth`), so the crew and agent flows share one picker and one AMP setup path. It only adds the code that edits the definition:

- New tools are appended to the definition's `tools` list; tools already present are skipped.
- `agent.json` is rewritten with 2-space indentation; `agent.yaml` keeps the scaffold's layout (block scalars for multi-line strings, indented lists).
- The `crewai` dependency becomes `crewai[tools]` when a non-`custom:` tool is added, since crewai_tools and platform tools need that extra.

## Reviewer notes

- **Python agents** (`--format python`) skip the picker, and `tool add` points the user to `Agent(tools=[...])`; editing `agent.py` safely is out of scope.
- **Comments:** definitions are rewritten as plain JSON/YAML, so comments are not preserved. An unparseable file (for example JSON with comments) gets a clear error instead of being overwritten.
- **Non-interactive runs** (CI, piped stdin, `CREWAI_DMN`) are unchanged for `create agent`; `tool add` without arguments asks for tool names there.
- **JSON crews:** `tool add` targets standalone agent projects only. Adding tools to an existing JSON crew would need an agent-selection prompt; that could be a follow-up.
- **Shared private helpers:** `agent_tools.py` imports underscore-prefixed functions from `create_json_crew.py` to keep this diff small. They could move to a shared module later.

## Testing

- `lib/cli/tests/test_agent_tools.py` (18 tests) covers JSON and YAML `tool add`, skipping tools already present, invalid platform references, unparseable definitions, cancelled AMP setup leaving files untouched, `tool setup`, onboarding during `create agent`, and the Python-agent paths.
- The CLI suites (`test_create_agent`, `test_create_crew`, `test_cli`, `test_create_unified`, `tests/tools`) pass: 392 tests. ruff, ruff-format and mypy are clean.
- End to end: scaffolded JSON and YAML agents, ran `crewai tool add SerperDevTool FileReadTool`, and loaded the JSON agent with `load_agent_project`, which resolved all 5 tools. The interactive picker was opened in a real terminal.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches CLI auth/platform integration and writes agent definitions plus `.env` tokens; changes are well-tested but affect security-sensitive AMP setup paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> Extends standalone **JSON/YAML agent** workflows so tool selection and CrewAI Platform setup match **`crewai create crew`**: interactive **`crewai create agent`** now runs the shared picker and AMP validation **before** writing files, avoiding partial projects when sign-in is cancelled.
> 
> Adds **`crewai tool add`** and **`crewai tool setup`** to append tools to `agent.json`/`agent.yaml`, bump **`crewai[tools]`** when needed, validate platform apps/actions, and persist **`CREWAI_ENTERPRISE_ACTION_AUTH_TOKEN`** in `.env`. Python agents are excluded from definition editing.
> 
> Introduces **`crewai_cli/agent_tools.py`** reusing crew onboarding helpers, plus a fix in **`_setup_platform_auth`** that restores machine proxy/CA/TLS settings after `crewai_tools` import-time `load_dotenv()` so project `.env` cannot steer AMP requests.
>

title: fix(llms): keep a streamed delta when its chunk also carries usage
body:
## Related issue

No issue covers this. Found while testing the DeepInfra provider added in #7459.

## Summary

When a streamed chunk carries `usage`, the chat-completions streaming handlers in `OpenAICompletion` record the usage and skip the rest of the chunk. That fits OpenAI, which reports usage only on a final chunk whose `choices` is empty. But the same handlers serve every OpenAI-compatible server: `openrouter`, `deepseek`, `ollama`, `hosted_vllm`, `cerebras`, `dashscope`, `deepinfra`, Snowflake and any `custom_openai` base URL. When such a server attaches usage to a chunk that still has a delta, crewAI drops that chunk's text, tool-call fragment and `finish_reason`.

vLLM does this on every chunk when the request sets `stream_options.continuous_usage_stats`. On `main` the answer comes back empty, although the tokens were generated and counted:

```python
llm = LLM(
    model="deepinfra/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash",  # DeepInfra honours the vLLM option
    stream=True,
    stream_options={"include_usage": True, "continuous_usage_stats": True},
)
llm.call(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: one two three four five"}])
# main:        ''                         (completion_tokens=6)
# this branch: 'one two three four five'  (completion_tokens=6)
```

The fix records the usage and keeps processing the chunk, in the sync, async and async structured-output handlers. The check that follows already skips a chunk with no choices, so OpenAI's usage-only chunk is handled as before. The LiteLLM path in `llm.py` already reads usage and choices from the same chunk.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

- Four new tests in `lib/crewai/tests/llms/openai/test_openai.py`, where every chunk carries usage and a usage-only chunk follows: sync text, sync tool call, async text, async structured output. Each asserts the full result and the final usage totals. All four fail on `main` and pass here.
- `uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/llms/openai lib/crewai/tests/llms/openai_compatible lib/crewai/tests/llms/snowflake -q` - 453 passed, 1 skipped
- `uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/llms -q` fails the same 345 tests on `main` and on this branch in my environment, all in the Anthropic, Azure, Google and Bedrock suites, whose SDKs are not installed there. The only difference is the four new tests passing.
- `uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check` on the changed code, `uv run mypy` on `completion.py` - clean
- live against api.deepinfra.com with `continuous_usage_stats`:

| Path | `main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| sync | `''` | `'one two three four five'` |
| async | `''` | `'one two three four five'` |
| async structured output | `''`, with a logged parse error | `Count(words=['one', 'two', 'three'])` |
| sync tool call | `''` | the `get_weather` call with `{"city": "Sofia"}` |

  With the default `stream_options={"include_usage": True}`, both return the full answer.

## Additional context

No behaviour change for OpenAI itself: its usage chunk has empty `choices`.

When every chunk carries usage, the recorded usage is the last chunk's, which holds the running totals.

How this surfaced: DeepInfra's API used to attach usage to the finish chunk, which also carried the last delta, so a streamed answer through `deepinfra/` lost its tail. We changed that on our side in October, and usage now arrives on a trailing chunk with empty `choices`, as OpenAI sends it. The default DeepInfra path is therefore no longer affected, but the client still drops deltas for any server that sends the other shape.

The code was written with AI assistance (Claude Code), so per CONTRIBUTING the `llm-generated` label applies - I can't set labels on this repo, please add it.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Targeted streaming parser change with regression tests; OpenAI’s usage-only chunks remain handled via the empty-choices check.
> 
> **Overview**
> **OpenAI-compatible streaming no longer drops content when a chunk includes token usage.** Sync, async, and async structured-output paths in `OpenAICompletion` used to `continue` after recording `usage`, which matches OpenAI’s usage-only final chunk but breaks servers (e.g. vLLM with `continuous_usage_stats`) that attach running usage on the same chunks as text, tool-call fragments, or `finish_reason`.
> 
> The handlers still extract usage from those chunks and still skip chunks with empty `choices`, so OpenAI-style trailing usage-only chunks behave as before. **Four tests** simulate “usage on every chunk” for sync text, sync tool calls, async text, and async structured output.
>

title: fix(tools): keep Annotated parameter constraints in inferred tool schemas
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #9093

## Summary

`CrewStructuredTool.from_function()` inferred its argument schema with `get_type_hints(func)`. Without `include_extras=True`, Python strips `Annotated[...]` metadata before Pydantic receives the parameter type, so any `Field(...)` constraints and descriptions authored inside `Annotated` were dropped from the generated schema.

The result was that the tool's JSON schema lost the authored constraints and `invoke()` / `ainvoke()` accepted values that violated them:

```python
def positive_count(count: Annotated[int, Field(gt=0, description="Positive count")]) -> int:
    """Return a positive count."""
    return count

tool = CrewStructuredTool.from_function(positive_count)
tool.args_schema.model_json_schema()["properties"]["count"]
# before: {'title': 'Count', 'type': 'integer'}
# after:  {'title': 'Count', 'type': 'integer', 'description': 'Positive count', 'exclusiveMinimum': 0}

tool.invoke({"count": 0})
# before: 0            (constraint ignored)
# after:  ValueError: Arguments validation failed: ...
```

The fix resolves the hints with `include_extras=True`, so the `Annotated` metadata reaches Pydantic and becomes part of the schema as authored.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

- Added `test_from_function_keeps_annotated_parameter_constraints` and `test_from_function_keeps_annotated_parameter_constraints_on_ainvoke` to `lib/crewai/tests/tools/test_structured_tool.py`. On `main` both fail (the schema has no `exclusiveMinimum`, and the invalid call does not raise); with this change they pass.
- `pytest tests/tools/test_structured_tool.py` — 27 passed.
- `pytest tests/tools/` — 297 passed. The two `tests/tools/test_tool_failure.py::TestPlatformActionTool` failures and the `tests/tools/agent_tools/test_read_file_tool.py` import error also fail on `main` in this environment and are unrelated to this change.
- `ruff check` is clean on the changed files.

## Additional context

This change is scoped to the `CrewStructuredTool.from_function()` schema inference path. `BaseTool`'s annotation resolution is tracked separately in #7626, which touches `base_tool.py` only; the two changes do not overlap.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow change to schema inference in `CrewStructuredTool.from_function()` with regression tests; no auth or data-path impact, though stricter validation may surface previously ignored invalid tool calls.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`CrewStructuredTool.from_function()` now preserves `Annotated` parameter metadata when inferring argument schemas.**
> 
> Schema inference in `_create_schema_from_function` resolves hints with `get_type_hints(..., include_extras=True)` instead of the default, so `Annotated[int, Field(...)]` constraints and descriptions reach Pydantic and show up in the generated JSON schema. **`invoke()` and `ainvoke()`** therefore reject arguments that violate authored `Field` rules (for example `gt=0`) instead of accepting bare integer types.
> 
> Tests cover sync and async validation paths for annotated constraints.
>

title: fix(agent): stop an agent whose apps CrewAI AMP cannot resolve
body:
An agent whose `apps` CrewAI AMP named as unresolvable (not connected, or unknown to AMP) warned and then ran with no tools, so the model invented what the apps would have returned: a fake Asana task with a valid-looking ID and URL. Now `Agent.get_platform_tools` raises `PlatformAppsUnavailableError` naming those apps, so a local run fails the way a deployed run does.

- Scope: `Agent.get_platform_tools`, which serves `Agent.kickoff`/`kickoff_async` and `Crew.kickoff`/`kickoff_async`. Other resolution failures (no token, AMP unreachable) still only warn.
- Compatibility: behavior change for code that relied on a warning plus a tool-less run. The warning now names a YAML-folded role (`role: >`) without its trailing newline, so filters like `r"Agent .* declares apps"` match crew agents too.
- Tests: the raise, and that each of the four kickoff entry points stops before the LLM. On `main` the same tests reach the LLM.
- Docs: `concepts/agent-capabilities` notes the raise (en, ar, ko, pt-BR). `enterprise-api.{en,base,ko,pt-BR}.yaml` documents the kickoff check for every token, selectors as declared, and the new `agents` list, which ships with crewAI-enterprise https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI-enterprise/pull/1437.
- Out: renaming or normalizing `Agent.role` itself (agent knowledge collections are named by role), hierarchical crews at kickoff, `app@connection` selectors at kickoff.

title: feat: make gpt-6-luna crewAI's default model everywhere
body:
crewAI's default models were a mix: `gpt-4.1-mini` for agents with no `llm`, `gpt-5.4-mini` for memory, crew planning and `crewai test`, `gpt-6.1-sol` in the agent templates, and older models in a few tools. Every default is now `gpt-6-luna`. On the native OpenAI provider, GPT-6 models also count as vision models and the tools retry is remembered, so the new default works for images and doesn't pay an extra request per tool turn.

- **Defaults:**
  - `DEFAULT_LLM_MODEL` in crewai and in the CLI (a test keeps them equal), Memory, crew planning, the OpenAI agents adapter, `crewai test --model`, and the `crewai create agent` templates (still on `api="responses"`).
  - OCRTool, without its `temperature=0.7`: Luna rejects any temperature but the default with a 400.
  - VisionTool: `easy` and `medium` (the default) use Luna; `hard` uses `gpt-6.1-sol`.
  - Weaviate and Stagehand are unchanged, since they hand the model name to an outside service.
- **Provider fixes the new default needs:**
  - `supports_multimodal()` includes `gpt-6` on both the native and LiteLLM paths; before this, a default agent given `input_files` raised `ValueError`.
  - When a model's function tools on `/v1/chat/completions` succeed only with `reasoning_effort="none"`, that's remembered per endpoint and model, so later tool calls send it up front.
- **Compatibility:**
  - Users with no `llm` and no `MODEL`/`OPENAI_MODEL_NAME` now run on `gpt-6-luna`. It reasons by default, gets no stop words (they're applied on the client), and returns a 400 for any temperature but 1.
  - A gateway set through `OPENAI_BASE_URL` with `MODEL` unset must serve `gpt-6-luna`.
- **Tests:**
  - New: the CLI/core default parity, GPT-6 vision on both paths, the default agent taking images, the learned tools setting on sync/async/streaming per endpoint, and OCRTool's default.
  - Updated pins: planning, `crewai test`, the agent templates.

title: fix(memory): skip unchanged recall searches
body:
Refs #7838

## Summary

Deep recall re-ran the same successful storage search after every exploration round even when no retrieval inputs changed. That added redundant storage work and replaced the enriched findings with an identical search result.

This focused PR1 change:
- records the effective search plan for the current recall;
- skips `re_search` when the plan is unchanged and a prior search completed successfully, preserving enriched findings;
- distinguishes all-failed storage attempts from successful empty searches, so failures are still retried;
- adds deterministic regressions for both paths.

Query rewriting and evidence-gap refinement remain outside this PR.

## Validation

- `python -m compileall -q lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/recall_flow.py lib/crewai/tests/memory/test_recall_flow.py`
- `git diff --check`

The local environment does not have `uv`, `pytest`, or repository dependencies installed, so the focused pytest run could not be executed here.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Targeted recall-path optimization with state excluded from serialization; behavior change only avoids redundant storage calls and preserves enriched findings.
> 
> **Overview**
> Deep recall was calling storage again after every exploration round even when retrieval inputs were unchanged, which duplicated work and overwrote **enriched** `chunk_findings` with a fresh search.
> 
> The flow now builds a canonical **`_search_plan()`** (embeddings, scopes, filters, limit) and persists **`last_search_plan`** / **`last_search_succeeded`** on state. **`re_search`** returns existing findings when the plan matches and at least one search attempt succeeded; failed runs still retry. A successful search with **no** tasks (no embedding×scope work) counts as succeeded so empty plans are not retried forever.
> 
> New tests lock in skip-on-unchanged-plan and retry-after-failure behavior.
>

title: feat(tools): add StallRowPageMetadataTool — first x402 pay-per-call tool
body:
Resolves #9295

## What this adds

`StallRowPageMetadataTool` — a new tool in `crewai_tools` that fetches one web page's declared metadata in a single call: title, description, canonical URL, OpenGraph and Twitter card fields, document language, favicon, the h1/h2 heading outline, and word count. It wraps StallRow's live `POST /v1/page-metadata` endpoint and mirrors the layout of the existing API tools (pydantic args schema, `env_vars` declaration, package README, docs page, unit tests, regenerated `tool.specs.json` entry).

```python
from crewai_tools import StallRowPageMetadataTool

tool = StallRowPageMetadataTool()
result = tool.run(url="https://www.x402.org/")
# {"url": ..., "title": "x402 — internet-native payments", ...,
#  "headings": {"h1": ["x402"], "h2": ["How it works"]}, "word_count": 120}
```

## Why

CrewAI has no pay-per-call tool today — there is no x402 support anywhere in the codebase. API-key tools force users to create accounts and manage subscriptions for utilities they may call a handful of times. With x402, payment *is* the auth: an agent pays $0.005 USDC per call, only when it calls, with no signup. Page metadata is the highest-frequency shape for this (an agent checks a page's identity and outline before deciding whether the full content is worth fetching), which makes it the right first tool of this class.

## How payment works

- The endpoint answers HTTP 402 with an x402 v2 challenge; the bundled `x402_client.py` helper selects the `exact`/Base requirement, signs an EIP-3009 `TransferWithAuthorization` as EIP-712 typed data, and retries with the `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header. The service's facilitator settles USDC on Base server-side. The challenge's `extensions` (Bazaar discovery declaration) are echoed into the payment payload, as facilitator catalogues index from the payload.
- **Price: $0.005 USDC per call.** A hard per-call cap (the tool's `max_price_usdc` parameter, or `STALLROW_MAX_PRICE_USDC`) defaults to exactly that price and refuses any higher price *before anything is signed*.
- The payer key is read from the `STALLROW_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY` environment variable only — never a tool parameter, never logged. With no wallet configured, the tool fails closed with an explanation and pays nothing. The tool module imports and constructs fine without the signer installed; `eth-account` is imported lazily at payment time and declared via `package_dependencies` plus a new `crewai-tools[stallrow]` optional-dependencies extra.

## Disclosure

I operate the StallRow service this tool calls — this is a first-party service tool, in the same sense as the Apify and Firecrawl tools already in this directory. The endpoint is live, listed in the CDP Bazaar, and priced at $0.005/call. I'm disclosing the affiliation plainly so maintainers and users can weigh it; the spend cap and fail-closed defaults are designed so an agent can never be charged more than the stated price for a call.

## Tests

- 10 new unit tests (`lib/crewai-tools/tests/tools/test_stallrow_page_metadata_tool.py`, HTTP fully mocked): the 402 → sign → retry flow (asserting the decoded payment payload: accepted amount/payTo, EIP-3009 authorization fields, signature shape, bazaar-extension echo), challenge parsing from the response body when the header is absent, cap refusal before signing (default cap, env override, tool-parameter override), fail-closed behaviour with no wallet configured, an upstream 503 after payment surfaced as an error, and a second 402 after payment treated as an error.
- `tool.specs.json` regenerated with the repo's own generator (one new entry, no unrelated churn).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean under the repo config; `mypy` (strict, repo config) clean on the new package.
- Verified end-to-end against the production endpoint with a real $0.005 payment from a test wallet: the tool returned the page's metadata and the payment settled on Base (payer −$0.005 USDC, service payTo +$0.005 USDC, read back on-chain).

## Notes for maintainers

- Docs: English page added under `docs/edge/en/tools/search-research/` and registered in `docs/docs.json` (edge nav only). Translations (ar, ko, pt-BR) not synced in this PR — happy to add them or leave them to the docs pipeline, as you prefer.
- Follow-ups I can add as separate PRs if this lands well: sibling tools for StallRow's url-unshorten ($0.005) and page-to-markdown ($0.01) routes, sharing the same payment helper.

> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`StallRowPageMetadataTool`**, CrewAI’s first **pay-per-call** tool: agents fetch a page’s title, description, OG/Twitter fields, heading outline, and word count via StallRow’s `/v1/page-metadata`, with **no API key**—each call costs **$0.005 USDC** settled over **x402 v2 on Base**.
> 
> A new **`x402_client`** implements the 402 → EIP-3009 sign → `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` retry flow, with a **hard price cap** enforced before signing, **fail-closed** behavior when `STALLROW_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY` is missing, and lazy **`eth-account`** via optional **`crewai-tools[stallrow]`**. title: feat(agents): read spreadsheet URLs in an agent's input with tools over every row
body:
An agent given the URL of a CSV, TSV or Excel file (how Studio passes uploads) had no way to compute over it: `URLReadTool` pulled the whole file into context, about 38K tokens for a 1,250-row workbook, and the counts came back wrong. With the new `crewai[spreadsheets]` extra installed, an agent now recognizes spreadsheet URLs in its own input, gets a short overview of each file, and gets `inspect_spreadsheet` / `query_spreadsheet` tools that compute over every row. On the same workbook it used about 2.7K prompt tokens per call and every count was correct.

- In: the agent's input on every entry point (`kickoff`/`kickoff_async`, `execute_task`/`aexecute_task`, crews, code and declarative flows), including presigned S3/Azure/GCS URLs whose name is only in `response-content-disposition`/`rscd`.
- Safety: only caller input is trusted. Crew/agent planning, crew-chat history and A2A text are kept apart, including across copies and checkpoints. Downloads go through `safe_get_bounded`, at most 10 files, under a 60s deadline that a watchdog enforces by shutting the socket down even mid-trickle. Errors never echo the signed URL.
- Public surface: `crewai_files.spreadsheets.url_filename`, `Task.checkpoint_input_description` (mirrors the other `checkpoint_*` fields), and a `deadline` keyword on `safe_get_bounded`. Nothing changes without the extra or a spreadsheet URL, and an agent's own same-named tool wins.
- Tests: 84 behavior tests cover every entry path, plus delegation, guardrail, planning, crew chat, checkpoint restore (including pre-1.15.38 checkpoints), copy, A2A, URL edge cases, the cap, deadline and cache. The devtools pin bump now handles extras.
- Docs: a "Spreadsheets" section in `concepts/agents.mdx` and a pointer in `files.mdx`, in en, ar, ko and pt-BR.
- Out: Studio's side is crewAIInc/crewai-plus#5230, crewAIInc/studio-runner#128 and crewAIInc/studio-assistant#378 (draft until the Studio version bump); also out: file-path and attachment inputs, any `URLReadTool` change, and bringing the download inside `max_execution_time`.

title: fix(tracing): upload a failed anonymous run that crewai eval started
body:
A logged-in failed run is recorded and graded, but an anonymous run's trace was discarded whenever the run raised. So `crewai eval` stopped with `untraced_after_run` for every failed anonymous run it had started. Now, when the eval handshake marks the run as awaited, a failed run's trace is shared (through the same consent path: the host callback, else the eval request itself) and recorded in `.crewai/last_run.json`, so the command grades it.

- Scope: `ephemeral_tracing` in `crewai/telemetry/tracing/ephemeral.py`. Only `Exception` failures of eval-awaited runs are shared; Ctrl-C, cancellation and discarded deferred lifetimes are not.
- A failed run's trace can never replace the run's own error: failures sharing it or shutting its session down are logged as a warning with the error class only.
- Unchanged: a failed run nobody is evaluating is still discarded without a question or request. `test_execution_failure_clears_buffer_without_consent_or_requests` stays, and a new end-to-end test pins it too.
- Composes with #9227 and #9221: with all three, a failed anonymous eval run is graded; a failed run that still leaves no trace counts as `run_failed` (#9227); classic crew/flow script failures reach that check through `ProjectScriptFailed` (#9221). The three touch different files, so no merge order needs a rebase; only #9221/#9227 overlap, in `eval_crew.py`.
- Tests: an eval-awaited failing flow is uploaded with an ERROR span and recorded (no terminal / under test / messages suppressed), the host consent callback is honored for it, interrupts are not uploaded, and a non-eval failure is discarded. The 4 eval-case tests fail on main.
- Out: no change to logged-in tracing, which already records failed runs; no CLI change. The TUI's own Evaluate after a failed in-app run is not covered and needs a Linear ticket.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches ephemeral trace upload and consent on failure paths used by `crewai eval`, but limits sharing to eval-awaited `Exception` failures and keeps interrupt/cancel behavior unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Anonymous runs that raised used to drop their ephemeral trace, so **`crewai eval`** could not grade failed anonymous runs (`untraced_after_run`). **`ephemeral_tracing`** now shares the buffered trace after **`Exception`** failures when **`run_awaited_by_evaluation()`** is true, using the same consent path as successful runs. Runs that fail outside eval, plus stops via Ctrl-C, cancellation, or **`GeneratorExit`**, still discard the trace without prompting.
> 
> Sharing and session shutdown on those eval failures go through **`_logged_instead`**, so exporter or flush errors are logged as warnings and never replace the run’s original error. Docs for **`trace_consent`** note that consent can run after eval-started failures. New tests cover eval-awaited upload (including **`ERROR`** spans and **`last_run`** recording), non-eval discard, interrupts, consent on failure, and best-effort trace teardown.

title: fix(llm): check openai-compatible providers' api key on the first call
body:
OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Cerebras, Dashscope and DeepInfra checked their API key while the model was validated, so `LLM("deepseek/...")` raised at construction and `Agent(llm="deepseek/...")` raised a pydantic `ValidationError` around `MissingAPIKeyError`. Like OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Azure, they now build without a key, and the first call raises `MissingAPIKeyError` with the same message. This partly reverses #8898, as decided.

- Scope: `OpenAICompatibleCompletion` resolves its key in `_get_client_params`, so `Agent`, `LiteAgent`, `Agent.model_validate`, `Agent(function_calling_llm=)` and `Crew(function_calling_llm=)` all construct keyless and raise on first use. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is never used for these providers (the OpenAI before-validator now fills it only for `provider == "openai"`).
- Behavior change: the deliberately pinned `test_agent_built_from_a_model_string`, and the construction-time tests in `test_openai_compatible.py`, `test_flow_telemetry.py` and `test_run_usage.py`, now pin the decided first-call behavior. The unwrap in `LLM.__new__` is removed because nothing raises the key error there any more. `from crewai.llm import MissingAPIKeyError` keeps working (released in 1.15.34-1.15.37), pinned by a test; `crewai.llms.base_llm` remains the documented path.
- CLI: `ENV_VARS` gains DEEPSEEK/OPENROUTER/DASHSCOPE/DEEPINFRA key names, so `crewai run` asks for them like OpenAI's key, and an agent project on these models now loads and reaches the key prompt. `crewai deploy` no longer pre-warns `llm_init_missing_key` for these providers on current crewai. Its `ValidationError` branch stays because the import runs on the project's own crewai, and 1.15.34–1.15.37 still produce that form (tests now build that form explicitly).
- Tests: missing/placeholder × env/explicit × sync/async × stream for all five providers, every model holder, the OpenAI-key isolation, the real agent-project prompt, and with a key set a sync/async/stream/tool-call/follow-up matrix over the real SDK (also green on main, so nothing else changed). 76 tests fail on main.
- Out: no docs change (`docs/edge` never said these providers fail at construction); Snowflake still checks its token at construction; the crewai-side copy of `ENV_VARS` (`crewai/constants.py`) is unchanged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes when and how API keys are validated across LLM construction, agents, CLI, and telemetry—behavior shift users may notice, but aligned with other native providers and heavily tested.
> 
> **Overview**
> **OpenAI-compatible providers** (DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Dashscope, DeepInfra, Cerebras, etc.) no longer fail at construction when an API key is missing. Key resolution matches native providers: models build with `api_key=None`, and **`MissingAPIKeyError` is raised on the first** `call`/`acall` via `_get_client_params`. `Agent`, `LiteAgent`, and crews using these models can load without a key and only fail when the LLM is actually invoked.
>

title: fix(devtools): read and write repository files as UTF-8
body:
Fixes #9230

## What

`crewai-devtools` reads and writes textbooks-of-record — `pyproject.toml`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `AGENTS.md`, docs pages — with text-mode `open()` / `read_text()` / `write_text()` and no `encoding`, so the platform default applies. On Windows that is the ANSI code page, and the tool cannot touch a file containing a typographic character:

```
tests\test_toml_updates.py:437: in test_default_packages_cover_all_workspace_members
    root_pyproject = (workspace_root / "pyproject.toml").read_text()
E   UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x94 in position 19647: illegal multibyte sequence
```

That is the repository's own `pyproject.toml` — the em dashes and curly quotes in it are UTF-8.

## Change

`encoding="utf-8"` on the 57 text-mode call sites:

| file | sites |
|---|---|
| `lib/devtools/src/crewai_devtools/cli.py` | 18 (`bump-version`, `tag`, `release`, changelog and workflow rewriting) |
| `lib/devtools/src/crewai_devtools/docs_check.py` | 5 (docs page reading and sidecar writing) |
| `lib/devtools/tests/test_toml_updates.py` | 30 |
| `lib/devtools/tests/test_docs_versioning.py` | 21 |
| `lib/devtools/tests/test_agents_md_eval.py` | 6 |

Purely mechanical: one keyword per call, applied with an AST pass so nested and multi-line calls got it in the right place, and calls that already passed an encoding were skipped. Binary opens (`"rb"` / `"wb"`) are untouched — they carry no encoding.

## Verification

Windows 11 / CPython 3.13, `lib/devtools` installed editable:

```
$ cd lib/devtools && pytest tests -q
# before

# after
105 passed

Found 18 errors        # same count at HEAD, verified with git stash
$ ruff check --no-fix lib/devtools/tests/test_toml_updates.py
All checks passed!
```

No behaviour change on POSIX, where UTF-8 is already the default; file contents are byte-identical there.

`@agent`, `@task`, `@crew` and the other CrewBase decorators memoized results in a module-level cache keyed by method name and `id(self)`. title: feat(files): read spreadsheets for agents in crewai-files
body:
Spreadsheets reach crewAI today as raw CSV text or, for Excel, as base64, so agents can't count, total or filter them. This adds the reading engine for native spreadsheet support: `crewai_files.spreadsheets` reads .xlsx, CSV and TSV into typed tables, writes a short overview of a file, and answers five fixed operations over every row with pandas. Nothing calls it yet; the crew wiring follows in the next PR. Plan: `crewai-spreadsheets-plan.md` (shared separately).

- Scope: `crewai_files.spreadsheets` (`is_spreadsheet`, `load_spreadsheet`, `reading`, `answers`), internal, not in `crewai_files.__all__`; a new `crewai-files[spreadsheets]` extra (pandas, python-calamine, charset-normalizer, pinned per Python version because pandas 3 and python-calamine 0.9 need 3.11); `pandas-stubs` added to dev only
- Ported from Studio Assistant (#370, #374), changed for a library: a scan of each sheet's XML replaces Studio's child-process guard (`RLIMIT_AS` isn't enforced on macOS and `resource` doesn't exist on Windows); OLE (password-protected .xlsx, legacy .xls) and .ods are refused before calamine opens them, keeping calamine's CFB parser (RUSTSEC-2026-0436) unreachable; total rows are left out of aggregates; filters use the sheet's number format; dates past 2262 stay dates on pandas 2; URLs stream with a byte cap
- Tests: 164, including hostile files (zip bombs, a value at XFD1048576, cells without positions, DTDs, encrypted members), the pre-scan matching calamine's own extent, exact answers over 200k rows, and every way a spreadsheet arrives (TextFile, File, AudioFile-typed CSV, bytes, URL). Production is 1,729 lines and tests 1,560: most of the code is ported from Studio, which these tests cover
- Measured (macOS, pandas 2.2.3): 9 MB / 200k-row CSV, parse 0.3 s and overview 2 s; 46 MB / 1M rows, 1.9 s and 10.5 s, about 930 MB peak; a 12 MB / 500k-row xlsx parses in 7 s
- Out: agent tools, prompt overview and routing (next PR), docs (they land with the user-visible change), .xls/.xlsb/.ods reading, writing files, pandas 3 in CI (the lock resolves pandas 2.2.3 because `crewai[pandas]` pins `~=2.2.3`)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01WfUv1NsUFz1RHjRgS73HBR

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Parses untrusted spreadsheet bytes with memory and DoS implications; security relies on pre-scan limits and format refusal staying correct before agent integration.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`crewai_files.spreadsheets`**, an internal engine for agent spreadsheet work (not wired to crew tools in this PR). **`crewai-files[spreadsheets]`** optional extra adds pandas, python-calamine, and charset-normalizer with Python-version pins.
> 
> **Loading** exposes `is_spreadsheet` (no extra deps) and `load_spreadsheet` with bounded LRU cache, byte-capped URL streaming, and shared parse limits.

> **Reading** parses .xlsx (calamine), CSV, and TSV into typed tables: header detection, EU/US number formats, far-cell and zip-bomb guards via XML pre-scan, refused OLE/.ods/legacy .xls, and capped concurrent parses.

body:

title: feat(platform-tools): name the apps CrewAI AMP cannot resolve for an agent
body:
When an agent's apps don't load, CrewAI AMP already says which ones: its actions endpoint answers 422 with `{"missing": [...]}`, and Clipper answers 409 `conflict` (no active connection) or 404 `clipper_not_found` (unknown app). Only those codes count, so another server's 404 or 409 keeps its own error. The platform clients raised the bare `HTTPError`, so the agent's warning could only say "none resolved". Now the clients raise `PlatformAppsUnavailableError` naming every app AMP could not resolve, and the agent warns with `UnresolvedPlatformAppsWarning`, which carries `agent_role`, `apps` and `missing_apps` and names them in its text.

- Scope: `LegacyClient` and `ClipperClient.get_actions`, `CrewaiPlatformTools` (names every missing app across selectors, each once), and `Agent.get_platform_tools`. New types live in `crewai_core.platform_apps`
- Compatibility: `UnresolvedPlatformAppsWarning` is a `UserWarning` whose text opens exactly as before, so `filterwarnings("error", message=r"Agent '.*' declares apps")` (CrewAI AMP's runtime) still matches. `CrewaiPlatformTools` now raises `PlatformAppsUnavailableError`, not `requests.HTTPError`, for those three answers only; a JSON crew's `platform:` ref reports the named apps in its `JSONProjectError`
- Tests: client answers (422 with and without a list, Clipper's 409/404 codes, a proxy's 404/409, 401/403/500), the factory naming every app once, the agent's warning fields, and both compatibility pins. Every new behavior test fails on main
- Next: crewAI-enterprise drops its own re-query of AMP once it pins a crewai with this
- Out: no warning when only some of an agent's apps load (AMP's 422 makes the actions endpoint all-or-nothing); AMP's actions endpoint does not separate "not connected" from "unknown", so neither does this; no docs change

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how platform tool resolution fails (new exception type vs raw HTTPError) and alters warning text/structure; behavior is scoped to AMP/Clipper discovery with tests guarding Clipper code discrimination.
> 
> **Overview**
> When platform app discovery fails, callers now get **specific app names** instead of generic HTTP errors or a vague “none resolved” warning.
> 
> **New types in `crewai_core.platform_apps`:** `PlatformAppsUnavailableError` carries `missing_apps`; `UnresolvedPlatformAppsWarning` (still a `UserWarning` with the same opening text) adds structured fields and AMP-specific guidance when AMP named the apps.
> 
> **Integration clients** map AMP/Clipper signals to that error: legacy actions API **422** with a `missing` list; Clipper **409 `conflict`** / **404 `clipper_not_found`** only when the response body matches (proxy/wrong-URL 404/409 stay `HTTPError`).

title: fix(cli): let an empty value keep its precedence in the run's key check
body:
`crewai run`'s key check read an empty value as unset and fell back to the other source. Example: CI exports `OPENAI_API_KEY=""` because a secret is missing, and the project `.env` has a real key. A Python crew's `load_dotenv` keeps the empty value, but the check counted the key as set, printed no line, and the run then failed with the provider's own error. The check now gives an empty value the same precedence the run does.

- Scope: `_is_set` and `_configured_model` in `lib/cli/src/crewai_cli/api_keys.py`. A Python crew keeps an empty shell key or `MODEL`, and a JSON crew applies a blank `.env` `MODEL` (crewAI then falls back to its default model)
- Tests: three regressions (empty shell key, empty shell `MODEL`, blank JSON `.env` `MODEL`), each failing on main. Existing precedence tests unchanged and passing
- Raised by Cursor on #9034 (code from #9032)
- Out: no change to what `load_project_env` or a crew loads; no docs change

title: fix(i18n): replace generic Exception with specific exception types
body:
## Problem

`crewai/utilities/i18n.py` used the generic `Exception` class for three different error conditions, making it difficult for callers to distinguish between error types:

1. **Line 47**: `raise Exception(f"Prompt file '{self.prompt_file}' not found.")` — Should be `FileNotFoundError`
2. **Line 49**: `raise Exception("Error decoding JSON from the prompts file.")` — Should be `ValueError` with error detail
3. **Line 128**: `raise Exception(f"Prompt for '{kind}':'{key}'  not found.")` — Should be `KeyError`

Additionally, line 127 catches `Exception` broadly when only `KeyError` is expected from dict access, and the JSON decode error message didn't include the underlying error detail.

## Fix

1. `FileNotFoundError` instead of `Exception` for missing prompt files
2. `ValueError` with `str(e)` detail instead of `Exception` for JSON decode errors
3. `KeyError` instead of `Exception` for missing prompt keys, with narrower `except KeyError` instead of `except Exception`
4. Fixed double-space typo in error message (`'{key}'  not found` -> `'{key}' not found`)

## Impact

Callers can now catch specific exception types:
- `try: ... except FileNotFoundError:` for missing files
- `try: ... except ValueError:` for invalid JSON
- `try: ... except KeyError:` for missing prompts

No behavior change for successful code paths.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized error-handling change with no success-path behavior change; callers that relied on catching generic `Exception` from i18n would need to catch the new types instead.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`crewai/utilities/i18n.py`** now raises standard, typed errors instead of bare `Exception`, so callers can handle missing files, bad JSON, and missing prompt keys separately.
> 
> On load, a missing prompt file re-raises **`FileNotFoundError`** (with the configured path), and invalid JSON becomes **`ValueError`** including the underlying decode error. **`retrieve`** (and helpers like **`slice`**) now catch **`KeyError`** only and re-raise **`KeyError`** with a clearer message; the docstring and a double-space typo in that message were updated accordingly.
> 
> Successful prompt loading and lookup behavior is unchanged; only failure types and messages differ.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit fe70431495b499e0c0096990b920f22ef454578d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(utilities): recover JSON log when the existing file is not a record list
body:
# fix(utilities): recover JSON log when the existing file is not a record list

Fixes #9082

## Summary

`FileHandler.log()` with a `.json` output path appends to the previous contents by `json.load`ing the file and calling `existing_data.append(log_entry)`. Only `json.JSONDecodeError` and `FileNotFoundError` are caught — so when the file contains **valid JSON that is not a list** (a JSON object like `{"already": "an object"}`, or a bare string such as `"a bare string"`), `json.load` succeeds and `.append` raises `AttributeError`. The outer handler converts that into `ValueError("Failed to log message")`, and because nothing ever repairs the file, **every subsequent `log()` call fails** for the rest of the process.

This is easy to hit in practice: `output_log_file` pointed at a path that already holds a JSON object written by another tool, a hand-edited file, or a file from an older crewai version with a different shape.

The fix validates what was loaded: a non-list payload starts a fresh record list instead of raising, so the log recovers (the foreign content is replaced by valid records, matching how a `JSONDecodeError` path already behaves) and later `log()` calls keep working. Files holding a valid JSON *list* — including lists of non-record entries — are appended to unchanged.

## Validation

New parametrized test `test_json_log_recovers_when_existing_file_is_not_a_record_list` in `lib/crewai/tests/utilities/test_file_handler.py` (existing content `{"already": "an object"}` and `"a bare string"`): seeds the file, calls `log()` twice, and asserts both records land in a valid JSON list.

- Red → green on Windows 11, Python 3.13.9, same command `python -m pytest lib/crewai/tests/utilities/test_file_handler.py -q`:
  - before the fix: **2 failed** (`AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'append'` → `ValueError: Failed to log message`);
  - after the fix: **11 passed** (all pre-existing tests included, no behavior change for lists or serialization-failure paths).
- `git diff --check` clean.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (bug localization, patch, and test authoring by an AI coding agent), reviewed and validated locally by the submitting contributor before opening this PR. Per `CONTRIBUTING.md`, please apply the **`llm-generated`** label to this PR.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized change to JSON append logic in file logging; behavior for valid list files is unchanged, with the tradeoff that foreign non-list JSON at the path is replaced on first log.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`FileHandler.log()`** for `.json` paths no longer breaks permanently when the file already contains valid JSON that is not a list (e.g. a JSON object or a bare string). Previously `json.load` succeeded and `.append` raised **`AttributeError`**, which surfaced as **`ValueError: Failed to log message`** on every later write.
> 
> After load, non-list payloads are treated like a corrupt/missing file: the handler starts a **fresh record list**, appends the new entry, and overwrites the file—so logging recovers instead of failing for the rest of the process. Valid JSON **lists** (including existing log arrays) still append as before.
> 
> A parametrized test covers object and string seed content and asserts two consecutive **`log()`** calls produce a normal record list.

title: fix(storage): serialize and decode task output JSON fields consistently
body:
Fixes #7746

## Problem

`KickoffTaskOutputsSQLiteStorage` was inconsistent between `add()` and `update()` / `load()`:

- `update()` JSON-encoded a value only when it was a `dict`. Passing a `list` raised `sqlite3.ProgrammingError: Error binding parameter: type 'list' is not supported`.
- `load()` called `json.loads()` unconditionally on `output` and `inputs`. If either column was NULL (for example after `update(..., output=None)`), it raised `TypeError`, which was not caught by the surrounding `except sqlite3.Error` and permanently broke `load()` for the whole table.

## Change

- `update()` now serialises the two JSON-backed columns (`output`, `inputs`) with `CrewJSONEncoder`, matching `add()`. `None` is stored as NULL. Other columns keep their raw values.
- `load()` decodes through `_decode_json_field`, which returns `None` for NULL/empty values and falls back to the raw value for legacy rows written unencoded by older `update()` calls.

- `test_update_serialises_non_dict_output`: a list output round-trips.
- `test_load_handles_null_json_fields`: NULL output and inputs load without raising.

title: fix(memory): probe worker liveness without os.kill on Windows
body:
Fixes #7684

## Problem

`QdrantEdgeStorage._cleanup_orphaned_shards` used `os.kill(pid, 0)` as a liveness probe and only caught `ProcessLookupError` / `PermissionError`. That probe is POSIX-only:

- On Windows, any signal other than CTRL_C_EVENT or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT is passed to `TerminateProcess`, so the probe would terminate a *live* worker process.
- For a dead pid, Windows raises a bare `OSError` (WinError 87), which escaped and crashed `QdrantEdgeStorage.__init__` for any Windows user with a leftover worker shard.

## Change

Introduce `_process_is_alive(pid)`:

- POSIX keeps the existing `os.kill(pid, 0)` semantics.
- Windows uses `OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)` plus `GetExitCodeProcess` and checks for `STILL_ACTIVE`. If the handle cannot be queried, it conservatively returns `True` so a live worker's shard is never deleted.

The cleanup loop now calls this helper instead of doing an inline `os.kill`.

## Tests

- `test_process_is_alive_does_not_signal_the_process`: the current process reports alive, a non-existent pid reports dead. On Windows this exercises the new branch.
- The existing `test_orphaned_shard_cleanup` now works on Windows instead of raising an unhandled `OSError`.

Verified locally on Windows: before the change `os.kill(99999999, 0)` raised `OSError [WinError 87]`; the new helper returns `False` for that pid and `True` for the current process.

## AI-generated contribution

This PR was authored with the help of an AI coding assistant. Per `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md` the `llm-generated` label is required for AI-authored contributions.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes multi-process shard cleanup and data recovery on Windows; incorrect liveness logic could delete live worker memory or leave orphans, though the implementation errs on keeping shards when uncertain.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#7684** by replacing the orphaned worker shard cleanup’s **`os.kill(pid, 0)`** probe with a cross-platform **`_process_is_alive`** helper.
> 
> On **POSIX**, behavior is unchanged (`kill` with signal 0, treating `ProcessLookupError` as dead and `PermissionError` as alive). On **Windows**, liveness uses **`OpenProcess`** / **`GetExitCodeProcess`** instead of signaling, because `os.kill` can **terminate** live workers and dead PIDs raise an unhandled **`OSError`**, which broke **`QdrantEdgeStorage.__init__`** when stale `worker-*` dirs existed.
> 
> When **`OpenProcess`** fails, only Win32 error **87** (`ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`) is treated as “pid gone”; **access denied** and other errors conservatively count as **alive** so cleanup does not drop a running worker’s shard. **`_cleanup_orphaned_shards`** now skips live workers via this helper and only then logs and recovers orphaned data.
> 
> Tests cover **`_process_is_alive`**, **`_win_pid_is_gone`**, and a mocked Windows **`OpenProcess`** failure path.
>

title: fix(utilities): stop re-interpolating inserted template values
body:
# fix(utilities): stop re-interpolating inserted template values

## Summary

- `interpolate_only` replaced each placeholder using `str.replace`, which
  rescans the already-substituted text. A value containing another template
  variable's placeholder was therefore interpolated a second time.
- This is template re-injection: user- or model-supplied data that happens
  to contain `{...}` patterns is treated as template code and substituted
  again with other inputs' values.

## Reproduction

On `main` (`dd21ecc`):

```python
from crewai.utilities.string_utils import interpolate_only

interpolate_only('{a} {b}', {'a': '{b}', 'b': 'injected'})
# → 'injected injected'   ← the value of a was re-interpolated
#   expected: '{b} injected'
```

Processing order: `{a}` is replaced with `{b}`, then the `{b}` that came
from `a`'s value is replaced with `injected` when `b` is processed.

## Fix

`lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/string_utils.py` — use a single
`re.sub` pass with a replacement function instead of looping with
`str.replace`. `re.sub` does not rescan its own replacement text, so
inserted values stay literal. The missing-variable check and input-type
validation are unchanged.

## Validation

Three regression tests in `lib/crewai/tests/utilities/test_string_utils.py`:

| case | on `main` | after |
|---|---|---|
| `interpolate_only('{a} {b}', {'a': '{b}', 'b': 'injected'})` | `injected injected` | `{b} injected` |
| `interpolate_only('{x}', {'x': '{x}'})` (self-reference) | `{x}` | `{x}` (control) |
| `interpolate_only('Hello {name}', {'name': 'World'})` (basic) | `Hello World` | `Hello World` (control) |

The re-interpolation case fails on unmodified `main` and passes after; both
controls pass on both sides.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Behavior change in a shared utility used for agent and task prompt interpolation; fixes incorrect double substitution but could differ from code that accidentally relied on the old behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`interpolate_only`** no longer treats `{...}` inside substituted input values as new template placeholders. The implementation switches from a loop of **`str.replace`** calls to a single **`re.sub`** pass with a replacement callback, because **`re.sub`** does not rescan replacement text.
>
