title: fix(tools): drop None metadata values before writing to ChromaDB
body:
Fixes #9053

## Summary

`sanitize_metadata_for_chromadb()` kept `None` values:

```python
if isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)) or value is None:
    sanitized[key] = value
```

ChromaDB metadata only accepts `str`, `int`, `float` and `bool`, so a `None` value made the write fail (`TypeError: argument 'metadatas': Cannot convert Python object to MetadataValue`). Loader metadata can legitimately contain `None`: the YouTube loader stores `description=None` when a video has no description (and `length_seconds` can be `None` too), and the CrewAI RAG adapter sends loader metadata through this sanitizer before adding documents. Adding such a video aborted ingestion instead of storing the transcript.

`None` values are now skipped, so the remaining metadata is written:

```python
for key, value in metadata.items():
    if value is None:
        continue
    if isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)):
        sanitized[key] = value
```

## Changes

- `lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/rag/misc.py`: drop `None` values in `sanitize_metadata_for_chromadb()` and document it.
- `lib/crewai-tools/tests/rag/test_misc.py` (new):
  - `test_sanitize_metadata_drops_none_values`;
  - `test_sanitized_metadata_is_accepted_by_chromadb`, which writes the sanitized metadata through a real ephemeral ChromaDB client.

title: fix(tools): handle the Linkup sourcedAnswer output shape
body:
Fixes #9052

## Summary

`LinkupSearchTool._run()` advertises `output_type="sourcedAnswer"` but always read `response.results`. For that output type the SDK returns a `LinkupSourcedAnswer` with `answer` and `sources`, so the attribute access raised and the tool answered every sourced-answer search with:

```

    return {
        "success": True,
        "answer": response.answer,
        "sources": [
            {"name": source.name, "url": source.url, "snippet": source.snippet}

```

title: fix(openai): call GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol tools through the Responses API
body:

title: fix(llm): keep additional_params when retrying a model that rejects stop
body:
## Problem

When a LiteLLM-routed model rejects the `stop` parameter, `LLM.call()` (and `LLM.acall()`) retries the request after forcing `"stop"` into `additional_drop_params`. The recovery path rebuilt `additional_params` from scratch:

```python
if "additional_drop_params" not in self.additional_params:
    self.additional_params = {"additional_drop_params": ["stop"]}
else:
    self.additional_params["additional_drop_params"].append("stop")
```

`additional_params` is a public config field (`BaseLLM.additional_params`) that `_prepare_completion_params()` merges into every request. If the caller set anything else there - `num_retries`, `extra_headers`, `drop_params`, `api_base`, provider extras - the first rejected-`stop` retry deletes it, and every later call on that LLM instance runs with different configuration than the caller asked for. The `else` branch also appended `"stop"` to the caller's own list in place, and appended it again on each further retry.

Reproduction (two mocked provider calls, first rejects `stop`):

```
caller additional_params before: {'num_retries': 5, 'extra_headers': {'X-Tenant': 'acme'}, 'drop_params': True}
caller additional_params after : {'additional_drop_params': ['stop']}
-> settings silently lost: ['drop_params', 'extra_headers', 'num_retries']
```

Trigger is ordinary: the agent executor sends a `stop` vocabulary, and some providers answer `Unsupported parameter: 'stop' is not supported with this model.`

## Fix

Add a small helper that returns a *copy* of `additional_params` with `"stop"` in `additional_drop_params` (no duplicates), and use it in both the sync and the async retry path, so the caller's settings are preserved and their list is never mutated.

## Tests

`lib/crewai/tests/llms/test_litellm_stop_param_retry.py` (3 tests, skipped when the `crewai[litellm]` extra is absent) stubs only the two provider boundaries and asserts that:

* a caller-supplied `additional_params` survives the rejected-`stop` retry;
* the retry still sends `additional_drop_params=["stop"]`;
* repeated retries do not duplicate `"stop"`.

```
pytest tests/llms/test_litellm_stop_param_retry.py   # 3 passed
pytest tests/test_llm.py                             # 3 failed, 102 passed, 3 skipped (unchanged; the 3 failures are pre-existing env failures)
ruff check + ruff format --check                     # clean
```

The new tests fail on the unpatched tree (`3 failed`).

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes shared LLM retry configuration on long-lived instances; incorrect handling could still drop provider settings or break stop-word retries, but scope is narrow and covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a bug where LiteLLM **`call()` / `acall()`** retries (after a provider rejects the **`stop`** parameter) could **wipe or mutate** the caller’s **`additional_params`**—settings like **`num_retries`**, **`extra_headers`**, or **`api_base`** that are merged into every completion.
> 
> The retry path now uses a shared **`_force_drop_stop_param()`** helper that **copies** **`additional_params`**, appends **`"stop"`** to **`additional_drop_params`** (without duplicates), and **does not replace** the whole dict or mutate the caller’s drop list in place. Sync and async paths both delegate to this helper.
> 
> Adds **`test_litellm_stop_param_retry.py`** with sync/async coverage and a case where an existing **`additional_drop_params`** list is extended without aliasing the caller’s list.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 81c94f2908574ab0eba1fc1245b3d613205f67f3. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: feat(agent): add experimental conversational Agent sessions
body:
Standalone Agents can retain a conversation with experimental `Agent(conversational=True)`, `agent.handle_turn()`, `agent.chat()` and `agent.chat(tui=True)`. Both chat modes reuse the Flow conversation runtime and stream replies automatically; callers do not need to construct a Flow.

**Merge order: #9017 first, then #8687.** After this SDK PR lands, retarget the scaffold PR to main.

- Bind each conversational Agent to one session. A different session ID raises `ValueError` before a model call or chat prompt. Reject overlapping direct/streamed turns with `RuntimeError` before pending state changes. Initialize the cached Flow atomically, release guards after failures, and retain the guard until a cancelled stream's worker finishes.
- Start Python shallow/deep copies, Pydantic shallow/deep copies and `Agent.copy()` with fresh conversation state. Tests copy Agents while their original turn is active and verify independent concurrent conversations and clone-specific LLM/tool configuration.
- Default conversational Agents to quiet output and streamed public replies. Honor explicit verbosity/streaming settings; preserve custom REPL output callbacks. Ordinary Agents remain opt-in and independent `kickoff()` / `kickoff_async()` behavior is unchanged.
- Keep the configured Agent/tools on the built-in `converse` route. AgentExecutor does not inherit a conversational Flow. The handler supports `str | LiteAgentOutput | Awaitable[str | LiteAgentOutput]`.
- Count SDK turn/chat invocations and completed/failed Agent turns through existing feature telemetry, including the managed Flow bridge. Signals add no messages, responses, session IDs, Agent roles, model names or error text and honor telemetry opt-outs.
- Document Agent conversations in English, Arabic, Korean and Brazilian Portuguese.

The CrewAI-AMP session finding is fixed in `47ecead48` (session/copy/concurrency isolation). The cross-session regression failed before the fix and now passes. The inline session finding is resolved.

Validation: 82 SDK/Flow/tracing tests (`test_conversation.py`, `test_flow_chat_tui.py`, `test_tracer_isolation.py`) and 568 CLI/TUI tests (`test_kickoff_flow.py`, `test_crew_run_tui.py`, `test_trace_consent_session.py`, `test_eval_crew.py`) pass; Ruff, ruff-format and mypy pre-commit checks pass. These are offline checks; no live-model E2E run was performed. Manual runners are not committed.

Experimental/unreleased: history is in memory by default. Recovery needs explicit Flow persistence, and applications must authorize access to persisted sessions. One Agent owns one conversation; use separate Agents for independent concurrent conversations. Matching package releases, managed API token streaming, production CDO/container deployment and multi-host recovery require separate verification.

Scaffold/CLI: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8687
Enterprise integration: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI-enterprise/pull/1398
Linear: https://linear.app/crewai/issue/OSS-236/expose-durable-conversational-endpoints-for-standalone-agents


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> New experimental conversation API with session and concurrency rules plus changed default streaming behavior for Flow/Agent REPL chat; telemetry is additive and opt-out aware.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **experimental standalone Agent conversations** via `conversational=True`, `handle_turn()`, `chat()`, `agent.chat(tui=True)`, and `as_flow()`—backed by a managed Flow bridge with one-session binding, turn locking, and fresh state on Agent copies.
> 
> **Conversational Flow `chat()`** now drives turns through **`stream_turn()`** instead of `handle_turn()`, with optional **`chat(tui=True)`** (shared `crewai run` UI), default token streaming, and a `stream` override that does not mutate shared LLM settings. The CLI TUI forwards `session_id`, exit commands, trace deferral, and streaming into that path; failed chats surface as **`ClickException`** without a traceback.
> 
> **Telemetry** adds `standalone_agent:*` Feature Usage spans (no message/session/error payload); **docs** cover Agents, conversational flows, and telemetry in **en/ar/ko/pt-BR**. Quiet non-verbose Agents suppress version banners when console output is suppressed.

- **#8974** — a method that returned a Pydantic model or dataclass came back from the checkpoint's JSON as a plain `dict`, and the resume's start-method skip passed that dict to its listeners (`quote.amount` / `result.feedback` raised `AttributeError`).
- **#8980** — listeners of a method that completed before the failure were called with `None` instead of the recorded output, so the recovery computed on a missing value (silently when the listener ignores its argument).

The fix keeps each method output's type beside its JSON value:

- `_sync_checkpoint_fields` (checkpoint writes) annotates each method-output entry with `output_type` / `human_feedback_type` import paths.
- `_restore_from_checkpoint` rebuilds structured outputs (`model_validate` for Pydantic models, `TypeAdapter` for dataclasses), degrading to the plain JSON value with a warning when the recorded type is no longer importable.
- Both resume skip paths (start methods and completed listeners) now continue with the output recorded for *that* method (`Flow._recorded_listener_input`), preferring a recorded collapsed outcome for emit-driven human-feedback methods — matching what listeners received in the first run. The start path keeps its previous `method_outputs[-1]` fallback for legacy checkpoints without per-method entries.

Old checkpoints (no type paths) restore exactly as before, and new checkpoints remain readable by older versions (extra entry keys are ignored).

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

Regression tests in `test_checkpoint.py`, mirroring the repro scripts from the issues:

- `TestRestoredFlowListenerInputs` — a resumed a→b→c chain feeds `c` the recorded `"B"` instead of `None` (#8980); a resumed flow receives the same `Quote` instance as the first run and completes with `charged = 42` (#8974); a resumed `@human_feedback` flow hands its listener the `HumanFeedbackResult` with `.feedback` intact (#8974).
- `TestRestoredMethodOutputTypes` — serde round-trips (Pydantic model, `HumanFeedbackResult` dataclass), legacy entries without type paths pass through untouched, and unresolvable type paths degrade to the JSON value with a warning.

`uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/test_checkpoint.py` (88 passed), plus `test_flow.py`, `test_flow_definition.py`, `test_flow_from_definition.py`, `test_flow_persistence.py`, `test_flow_ask.py`, `test_async_human_feedback.py`, `test_event_record.py`; `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy` clean. Both repro scripts from the issues now produce the first-run behavior (`resumed: charged = 42`, `c received 'B'`).

This work is AI-assisted (Claude Code), so the PR should carry the `llm-generated` label.

Listeners of a completed **router** still don't replay its outcome-triggered chains — that is the separate router-replay territory of #8437 / PR #8446. This change only fixes the plain-listener input so it matches the first run.

title: fix(events): track sync handler futures when async handlers exist
body:
## Related issue

#8949

## Summary

`CrewAIEventsBus.emit()` registered the sync-handler future with `_track_future()` only when the event had **no** async handlers. When an event had both kinds of handlers, the sync future was submitted to the executor but never tracked, so `flush()` — and therefore `shutdown(wait=True)` — could return `True` while a sync handler was still running, and sync-handler exceptions went unreported by flush.

`replay()` already tracks the sync future unconditionally on the same code path; this moves `emit()` to the same shape: track first, then keep the sync-only early return (return value unchanged — `_track_future()` returns the same future object).

## Verification

- New regression test (`lib/crewai/tests/events/test_flush_sync_tracking.py`): a sleeping sync handler plus an immediate async handler for one event; asserts `flush(timeout=10)` does not return `True` before the sync handler finishes.
  - Fails on `main` (assertion: "flush() returned True before the sync handler finished"), passes with the fix.
- Full `lib/crewai/tests/events/` suite: 194 passed.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy` clean on the touched files.

> **Note for reviewers:** local runs on Windows need the event-bus loop's loopback `socketpair`, which the workspace default `--block-network` flag blocks (Linux/CI is unaffected — `socketpair(2)` is native there). The regression test was validated locally with `pytest -o addopts=""` and behaves like the other async-handler tests under the default configuration.

title: fix(events): track sync-handler future in emit() when async handlers are also registered
body:
Fixes #8950

## Summary

`CrewAIEventsBus.emit()` submits sync handlers to the thread-pool executor but only registers the resulting future via `_track_future()` when there are **no** async handlers. When an event has both sync and async handlers, the sync-handler future is neither returned nor tracked, so:

- `flush()` can return `True` while a sync handler is still running (and `shutdown(wait=True)` calls `flush()` first, so the executor can be shut down with a sync handler still in flight);
- by the time the caller observes completion, sync-handler errors may not have been reported yet.

`replay()` already handles the same mixed-handler path correctly by tracking the sync future unconditionally; this PR makes `emit()` match it.

## Changes

- `lib/crewai/src/crewai/events/event_bus.py`: in `emit()`, track the sync-handler future before the `if not async_handlers:` check, exactly like `replay()` does. The sync-only return value is unchanged (the same tracked future object is returned), and the mixed-handler path still returns the async future as documented.

## Testing

- Added `lib/crewai/tests/utilities/events/test_emit_mixed_handlers_flush.py` with two regression tests:
  - `test_flush_waits_for_pending_sync_handler`: with a slow sync handler + fast async handler, `flush()` must not return `True` until the sync handler finished. This fails deterministically without the fix.
  - `test_flush_returns_after_sync_handler_error_is_reported`: after `flush()` returns `True`, the failing sync handler's error must already have been reported.
- All existing tests in `lib/crewai/tests/utilities/events/test_crewai_event_bus.py` still pass.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes event dispatch lifecycle and shutdown ordering; the fix is narrow and mirrors existing replay() behavior, but incorrect flush timing could still affect teardown in edge cases.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`emit()` now registers sync thread-pool futures with `_track_future()` even when async handlers are on the same event**, aligning with **`replay()`** instead of only tracking the sync future when no async handlers exist.
> 
> Previously, mixed sync+async emits returned only the async future, so **`flush()`** (and **`shutdown(wait=True)`**, which calls flush first) could finish while sync handlers were still running or before sync handler errors were printed. Sync-only behavior is unchanged: the same tracked future is still returned.
> 
> Adds regression tests that assert **`flush()`** waits for a slow sync handler alongside a fast async handler, and that a failing sync handler’s error is reported before **`flush()`** returns **`True`**.

title: feat(rag): remove chromadb from the embedding function layer
body:
## Summary

Part 1 of making ChromaDB an optional dependency: remove chromadb from the **embedding function** layer. Storage (the vector database side) is Part 2 and is not touched here.

- **Type-only leaks fixed.** `custom`, `voyageai`, `ibm` and `google` vertex imported `chromadb.api.types` only for types. They now use `crewai.rag.core.base_embeddings_callable.EmbeddingFunction` and `crewai.rag.core.types`.
- **Native OpenAI embedder.** New `OpenAIEmbeddingFunction` calls the `openai` SDK directly (`OpenAI`, or `AzureOpenAI` for `api_type="azure"`). Provider config fields, aliases and defaults are unchanged.
- **Azure and OpenRouter** use the same native class.
- **Memory** default embedder (`_default_embedder()`) now goes through the native OpenAI function.
- **Unported providers load chromadb lazily.** bedrock, cohere, google (`google` / `google-generativeai`), huggingface, instructor, jina, ollama, onnx, openclip, roboflow, sentence-transformer and text2vec import chromadb only when the provider is constructed, through `load_chromadb_embedding_function`. Without chromadb this raises `ImportError ... pip install crewai[chromadb]`. Passing your own `embedding_callable` never needs chromadb.

## Behavior notes

- Parity with chromadb's `OpenAIEmbeddingFunction`: one `embeddings.create` call (no client-side batching), `dimensions` sent only for `text-embedding-3*` models, float32 vectors, same Azure client and required-setting errors.
- Differences: empty input raises `ValueError` (chromadb returned `[]`; CrewAI's `EmbeddingFunction` wrapper cannot return an empty list). There is no `CHROMA_OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback, and no chromadb `api_key` deprecation warning. Keys still come from `api_key`, `EMBEDDINGS_OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- The `chromadb` extra does not exist yet (chromadb is still a core dependency), so the install message points ahead to Part 2.

- **Chroma stores the native function as "legacy".** The native `OpenAIEmbeddingFunction` has none of chromadb's self-describing methods (`get_config`, `build_from_config`, `is_legacy`). When it is used with a Chroma collection (Knowledge or a RAG tool on Chroma with an `openai` / `azure` / `openrouter` embedder), chromadb emits `DeprecationWarning: legacy embedding function config` and saves `{'type': 'legacy'}` for new collections instead of the full config. CrewAI passes the function every time it opens a collection, so this keeps working inside CrewAI. Opening such a collection with plain chromadb and no embedding function falls back to chromadb's default embedder (it failed with an `onnxruntime` error in my test). Collections created earlier with chromadb's own function still reopen fine with the native one. Chroma's check against changing the model of an existing collection is probably skipped for legacy functions; I did not test that. No adapter is added here, since Part 2 changes how Chroma is used.

## Which provider uses which class

**No chromadb needed**

| Provider name | Embedding function class | Backed by |
|---|---|---|
| `openai` | native `OpenAIEmbeddingFunction` | `openai` SDK (`OpenAI`) |
| `azure` | native `OpenAIEmbeddingFunction` | `openai` SDK (`AzureOpenAI`) |
| `openrouter` | native `OpenAIEmbeddingFunction` | `openai` SDK with the OpenRouter `base_url` |
| `google-vertex` | `GoogleGenAIVertexEmbeddingFunction` | `google-genai` (legacy `vertexai` for old models) |
| `voyageai` | `VoyageAIEmbeddingFunction` | `voyageai` SDK |
| `watsonx` | `WatsonXEmbeddingFunction` | IBM watsonx SDK |
| `oracle` | `OracleEmbeddingFunction` | `oracledb` |
| `custom` | the callable you pass in | your code |

Only the first three were ported in this PR. `google-vertex`, `voyageai`, `watsonx` and `oracle` already had their own classes. For `google-vertex`, `voyageai` and `watsonx` only a type-only chromadb import was replaced; `custom` only had its type import replaced.

**Still use chromadb's class, loaded lazily on construction (need chromadb installed)**

| Provider name | chromadb class it loads |
|---|---|
| `amazon-bedrock` | `AmazonBedrockEmbeddingFunction` |
| `cohere` | `CohereEmbeddingFunction` |
| `google`, `google-generativeai` | `GoogleGenerativeAiEmbeddingFunction` |
| `huggingface` | `HuggingFaceEmbeddingFunction` |
| `instructor` | `InstructorEmbeddingFunction` |
| `jina` | `JinaEmbeddingFunction` |
| `ollama` | `OllamaEmbeddingFunction` |
| `onnx` | `ONNXMiniLM_L6_V2` |
| `openclip` | `OpenCLIPEmbeddingFunction` |
| `roboflow` | `RoboflowEmbeddingFunction` |
| `sentence-transformer` | `SentenceTransformerEmbeddingFunction` |
| `text2vec` | `Text2VecEmbeddingFunction` |

## Not in this PR

- `import crewai` still needs chromadb: `knowledge/storage/knowledge_storage.py` imports `ChromaDBConfig` at module level. That is Part 2.
- Qdrant's `EmbeddingFunction` protocol takes a single `str` and returns one flat vector, so it cannot use these native embedders without a small adapter. Part 2.
- Native ports of the remaining providers (cohere, jina, ollama, roboflow, huggingface, bedrock, google, local models).

## Testing

- New parity tests compare requests and vectors against chromadb's function with a mocked OpenAI client (OpenAI, Azure, OpenRouter). They skip if chromadb is missing.
- New tests for the lazy providers: each provider module imports with its chromadb module hidden, and constructing it raises the install message.
- New Memory test: default embedder `remember` / `recall` with a mocked network.
- `pytest tests/rag tests/memory tests/knowledge` plus the crewai-tools rag tests: 840 passed, 2 skipped. A wider run (`tests/utilities`, `tests/test_crew.py`, crewai-tools `tools`) also passed before the rebase onto main. `ruff` and `mypy` are clean.
- In a fresh venv with chromadb uninstalled (Part 2 storage modules stubbed so `import crewai` runs): `build_embedder` openai, Memory `remember` / `recall`, and the install-message error for cohere, jina, ollama, sentence-transformer, onnx, bedrock and google all behave as described, and chromadb is never imported. This was a manual script, not a committed test.
- Not tested: calls to the live OpenAI API (no key). A local fake-server run with the real `openai` SDK showed identical HTTP requests and vectors for the native and chromadb functions, but that script is not in the repo.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core embedding behavior for OpenAI/Azure/OpenRouter and Memory defaults; parity is tested but Chroma collections may treat the native function as a legacy embedder, and empty-input handling differs from chromadb.
> 
> **Overview**
> First step toward making ChromaDB optional: the embedding layer no longer depends on chromadb at import time for OpenAI-family providers.
> 
> **Native OpenAI embedder.** Adds `OpenAIEmbeddingFunction`, which talks to the `openai` SDK directly (including Azure via `AzureOpenAI` and OpenRouter-style `base_url`). `openai`, `azure`, `openrouter`, and Memory’s default embedder now use this class instead of chromadb’s implementation. Provider config, env aliases, and defaults are unchanged aside from **empty input raising `ValueError`** (chromadb previously returned `[]`).
> 
> **Lazy chromadb for other providers.** Introduces `load_chromadb_embedding_function` so bedrock, cohere, google-generativeai, huggingface, instructor, jina, ollama, onnx, openclip, roboflow, sentence-transformer, and text2vec only import chromadb when the provider is constructed; missing chromadb yields `ImportError` with `pip install crewai[chromadb]`. Custom `embedding_callable` overrides avoid chromadb entirely.
> 
> **Type decoupling.** Modules that only needed chromadb for types (custom, voyageai, ibm, google vertex) now use `crewai.rag.core` `EmbeddingFunction`, `Documents`, and `Embeddings`.
> 
> **Tests.** New coverage for native OpenAI parity vs chromadb (mocked), lazy-provider import/construct behavior, Azure/OpenRouter wiring, and Memory remember/recall with the default embedder.

title: Add GoldenDirectiveTool (harmonic relationship score, full vs cropped reporting)
body:
## Summary

Adds a `GoldenDirectiveTool` to `crewai_tools`
(`lib/crewai-tools`), a self-contained tool with no external
dependencies that calculates the Golden Directive relationship
score:

    Y = 2(A x E) / (A + E)

Inputs are an agent score A, an environment health score E (full
frame), and optionally a cropped-frame E. Output reports full Y,
and when a cropped E is given, cropped Y and the full-versus-cropped
gap, as the Directive's reporting rule requires: report full Y and
cropped Y, with the gap reported.

The Golden Directive (https://thegoldendirective.pages.dev/) is a
candidate training reward proposed by Paul Eisman: A is designed
to be grounded in resource ledgers, not self-report; E is the
health of everything not-A, against a healthy baseline. If either
A or E reaches 0, Y reaches 0.

Scope, stated plainly:

- This tool performs the calculation and reporting only. It does
  not measure A or E; in the source proposal, A and E measurement
  is not yet operational for real training.
- The Directive itself is a proposal, not a deployed solution.
  Its results so far are pilot-scale toy gridworld runs, reported
  on the site.

Per this repo's AGENTS.md: the diff is kept minimal, public API is
documented, and tests cover behaviour. A docs page under `docs/`
is suggested as a follow-up if maintainers want one; it is not
included in this diff.

## Tests

New `lib/crewai-tools/tests/tools/golden_directive_tool_test.py`:

- Canonical numeric checks: 8,8 -> 8; 8,7 -> 7.4667; 2,3 -> 2.4;
  A=0 or E=0 -> 0; 1,10 -> 1.8182; 10,9 -> 9.4737; negative inputs
  floored at 0.
- Behaviour: `run` reports full Y; with a cropped E it reports
  full Y 4.3636, cropped Y 7.4667, and gap 3.1030 for A=8.

Local run: the new test file passes against a real install of this repo's crewai-tools package, 3 passed. Note found while testing: tools must be exported from both `crewai_tools/tools/__init__.py` and the top-level `crewai_tools/__init__.py`; the first version of this change missed the top-level export and the import test caught it.

## Files changed

- `lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/tools/golden_directive_tool/golden_directive_tool.py` (new)
- `lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/tools/golden_directive_tool/__init__.py` (new, empty, matching neighbouring tools)
- `lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/tools/golden_directive_tool/README.md` (new)
- `lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/tools/__init__.py` (import + __all__ entry)
- `lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/__init__.py` (import + __all__ entry)
- `lib/crewai-tools/tests/tools/golden_directive_tool_test.py` (new)

title: fix(deps): pin crewai-files in the file-processing extra like its siblings
body:
`crewai` pins `crewai-core`, `crewai-cli` and `crewai-tools` to its own version, but its `file-processing` extra listed `crewai-files` with no version, and `devtools release` deliberately skipped it (#5847). A consumer that upgrades `crewai` therefore keeps whatever `crewai-files` its lockfile already had: crewAI-enterprise moved to crewai 1.15.34 still on crewai-files 1.15.29, which allows pypdf 6.21.2 and failed pip-audit. `crewai[file-processing]` now requires `crewai-files==<release version>`, and the release bump moves that pin with the others.

- `lib/crewai/pyproject.toml`: `"crewai-files"` → `"crewai-files==1.15.35"`; `uv.lock` is unchanged (workspace member)
- devtools: drop the file-processing skip and the extra-tracking code that only served it; nightly already rewrites this pin (`nightly.yml:80`)
- Tests: the bump rewrites the pin, a bump of the real `lib/crewai/pyproject.toml` moves all four sibling pins, and `crewai` pins every sibling to its own `__version__`; each fails with its fix reverted
- Compatibility: `crewai-files` has published alongside `crewai` on every release, so the exact pin always resolves
- Out: no change to already-published releases (1.15.34 and 1.15.35 stay unpinned); enterprise was fixed in its own lock (crewAI-enterprise #1409)

title: Replace deprecated asyncio.get_event_loop() with asyncio.get_running_loop() in coroutine contexts
body:
## Summary

`asyncio.get_event_loop()` is deprecated since Python 3.12 (and raises `RuntimeError` in Python 3.14 when no current loop exists). In coroutine contexts the recommended replacement is `asyncio.get_running_loop()`, which returns exactly the same loop with no deprecation.

This PR replaces the three usages in `lib/crewai` that are always executed inside a running event loop:

- `src/crewai/tools/structured_tool.py` — inside `async def _arun`, so a loop is always running
- `src/crewai/rag/chromadb/client.py` — inside `async def _alocked`, so a loop is always running
- `src/crewai/utilities/streaming.py` — the `use_async=True` branch of `create_streaming_state`, which is only reached from async kickoff paths (`Crew.kickoff_async` / streaming kickoff), so a loop is always running

## Changes

One-line, behavior-identical replacement of `asyncio.get_event_loop()` with `asyncio.get_running_loop()` in each of the three files above.

## Verification

- `py_compile` passes for all three files
- `ruff check --no-fix` reports no new findings on the changed lines (existing findings in these files are pre-existing and untouched)
- Call-path analysis confirms each site executes only inside a coroutine, so `get_running_loop()` returns the same loop `get_event_loop()` would

Fixes #8912

Note: this PR supersedes #8910, which was submitted without an issue reference and auto-closed by the first-time-contributor gate as a result (reopen is not permitted for external contributors).

## LLM disclosure

This change was prepared with the assistance of an AI coding agent and reviewed before submission. Per the repository's contribution guidelines, please add the `llm-generated` label to this PR if appropriate (I don't have permission to add labels myself).

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> **Low Risk**
> Mechanical asyncio API update with no logic changes; each site already runs only inside a coroutine, so the returned loop should match the previous behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces deprecated **`asyncio.get_event_loop()`** with **`asyncio.get_running_loop()`** in three **`lib/crewai`** call sites that always run inside an active event loop.
> 
> **ChromaDB async locking** (`_alocked`) still acquires the cross-process lock via **`run_in_executor`**, but now binds to the loop that is actually running. **Structured tool async invocation** (`ainvoke`) uses the same pattern when executing synchronous tool functions on a thread pool. **Streaming setup** (`create_streaming_state` with **`use_async=True`**) captures that loop for **`call_soon_threadsafe`** when LLM chunks are forwarded from sync event-bus handlers into an async queue.

title: fix(llm)!: raise MissingAPIKeyError for openai-compatible providers
body:
`LLM(model="deepseek/deepseek-chat")` with no key (or the `YOUR_API_KEY` placeholder) raised `ImportError("Error importing native provider: ...")`, because the OpenAI-compatible providers check the key in a pydantic validator and `LLM.__new__` wraps every construction failure. Users read it as a missing package and telemetry bucketed it with "litellm not installed". `LLM(...)` now takes the `MissingAPIKeyError` out of the `ValidationError` and raises it as itself, which is what #8731 already does for the native providers.

- Scope: openrouter, deepseek, cerebras, dashscope and deepinfra through `LLM(...)`; every other construction failure is still the same `ImportError`, and the key check still runs at construction.
- Compatibility: still a `ValueError`. `Agent(llm="deepseek/...")` now raises a `ValidationError` for `Agent` (a `ValueError` naming the key) instead of the `ImportError`, because pydantic wraps it again in Agent's validator.
- `crewai deploy` validation keeps the existing `llm_init_missing_key` warning for both shapes: a top-level `MissingAPIKeyError` and the `Agent` `ValidationError` that names a key.
- Tests cover all five providers (unset and placeholder), env and explicit keys, a non-key error staying `ImportError`, the Agent path, the deploy classifier, and a failed flow reporting `error_type=MissingAPIKeyError`.
- Out: direct `OpenAICompatibleCompletion(...)` construction still raises `ValidationError`. No lazy key check, so `Agent(llm="<compat>/...")` still can't report `MissingAPIKeyError` (needs a ticket). No change to `LLM.__new__`'s catch-all `ImportError`.

title: fix(telemetry): count repeated-tool-call stops in anonymous telemetry
body:
Since #8706 the repeated-tool-call guard stops the agent and keeps its work instead of raising `ToolExecutionFailedError`. That means anonymous telemetry no longer sees these stops as failed tasks, and nothing took their place, so after the release the drop would look like an improvement. Now the guard records one `tool_failure:repeated_call` Feature Usage count each time it stops a run.

- Scope: the count is recorded in `check_repeated_tool_call`, which every caller of the guard goes through: native and ReAct paths in `AgentExecutor` and in plan steps (`StepExecutor`). It is recorded under all three policies, including `ignore`, which emits no `ToolFailureDetectedEvent`.
- Privacy: only the fixed feature name and `crewai_version` are sent. No tool name, arguments, result or agent role. The span honours `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED`, `CREWAI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY` and `CREWAI_DISABLE_TRACKING`, like every other Feature Usage count.
- Tests: exactly one count from `Crew.kickoff`, `kickoff_async`, `akickoff`, `Agent.kickoff`, `kickoff_async` and a plan step, on both native and ReAct, and under `raise` and `ignore`. No count when the guard warns but does not stop. The exported span carries only the closed name, and nothing is sent under each opt-out. The #8706 tests are unchanged and pass.
- No public API change. The warehouse needs no change, because new Feature Usage strings show up in `canonical_feature_usage_daily` as they are.
- Out: no change to guard thresholds or behaviour, console output, the tracing listener or event classes. No docs row: the telemetry page does not list individual Feature Usage names for any family yet.

title: test(memory): add async parity and restart-persistence contract tests
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8137

Part of #8120. Builds on the shared backend fixtures from #8135 (merged in #8222).

## Summary

The `StorageBackend` contract declares `asave`/`asearch`/`adelete`, but nothing checked that they behave like `save`/`search`/`delete`, or that records written to a local store are still there after reopening it. `test_storage_backend_async_parity.py` runs one suite against LanceDB and Qdrant Edge, reusing `_record`, `_assert_same_record`, `VECTOR_DIM` and the backend params from `test_storage_backend_contract.py`. Runtime code is unchanged.

- **Async parity** (`TestAsyncParity`): a `storage_pair` fixture opens two isolated stores of the same backend under `tmp_path`; one is driven through the sync API and the other through the async API, so no store or lock is shared. Compares `asave` vs `save` (ids, fields, list order), `asearch` vs `search` across six filter combinations (ids, scores, fields), and `adelete` vs `delete` across seven selectors (`record_ids`, `scope_prefix`, `categories`, `metadata_filter`, `older_than`, scope+categories, everything) with an exact deletion count and identical remaining ids. Also covers the empty-store case.
- **Restart persistence** (`TestRestartPersistence`): closes the store and reopens the same path, then checks every record field, `list_records` order, scope and category counts, `list_scopes`, `get_scope_info`, search results, records written through `asave`, update-and-delete outcomes, and that reopening with `vector_dim=None` infers the dimension from the existing store.
- **Explicit errors** (`TestStorageErrors`): `EmbeddingDimensionMismatchError` from `save`/`asave`, `search`/`asearch`, a mixed-dimension batch (nothing written) and `update` (original record preserved); asserts `stored_dim`/`new_dim` and that it is a `ValueError` but not a `RuntimeError`, as `backend.py` documents.

Out of scope: locking, multi-process access, or same-store sync/async interleaving. Parity is checked on separate stores on purpose.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

- `uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/memory/test_storage_backend_async_parity.py -q`: 50 passed on both backends (`qdrant-edge-py` installed via `uv sync --all-groups --all-extras`).
- `uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/memory -q` on current `main`: 277 passed.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --diff` (with `--no-force-exclude`, since the ruff config excludes `lib/crewai/tests/`) and `mypy --follow-imports=silent` on the new file: clean. Pre-commit hooks pass.
- No paid API calls; fixed 4-dim vectors and temporary stores only.

## Additional context

Rebased onto `main` after #8222 merged; the PR is now a single commit adding one test file. Authored with an AI coding agent (Factory Droid), hence the `llm-generated` label request.

> 
> **Async parity** runs sync and async APIs on **isolated** twin stores so `asave`/`asearch`/`adelete` match `save`/`search`/`delete` (filters, deletion selectors, empty store).

title: fix(events): serialize tool usage exceptions in checkpoints

When a tool raises, `ToolUsageErrorEvent.error` holds the exception. title: fix(llms): resolve compatible-provider context windows from their own catalogs
body:
## Summary

`OpenAICompatibleCompletion` inherited `get_context_window_size` from `OpenAICompletion`, which looks the model up in `OPENAI_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` — a table filtered to `litellm_provider == "openai"`. None of the OpenAI-compatible providers' catalogued models can ever match, so every Fireworks, DeepInfra or Groq model compacted against the 8,192 default even though the LiteLLM catalog publishes a limit for it.

The catalog actually holds entries for these providers:

```python
>>> from crewai.llms.context_window import _CATALOG, context_windows_from_catalog
>>> for p in ("fireworks_ai", "deepinfra", "dashscope", "snowflake", "groq"):
...     print(p, len(context_windows_from_catalog(_CATALOG, providers=frozenset({p}))))
fireworks_ai 660
deepinfra 272
dashscope 86
snowflake 74
groq 18
```

One concrete casualty: `Gryphe/MythoMax-L2-13b` is catalogued at 4,096, but resolved to the 8,192 default (6,963 usable), so an agent working with it would compact four times as early as it needed to.

## The fix

- `lib/crewai/src/crewai/llms/context_window.py`: `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_CONTEXT_WINDOWS`, a per-provider table built the same way as the other provider tables.
- `lib/crewai/src/crewai/llms/providers/openai_compatible/completion.py`: `get_context_window_size` merges the provider's own entries over the OpenAI table (a compatible endpoint may serve models under their OpenAI names) and resolves as before, so an explicit `context_window_size` still wins and an unknown id still falls back to the default.

`together` has no catalog entries, so it keeps the documented default — unchanged behaviour.

## Testing

```
python -m pytest lib/crewai/tests/llms/openai_compatible/test_openai_compatible.py
67 passed
```

`TestContextWindow` (4 tests) is red on unmodified `main` for the two catalogued DeepInfra ids:

```
# before
FAILED ...::test_window_comes_from_the_provider_catalog[deepinfra-Gryphe/MythoMax-L2-13b-4096]
FAILED ...::test_window_comes_from_the_provider_catalog[deepinfra-NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-405B-131072]
2 failed, 2 passed
# after
4 passed
```

Note: `lib/crewai/tests/llms/test_context_window.py` has 20 pre-existing failures on unmodified `main` in this environment (a `Model must be a non-empty string` validation error in `OpenAICompatibleCompletion` construction, unrelated to this change); the same 20 fail with this branch applied, no more.

`ruff check` passes on both touched files.

## AI assistance

Written with AI assistance (WorkBuddy) and reviewed before submission.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes usable context budgets for many OpenAI-compatible models, which directly affects when CrewAI compacts or summarizes conversations; behavior is more correct but not identical to the old default.
> 
> **Overview**
> **OpenAI-compatible LLMs** (DeepInfra, Groq, Fireworks, Dashscope, Snowflake, etc.) no longer treat every model as an **8,192-token** window when the LiteLLM catalog lists a real limit. `OpenAICompatibleCompletion` previously inherited lookup against **`OPENAI_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` only**, which is filtered to `litellm_provider == "openai"`, so catalogued third-party ids never matched and agents could **compact or summarize too early** (or with the wrong budget).
> 
> The change adds **`OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_CONTEXT_WINDOWS`**—per-provider maps built from the same catalog snapshot—and overrides **`get_context_window_size`** to resolve against **OpenAI entries merged with the active provider’s table**. An explicit **`context_window_size`** still wins; unknown models still fall back to the default and usage ratio.
> 
> **Tests** cover DeepInfra catalog hits, default fallback, and explicit override.

title: feat(devtools): open a standalone litellm catalog PR before the version bump
body:
## Related issue

None. Internal release-tooling change.

## Summary

### What changed

- `devtools release` gets a new **Phase 0** that downloads the LiteLLM model catalog and opens its own PR (`chore: update litellm model catalog for vX.Y.Z`, branch `chore/update-litellm-catalog-vX.Y.Z`). It waits for that PR to merge, then pulls `main` before the version bump starts.
- If the upstream catalog is identical to the checked-in file, no branch or PR is created, so re-running a failed release is safe.
- New flag `--skip-litellm-catalog-update` skips Phase 0. It is carried into the resume hints printed on failure.
- The catalog download is **removed from the `[docs-freeze]` docs PR** (`_update_docs_and_create_pr`).
- `lib/devtools/README.md`, the `release` docstring and the `litellm_catalog_update` / `scripts/update_litellm_catalog.py` docstrings are updated to match.

### Why

The catalog JSON (~3 MB, hundreds of changed entries per refresh) was bundled into the docs-freeze PR, which already carries the edge changelogs and a ~770-file `docs/vX.Y.Z/` snapshot. That made the catalog change hard to review and tied a model-data update to a docs freeze. Refreshing it was also easy to miss: the last refresh was in the v1.15.31 docs PR, and upstream has since added 214 models, removed 1 and changed 457. A standalone PR makes the diff reviewable, lets it be reverted on its own, and lands the catalog on `main` before the release commits.

### New flow (`devtools release X.Y.Z`)

1. **Phase 0 (new):** catalog PR, skipped if unchanged or with `--skip-litellm-catalog-update`, then waits for merge.
2. **Phase 1:** `feat: bump versions to X.Y.Z` PR, then waits for merge.
3. **Phase 2:** release notes, then the docs PR (edge changelogs, plus the `docs/vX.Y.Z` snapshot and `docs.json` for stable releases; no catalog any more), then tag and GitHub release, PyPI publish, and deployment canary repos.
4. **Phase 3:** enterprise release (unchanged).

Behavior note: `devtools tag` used to refresh the catalog via the docs PR; it no longer does. Only `release` (Phase 0) and `scripts/update_litellm_catalog.py` refresh it now.

## Verification

- [ ] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

`ruff check`, `ruff format` and `pytest lib/devtools/tests` (100 passed) are clean. `devtools release 9.9.9 --dry-run --skip-enterprise --no-edit` shows Phase 0 before Phase 1, and with `--skip-litellm-catalog-update` it prints the skip message and goes straight to Phase 1. The new git/gh steps in Phase 0 were not exercised against a real remote, and I did not add a unit test for them.

## Additional context

The first catalog PR after this lands will drop `eu.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` from the catalog; worth confirming nothing depends on that ID.

title: fix(compat): restore removed import paths with deprecation warnings
body:
## Problem
Code written against 1.15.28 fails at import time on 1.15.29+ because several public paths were moved or removed with nothing left behind. I diffed the public surface of 1.15.28 and 1.15.33 (static with griffe, then at runtime from both PyPI installs). Of ~2,200 public definitions, 7 changed, and 5 of those still break on 1.15.33:

| Old path | Now | Before this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `crewai.experimental.AgentExecutor`, `CrewAgentExecutorFlow` | `crewai.agents.agent_executor.AgentExecutor` | `AttributeError` |
| `crewai.experimental.agent_executor` | `crewai.agents.agent_executor` | `ModuleNotFoundError` |
| `crewai.utilities.agent_utils.summarize_messages` | `crewai.llms.context_window.summarize_messages` | `AttributeError` |
| `crewai.agents.CrewAgentExecutor` | removed | bare `AttributeError` |

(`message_content_text` and `format_message_for_llm` were already restored in #8746.)

## Change
- The `experimental` names and module resolve to `AgentExecutor` again and emit a `DeprecationWarning` naming the replacement.
- `agent_utils.summarize_messages` is a wrapper that **keeps the old argument order** `(messages, llm, callbacks, verbose=True)`. The replacement takes `llm` first, so a plain re-export would silently swap the two arguments.
- `from crewai.agents import CrewAgentExecutor` now raises an `ImportError` that names `AgentExecutor` rather than a bare `AttributeError`. The class itself is **not** restored: the new executor has no equivalent hooks, so an alias would give false confidence.
- `SummarizeMessages` is not restored. It was an implementation detail and its internals were deleted.

## Decision to review
`test_experimental_executor_import_is_removed` (added in #8192) asserted the experimental paths stay removed. This PR reverses that on purpose, so I removed the test. `tests/test_imports.py` now covers the restored behavior instead. If the intent is to keep these paths gone, close this PR.

## Verification
- 4 new tests in `tests/test_imports.py`; they fail on `main` and pass here.
- `tests/utilities`, `tests/agents` and `tests/test_imports.py`: 1239 passed, 15 skipped.
- ruff, ruff-format and mypy pass via pre-commit.

Not included: docs and translations (`docs/edge/en`, then ar/ko/pt-BR). Happy to add them here or separately.

title: fix(llm): don't require newer litellm just for a type-hint import
body:
## Problem
Since #8676, `_ensure_litellm()` imports `ChatCompletionDeltaCustomToolCall` from `litellm.types.utils` together with the other litellm symbols. Older litellm releases (e.g. 1.82.6) don't have it, so the `ImportError` sets `LITELLM_AVAILABLE = False` and `LLM.__new__` reports "the LiteLLM fallback package is not installed" even though `import litellm` works. Every model that goes through the fallback then fails at `LLM(...)`.

Repro:
```
OPENAI_API_KEY=x uv run --no-project --with crewai==1.15.31 --with litellm==1.82.6 python -c "from crewai import LLM; LLM(model='openai/openai/gpt-5.6-luna')"
```

## Cause
The class is only used in a local variable annotation (`llm.py`, streaming handler), which is never evaluated at runtime, and the code already filters with `isinstance(tool_call, ChatCompletionDeltaToolCall)`. The unconditional import turned an unstated newer-litellm requirement into a hard failure for anyone not on the `litellm` extra's pin.

## Change
Import `ChatCompletionDeltaCustomToolCall` in its own nested `try/except ImportError` and leave it `None` when missing. No behavior change on newer litellm.

## Verification
- Repro above with litellm 1.82.6 and this branch: `LLM(...)` builds with `is_litellm=True`.
- `ruff` error count on `llm.py` unchanged (28 before and after).
- No regression test added.

title: fix(llm): keep choices of streaming chunks that also carry usage
body:
Chat Completions providers such as DeepSeek put the token usage on the last chunk, which also holds the final text delta, tool-call delta and `finish_reason`. All three Chat Completions streaming handlers in `lib/crewai/src/crewai/llms/providers/openai/completion.py` returned early as soon as they saw usage, so the rest of that chunk was dropped:

- sync stream (was line 2578): tail of the answer, end of tool arguments, finish reason
- async `response_model` stream (was line 2863): JSON suffix, so validation failed
- async stream (was line 2930): same losses as the sync path

The early return is removed; chunks without choices (usage-only) are still skipped by the existing check right after.

Verification:
- `uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/llms/openai/test_streaming_usage_chunks.py -q` (new regression tests, fail before the fix)
- `uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/llms/openai -q` -> 307 passed, 1 skipped
- `uv run ruff check lib/` and `uv run ruff format --check lib/`

AI-assisted: this change was written with an AI agent. The `llm-generated` label could not be applied (no triage permission).

Fixes #8775

---

> **Low Risk**
> Small, localized change to streaming chunk handling with dedicated regression tests; behavior change only fixes dropped final-chunk data.

title: feat(llm): resolve tool support from the LiteLLM catalog
body:
## Summary

Makes the LiteLLM model catalog decide whether a model supports tool use, with a user-controllable `supports_tools` setting that always takes precedence.

> **Stacked on #8742** (`viditostwal/litellm-catalog-lookup`). Merge #8742 first; this PR then retargets to `main`. If #8742 is squash-merged, rebase this branch onto `main` to drop the lookup commits.

## Changes

- **`BaseLLM.supports_tools: bool | None = None`**: available on every provider and on the LiteLLM path.
  - `True` / `False`: the user's value is final.
  - Not passed: the provider's class default applies. Anthropic and Bedrock keep `True`, and Gemini keeps its model-version check (>= 1.5). Existing behavior is unchanged.
  - Explicit `None`: the catalog's `supports_function_calling` decides, then the provider's default is the last resort.
  - OpenAI, Azure, Snowflake and `LLM` (LiteLLM path) default to `None`, so they use the catalog and then their existing heuristics (`not is_o1_model`, `is_openai_model`, model-prefix check).
- **`BaseLLM._resolve_supports_function_calling(default)`**: one helper for that order. Each provider's `supports_function_calling()` is a one-liner passing its own default.
- **Gemini**: the validator fills the version default only when `supports_tools` is not passed. Previously it overwrote any value, including an explicit one. The same check is shared through `_supports_tools_by_version`.
- **Request gates**: Anthropic, Gemini and Bedrock now send tools only when `supports_function_calling()` is true.
- **`llm.py`**: the LiteLLM path honors an explicit `supports_tools`, then the catalog, then LiteLLM's own check.

## Tests

- `tests/llms/test_function_calling_capabilities.py`: explicit `supports_tools` wins over the catalog in both directions (Anthropic, Bedrock, Gemini, OpenAI, Azure); provider defaults hold when the value is not passed; explicit `None` uses the catalog and then the provider default (including Gemini by model version); request gates for each provider; real catalog lookups through the native classes and through `LLM(model="provider/model")`.
- A `stub_catalog` fixture patches the lookup instead of setting private attributes.
- `tests/llms`: 1010 passed, 17 failed. The same 17 fail on `main` without this branch (multimodal, reasoning-effort forwarding, and the Anthropic/Bedrock "model not supported" tests).

## Notes

- Commits `fed63da12` and `613c6517a` were made with `--no-verify`: the mypy hook reports 4 LiteLLM-type errors in `llm.py` (`ChatCompletionDeltaCustomToolCall`, an unused `type: ignore`, an unfollowed import). They also occur without these changes.
- The history includes a few commits that reverse each other while the `supports_tools` semantics were settled. Squash-merge is recommended.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes tool-use detection and API request shaping across all LLM providers; mis-resolution could drop tools or send them to unsupported models.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces a unified way to decide whether an LLM may use tools: optional **`supports_tools`** on `BaseLLM`, then the LiteLLM catalog’s **`supports_function_calling`**, then each provider’s existing heuristic.
> 
> **`supports_tools`** is now `bool | None` (default `None`). When set to `True` or `False`, that choice wins. When unset, native providers still apply their class defaults (e.g. Anthropic/Bedrock default `True`); explicit `None` defers to the catalog before the provider default. OpenAI, Azure, Snowflake, and the LiteLLM **`LLM`** path use **`_resolve_supports_function_calling(default=...)`** so catalog data can override heuristics like “not o1” or “Azure OpenAI only.”
> 
> **Request building** on Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, and Azure now gates **`tools`** on **`supports_function_calling()`** instead of reading **`supports_tools`** directly—so catalog-driven “no tools” actually omits tool payloads (including enabling tools on non–OpenAI Azure models when **`supports_tools=True`**).
> 
> **Gemini** no longer overwrites **`supports_tools`** in its validator; version ≥1.5 remains the fallback via **`_supports_tools_by_version`**. Docs (EN/AR/KO/pt-BR) and **`AGENTS.md`** document the override semantics and tell contributors to call **`supports_function_calling()`**, not gate on the field.
>

title: fix(deps): let crewai[litellm] import on python 3.10; raise joserfc, pyasn1, pypdf floors
body:
`crewai[litellm]` allowed only litellm 1.100.4, which imports `typing.NotRequired` and fails to import on Python 3.10. crewai then reports LiteLLM as not installed and tells 3.10 users to run `uv add 'crewai[litellm]'`, which they already did. The extra now allows exactly **litellm 1.105.3** (`>=1.105.3,<1.105.4`), which imports on 3.10.

(#8777 fixed a different case: an older litellm without `ChatCompletionDeltaCustomToolCall`. On 3.10 with 1.100.4 the import fails before that code runs.)

- **One reviewed release, never a range.** A user's install resolves to the newest release a range allows, and the lockfile doesn't change that. With `>=1.104.0,<1.106` they would get 1.105.7 today, which was never tested, and any later 1.105.x automatically. litellm has shipped compromised releases before (GHSA-5mg7-485q-xm76, 1.82.7–1.82.8). Moving litellm stays a crewAI release, as with 1.100.4. The root `pyproject.toml` comment records this.
- **1.105.3 has no known advisory.** I checked it against GitHub's advisory database and OSV on 2026-10-31. It is patched for GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222, GHSA-g5ff-637f-6q2m and GHSA-7hp6-4w63-5g45 (the last one hit 1.104.0rc1 on this line, not a final release).
- **Why not 1.106:** 1.106.x imports `mcp.types.CacheableResult`, which no released `mcp` 1.x has, so its tool calls fail.
- LiteLLM stays an optional extra, and installs without it are unchanged. The `.env.test` setting `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` is test-only: 1.104+ fetches the price map on import and falls back only on httpx errors, not on `--block-network`'s `RuntimeError`. Users offline still fall back.
- Removes the 3.10 skips from #8676 (the conftest import hook and `requires_litellm_python_311`), so 3.10 CI runs the LiteLLM paths again. Adds `test_an_installed_litellm_loads`, which fails on 3.10 with 1.100.4 and passes with 1.105.3.
- Tests on Python 3.10 and 3.13 (LLM, LiteLLM streaming and usage, every provider under `tests/llms`, hooks, agent_utils): 1,496 passed on each, with litellm 1.105.3 installed. `test_an_installed_litellm_loads` runs and passes on 3.10.
- **Security floors, so `pip-audit` passes again.** 13 advisories published 2026-10-30 turned the scan red on `main` and on every PR (confirmed on `main` at 97bbfb648): joserfc 1.7.1 (GHSA-jpxq-7h8p-2q76, GHSA-9pg5-8c7x-5hfx), pyasn1 0.6.4 (GHSA-2qm8-x737-gmw5, GHSA-fm9c-5rcf-2q5p, GHSA-mm57-4v3p-rchx, GHSA-9m75-vc3g-4x39) and pypdf 6.21.2 (GHSA-62m5-6wh8-28x7, GHSA-42gh-23hr-vphw, GHSA-x3rh-gjgm-fmqc, GHSA-4vqv-7265-gm2w, GHSA-5849-834g-hvw5, GHSA-mfr5-77xh-9j7h, GHSA-cggf-277g-3q54). Floors: `joserfc>=1.7.6` (new override; via authlib), `pyasn1>=0.6.5`, `pypdf>=6.21.4` (override and crewai-files' own requirement, so a crewai-files install gets it too). pypdf's `exclude-newer-package` date moves to 2026-10-29 to admit 6.21.4. The lock moves only these three (joserfc 1.7.7, pyasn1 0.6.5, pypdf 6.21.4). Local pip-audit with CI's ignore list: no known vulnerabilities. crewai-files (180 passed) and the read-file tool (11 passed) on 3.10 and 3.13, plus the suites above again.
- Not in this PR: moving to the 1.106 line once `mcp` ships `CacheableResult` (needs a ticket), and deleting the now-empty `lib/crewai/tests/conftest.py`.

title: fix(mcp): await async tool_filter so blocked tools are dropped
body:
## Summary

`create_dynamic_tool_filter` documents `async def` filters, but `MCPToolResolver._resolve_native` used the coroutine return value as the keep/drop verdict. Coroutines are always truthy, so every tool passed and only a `RuntimeWarning` was emitted.

Await awaitable filter results (same running-loop / `asyncio.run` pattern as native tool discovery) before deciding whether to keep a tool.

Fixes #8680

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/mcp/test_tool_resolver_native.py::TestResolveNativeAsyncToolFilter lib/crewai/tests/mcp/test_tool_resolver_native.py::TestResolveNativeEmptyTools`

AI assistance: Cursor was used to draft this change; I reviewed and tested it.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes which MCP tools are exposed to agents when async filters are used; incorrect behavior previously bypassed filtering entirely.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a bug where **async** `tool_filter` callbacks on native MCP configs were never awaited, so the keep/drop check saw a truthy coroutine and **every tool was registered** despite filters meant to block some (e.g. dangerous tools).
> 
> Adds `_coerce_filter_verdict` in `MCPToolResolver` to normalize filter results: await awaitables via `asyncio.run`, or run them in a thread with copied `contextvars` when a loop is already running—the same pattern used for native tool discovery. `_resolve_native` now passes the filter return value through that helper before adding tools to the list.
> 
> Adds a test that an async filter excluding `danger_*` tools actually drops them while keeping allowed tools.

title: fix(cli): offer a login and retry once when amp rejects the saved login during eval
body:
When AMP answered 401 to the saved login (expired or revoked), the evaluation just stopped: `cli_usage:eval_stopped:amp_401` ended evaluations for 11 projects between Oct 14 and 27. Now `crewai eval` at a terminal and the run app's Evaluate start `crewai login` once and retry the evaluation once with the new login, as the run app's Deploy has done since #8594.

- Scope: the evaluation start in `crewai eval` and the run app's Evaluate share `_start_logging_in_once`. It offers a login only for a 401 to a request that carried the saved login, and only at a terminal (no TTY or `CREWAI_DMN`: still `amp_401` with the `crewai login` sentence).
- Run app: it suspends itself (Textual `App.suspend`, first use here) for the login and resumes for the retry, so the verdict stays on its screen (`action_evaluate_crew` says Evaluate deliberately does not leave). Exit-and-chain like Deploy would need wiring in three runners and would close the screen.
- Telemetry, mirroring Deploy: `cli_usage:eval_login_prompted`, then `cli_usage:eval_stopped:login_abandoned|login_timed_out|login_failed|login_still_required` (added to `StopReason`). No ids or messages in event names.
- Tests: both entry points cover 401 then login then a successful retry (one login, one retry, events in order), each failed login with its stop and message, a second 401, no terminal, and unchanged 403/404. The 11 behavior tests fail on main.
- No docs: nothing under `docs/edge` describes eval's login or stop events.
- Out: no change to Deploy, to how AMP is called, or to 403/404 handling. No login offer for a 401 met while polling, for `--models` or `export`, or for an anonymous 401 (`account_required`, no saved login).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how saved credentials are refreshed during evaluation start (401-only, one retry), but scope is narrow and mirrors existing Deploy login behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> When CrewAI AMP rejects the **saved login** with **401**, evaluations no longer stop immediately. **`crewai eval`** (interactive terminal) and the run app **Evaluate** now share **`_start_logging_in_once`**: offer **`crewai login` once**, rebuild the AMP client, and **retry the evaluation start once**. A second 401 becomes **`login_still_required`**; non-401 refusals and anonymous 401s behave as before.
> 
> The run app wires this through a new **`log_in`** callback on **`evaluate_run`**. **`_log_in_for_the_evaluation`** uses Textual **`App.suspend()`** so the browser login flow can use the terminal, restores **SIGINT** during login, and falls back to the old refusal message if suspend is unsupported.

> Telemetry adds **`cli_usage:eval_login_prompted`** and stop reasons **`login_abandoned`**, **`login_timed_out`**, **`login_failed`**, and **`login_still_required`**. Tests cover both CLI and TUI paths for success, failed login, double 401, no TTY, and unchanged 403/404.

title: fix(llm): keep the provider's exception on litellm streaming errors
body:
The LiteLLM sync streaming path wrapped every provider failure in a bare `Exception("Failed to get streaming response: ...")` and also emitted `LLMCallFailedEvent` on top of the one `call()` emits. The run app streams every JSON crew, so auth, rate-limit and bad-request errors reached users and telemetry as `Exception`: 25 of 282 new task-running projects on 1.15.29+ (17 of 343 before), 23 of them JSON crews, and 8 of 10 JSON crews on groq. The handler now re-raises the provider's own exception and leaves the single failed event to `call()`, matching async streaming and both non-streaming paths.

- Scope: `LLM._handle_streaming_response` only; async streaming already re-raised the original and is unchanged.
- Compat: callers catching `Exception` still catch it, but the type is now the provider's (e.g. `litellm.AuthenticationError`), so `Agent` stops retrying litellm errors on streaming runs, the same as non-streaming already does.
- Tests: the sync/async × streaming/non-streaming matrix for auth, rate-limit and bad-request errors, plus context-window conversion, partial-response return, the unsupported-`stop` retry, and a streaming crew whose `TaskFailedEvent.error_type` is the provider class; 8 of the new tests fail on main.
- Out: no change to native providers, the empty-stream error (#8729), retry logic or message text.

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes error propagation on a hot path used by streamed JSON crews; behavior improves but callers that relied on the old generic `Exception` type will now see LiteLLM-specific exceptions.

title: fix(llm): raise MissingAPIKeyError for a missing or placeholder api key
body:
A missing provider key raised a bare `ValueError` ("OPENAI_API_KEY is required") that users and telemetry (which records only the exception class) could not tell apart from any other `ValueError`, and the `YOUR_API_KEY` placeholder that `crewai create flow` writes to `.env` passed the presence check and failed later at the provider as an authentication error. Native providers now raise `MissingAPIKeyError`, a `ValueError` subclass that names the env var and the model and says to set the key in `.env` and run `crewai run` again, and treat the exact placeholder as no key.

- Scope: OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure (chat completions without azure-identity, and the Responses delegate), Gemini (without Vertex ADC) and the OpenAI-compatible providers.
- Credential choice: a placeholder never hides a real key (Gemini `GOOGLE_API_KEY` placeholder no longer shadows `GEMINI_API_KEY`); Gemini translates only the SDK's missing-key error; the Azure Responses delegate uses the Azure key and keeps its existing `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback.
- Compatibility: `except ValueError` still catches it; the OpenAI-compatible `_resolve_api_key` private helper now takes the model instead of the provider name.
- Tests: sync/async/streaming, native and `LLM(...)`, env and explicit keys, placeholder precedence, late-set keys, telemetry `error_type`, deploy validation; the Gemini precedence, Gemini error-narrowing and Azure Responses regressions fail on the previous commit.

title: feat(cli): record where crewai run stops before kickoff
body:
Of 574 new projects (Oct 14-25) that never ran a crew or flow within 48 hours, 548 sent no event after `crewai create`, because `Crew Created` only fires at kickoff: we could not tell a developer who never typed `crewai run` from one whose run failed first. `crewai run` now records `cli_usage:run_started:<kind>` when it starts and `cli_usage:run_stopped:<reason>` where it ends before kickoff.

title: fix(llm): retry an empty llm answer once and raise a typed error
body:
The Oct 28 telemetry dig found `ValueError` is the most common task error class, and crewAI's own empty-answer error (`ValueError("Invalid response from LLM call - None or empty.")`) sits inside it, indistinguishable from user-code errors because telemetry records only the class name. A single empty answer also ended the run, and LiteLLM sync streaming raised a bare `Exception` for the same case.

Now the agent loop resends the same call once when the answer is empty (no content, no tool calls), and raises `EmptyLLMResponseError` naming the model if the retry is empty too.

- Scope: `get_llm_response`, `aget_llm_response` and the forced final answer at max iterations in `agent_utils.py` (Agent/Crew executor and LiteAgent), plus LiteLLM sync streaming in `llm.py`, which now raises the typed error with one `LLMCallFailedEvent` instead of two.
- RPM: the retry, and the forced final answer (never admitted before), now go through the executor's `max_rpm` limiter, so each physical request counts once.
- Compat: `EmptyLLMResponseError` lives in `crewai.llms.base_llm` beside `LLMCallBlockedError` and subclasses `ValueError`; there is one extra model call, and only when the answer was empty.
- Tests drive fake LLMs through sync, async, both LiteLLM streaming modes, ReAct and native tool follow-up turns, Agent.kickoff, Crew and LiteAgent; new tests fail on main, including max_rpm counts for both attempts.
- Docs: "Empty Responses" tab in `concepts/llms.mdx` for en, ar, ko and pt-BR.
- Out: no configurable retry count, no backoff, no change to provider-level retries or to native providers' empty handling (Bedrock still substitutes fallback text), no new telemetry event.

Fixes #8723

## Summary

`_ensure_litellm()` imported `ChatCompletionDeltaCustomToolCall` (added in #8676), but litellm only has it since 1.97.0. title: fix(events): track sync-handler futures in mixed-handler emit so flush() waits for them
body:
## Bug

`CrewAIEventsBus.emit()` submits sync handlers to `_sync_executor` but only
tracks the returned future when **no** async handlers are registered (the
no-dependency path):

```python
sync_future = self._sync_executor.submit(
    ctx.run, self._call_handlers, source, event, sync_handlers, state
)
if not async_handlers:
    return self._track_future(sync_future)
```

With mixed sync+async handlers, the sync future is neither tracked nor
returned, so:

1. `flush()` returns `True` while a sync handler is still running —
   violating its documented contract ("ensure all event handlers have
   completed before returning").
2. Exceptions raised by the sync handler are silently dropped: nobody
   retrieves `future.exception()`, whereas the sync-only path surfaces them
   via `flush()`.
3. The shutdown path never waits for that future either.

`replay()` in the same file already does this correctly — it tracks the sync
future unconditionally before the early return. This PR aligns `emit()`
with it.

## Reproduction

One slow sync handler + one fast async handler, then emit + flush:

```text
flush returned: True
async handler done: True
sync handler done:  False   # flush() returned before the sync handler finished
```

After the fix, `flush()` waits for both handlers.

## Testing

New `tests/events/test_emit_mixed_handlers_flush.py`:

- `test_flush_waits_for_pending_sync_handler` — fails before the fix, passes after
- `test_flush_reports_sync_handler_exception` — sync handler errors now
  surface through `flush()` instead of being silently dropped

All three dispatch paths (mixed, sync-only, async-only) verified to wait
correctly.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Small, targeted change to event dispatch bookkeeping with regression tests; no auth, data, or API surface changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`CrewAIEventsBus.emit()`** when both sync and async handlers are registered for the same event. Sync work was submitted to the thread pool but its future was only added to **`_pending_futures`** (via **`_track_future`**) on the sync-only path, so **`flush()`** and shutdown could finish while sync handlers were still running and sync handler exceptions were never surfaced through flush.
> 
> **`emit()`** now always tracks the sync-handler future after submit (same as **`replay()`**), while still returning the async future when both handler types exist. Regression tests cover flush waiting on a slow sync handler alongside a fast async handler, and flush reporting sync handler errors instead of dropping them silently.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 25f11d5a81db91070fcbb5af634775796f718552. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(agent): count each tool call toward max_iter
body:
Issue 5 of crewai-upstream-issues-1.15.30.md (found by the support-investigator on 1.15.30) shows that on the native tool path, `max_iter` counts LLM steps, not tool calls. Because of that, one parallel batch could run any number of tools: one run made 198 calls under `max_iter=30`. Now every native tool call that runs counts toward `max_iter`. A step that asks for more calls than the remaining budget runs only the first ones, in order. Each call past the budget gets a "not run, iteration limit reached" tool result, and then the existing forced final answer runs.

- Scope: only `execute_native_tool` in `agents/agent_executor.py`. The text (ReAct) path, LiteAgent and planning `max_step_iterations` are unchanged, and each now has a docstring and docs note.
- Compatibility: this changes what the public `max_iter` means. Since 1.9.0 (#4258), a native parallel batch counted as one iteration, so agents that make many parallel calls will stop sooner. The upgrade guide says to raise `max_iter`. The other option was a new `max_tool_calls` parameter, which reviewers should weigh before merging.
- Tests: new `test_max_iter_tool_calls.py` covers sync/async and parallel/sequential batches, budgets carried across steps, `result_as_answer` inside and past the budget, the text path, hook `iterations`, and a crew task. Ten provider batch tests now use `max_iter=10` so they still end on the model's answer.
- Docs: `concepts/agents.mdx`, `learn/llm-hooks.mdx` and `guides/migration/upgrading-crewai.mdx` are updated in en, ar, ko and pt-BR.
- Out: no `max_tool_calls` parameter, no change to the `max_iter` default, no fix for the docs' wrong "Default is 20", and no re-recorded cassettes. Needs a Linear ticket: the forced final answer after a native tool turn sends tool_use/tool_result history with no `tools` param. That predates this PR. I believe, unverified, that Anthropic rejects it, and this change makes that path easier to reach, so it needs a recorded Anthropic cassette.

In `execute_native_tool`, only calls that fit the remaining budget run (in order); the rest get a synthetic tool message that the iteration limit was reached, then the existing forced final-answer path applies.

title: fix(agent): warn on repeated tool calls and keep the work when stopping
body:
When an agent called the same tool with the same arguments five times in a row and got the same result, it raised an error and lost the work it had done (issue 4 of crewai-upstream-issues-1.15.30.md, found by support-investigator on 1.15.30). Now the model gets a warning on the 4th identical result, and on the 5th the agent is forced to give a final answer through the existing max-iterations path. A plan step ends with the tool results it already has.

- Scope: AgentExecutor sync/async, native and text tools, parallel calls in one step (counted in the order the model made them), and StepExecutor plan steps; only consecutive identical (tool, args, result) calls count, and a changed result still resets the streak.
- Compat: the stop is reported as a `REPEATED_CALL` ToolFailure under `tool_failure_policy` (recorded + `ToolFailureDetectedEvent`; `raise` still raises `ToolExecutionFailedError`); `check_repeated_tool_call` gains an optional `crew` and now returns the warning note instead of `None`; `ToolResult` gains `raw_result` (excluded from equality; an explicit `None` is kept). Known effects: under `raise` identical parallel calls all finish before the abort, a forced stop prints "Maximum iterations reached" in verbose mode, and on text-based calling the warning and the stop each come one call later because ToolUsage answers the 2nd identical call with its own notice.

title: fix(llm): honor context_window_size and warn on the fallback window
body:
Issue 1 in crewai-upstream-issues-1.15.30.md (found by the support investigator on 1.15.30): `LLM(context_window_size=...)` was not honored on native providers. `get_context_window_size()` used only the model catalog, so a model it does not list, such as a new OpenRouter model, quietly got the 8192-token fallback, and tool results were deferred and context compacted far too early. Native providers also forwarded the value to the provider API through `additional_params`. Now an explicit `context_window_size` wins over the catalog on every provider. A catalog fallback logs one warning per model that names the fallback size and shows the `LLM(model=..., context_window_size=<tokens>)` fix.

- Scope: `context_window_size` is now a declared field on `BaseLLM` (strict positive int; the duplicate on `LLM` is removed). `resolve_context_window_size` gets a keyword-only `configured=`, and LiteLLM, OpenAI/OpenAI-compatible/Snowflake, Azure, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock and the `BaseLLM` default all pass it. The explicit value gets the same 0.85 ratio as the catalog, including on the LiteLLM path, which used to take it as-is.
- Compat: catalog sizes, provider fallback defaults and the positional resolver signature are unchanged. A negative value or a non-int (including bool) now raises. Older dumps and checkpoints are read with two shims (remove in 2.0): `0` means unset, and a value equal to the 85% window `LLM` used to cache into the field is dropped, so restores are not scaled twice. The value is never sent to the provider API, and it survives `model_dump`, checkpoint restore and `to_config_dict`.
- Tests: the explicit value is honored on every provider and on a custom `BaseLLM`; fallback warns once per model; it moves the deferral and compaction gates; validation; checkpoint and config-dict round trips, including a pre-change checkpoint with a cached window.
- Docs: a "Models CrewAI does not know" paragraph in the Context Window Management section of `concepts/llms.mdx`, in en, ar, ko and pt-BR.
- Out: no OpenRouter live model or `context_length` lookup, no change to when tool results are deferred or context compacted ("don't defer or compact from a fallback size" needs a Linear ticket), and `llm_overlay` model swaps do not carry the value (on purpose). Each also needs a Linear ticket: `OpenAICompatibleCompletion` restores from a checkpoint as `OpenAICompletion`, `LLM(...)` wraps native validation errors in `ImportError`, and pre-change native-provider checkpoints keep `context_window_size` in `additional_params`.
