title: fix(ci): preserve maintainer-reopened pull requests
body:
## Summary

Prevent the first-time-contributor issue gate from closing a pull request that a repository maintainer has reopened. The same permission check also prevents maintainer-authored PRs from being treated as first-time contributions, and avoids sending maintainers the first-merged-PR welcome message.

## Why the earlier checks were insufficient

The workflows previously relied on `author_association` from the pull-request event. That value can be stale or be `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`/`NONE` on `pull_request_target`, even when the PR author now has repository access. It also describes the PR author, not the person who reopened the PR. Consequently, a maintainer reopening an external contribution could have it immediately closed again by the issue gate.

## What changed

- Query GitHub collaborator permissions for the PR author before applying first-time-contributor behavior.
- On `reopened`, query the event actor as well; users with admin, maintain, push, or write access bypass the issue gate.
- Apply the same author-permission check to the first-merged-PR welcome workflow.
- Add regression coverage for repository roles, read-only contributors, and a maintainer reopening another author's PR.

## Commit

- `d3d287932` — adds permission-aware maintainer safeguards to first-contributor workflows and their regression tests.

## Verification

- [x] `uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/ci/test_ftc_require_issue.py -q`
- [x] `uv run ruff check --isolated lib/crewai/tests/ci/test_ftc_require_issue.py`
- [x] `uv run ruff format --check --isolated lib/crewai/tests/ci/test_ftc_require_issue.py`
- [x] `git diff --check`

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Changes are limited to GitHub Actions first-contributor workflows and CI regression tests, with no application runtime impact.
> 
> **Overview**
> First-time-contributor automation no longer trusts **`author_association` alone**, which can be stale on `pull_request_target`. Both workflows now **query collaborator permissions** before treating someone as a first-timer.
> 
> The **issue gate** (`ftc-require-issue`) skips closing/labeling when the PR author has repo write access (`admin`, `maintain`, `push`, or `write`), and on **`reopened`** events it also skips when the **actor** who reopened has that access—so a maintainer reopening an external PR is not immediately closed again. The **first-merged welcome** job uses the same idea for the author and **does not post** the welcome comment if they have **admin** or **write** permission.
> 
> Regression tests extend the embedded workflow harness to mock permission lookups and cover maintainer bypass, read-only contributors still being gated, and maintainer reopen bypass.
>

title: fix(flow): snapshot class dict while collecting flow methods
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8697

## Summary

`_iter_flow_methods` walks `flow_class.__dict__` while it collects methods. `Flow.flow_definition` then stores `_flow_definition` on that class. When two threads build the same class for the first time, one can insert that key while the other is still iterating the dict, which raises `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`.

The loop now iterates a snapshot of the keys, so that insert no longer invalidates the iterator.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

`tests/test_flow_definition.py::test_build_flow_definition_survives_class_dict_insert` inserts `_flow_definition` on the first method check. That is the same class-dict write `Flow.flow_definition` performs.

- Before this change the test fails with `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration` in `_iter_flow_methods`.
- After this change the same test passes, and `tests/test_flow_definition.py` reports 69 passed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on `lib/crewai/src/crewai/flow/dsl/_utils.py`.

## Additional context

None

---

> **Low Risk**
> Narrow concurrency fix in flow definition introspection; behavior is unchanged except avoiding the race-time crash.
> 
> **Overview**

title: fix(cli): keep deeply nested json as text in the run tui on python 3.12
body:
On Python 3.12 the run TUI raised `RecursionError` from its render tick when streamed output contained deeply nested JSON. 3.12's C decoder accepts nesting its pure-Python `indent` encoder cannot walk (3.10/3.11 refuse it on load, 3.13 encodes `indent` in C), and `_try_parse_structured` returned the `json.loads` result unchecked. It now checks that result with the same `dumps` call the `ast` fallback already uses, so such text is shown as it was.

- Scope: `_try_parse_structured` in `lib/cli/src/crewai_cli/crew_run_tui.py`; valid JSON is still pretty-printed.
- Found by #8603, which runs the `lib/cli` suite in CI for the first time: `test_format_json_in_text_survives_deep_nesting` fails on 3.12 there, and only there. #8603 is red until this merges.
- Tests: a new test reproduces the decoder/encoder mismatch on every version and fails without the fix; on 3.12 the existing deep-nesting test fails before and passes after (`test_crew_run_tui.py`, 116 passed).
- Checked: the cli/core/files suites have no other version-specific failure on 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 or 3.13.
- Out: no change to how `_format_json_in_text` finds candidates; no docs change.

title: feat(agent): scaffold and load standalone agent projects
body:
Add experimental standalone Agent projects with YAML, JSON or Python definitions. `crewai create agent support_agent` scaffolds YAML by default; `--format json` and `--format python` choose the other layouts. `crewai run` opens the shared conversational TUI through `Agent.chat(tui=True)`; `crewai run --inputs '{"messages":"Hello"}'` performs an independent kickoff.

**SDK prerequisite #9017 is merged.** This PR now targets `main` and contains only the five standalone Agent scaffold/loader/CLI commits. Rebased onto `7abc196a1`; the five patches are unchanged.

- Resolve `[tool.crewai] type = "agent"` and an explicit definition/entrypoint. Configuration projects need no `main.py` or `src/` package.
- Scaffold a general-purpose Agent using `gpt-6.1-sol`, reference tools and an empty skills directory. Generated projects contain no local checkout overrides or manual test runners.
- Before the first chat turn or kickoff, ask for the API key the loaded Agent's model needs (or print the line to add without a terminal), reusing the CLI's key prompt. Providers build clients lazily, so a missing key otherwise fails only on the first turn.
- Keep Agent execution in `run_agent.py`, using the selected project's environment and the shared public SDK chat API. Preserve crew/flow dispatch and current CLI API-key preflight behavior.
- Validate declarative configuration structurally without constructing Agents or executing custom/imported/serialized tools, callbacks or Agent subclasses. Report unresolved tool references. Explicit Python projects retain their Python import behavior.
- Retain Agent project-creation and CLI run-attempt telemetry, with closed event names and opt-outs; document these counts in all four locales.
- Document the experimental contract, local/source installation, project layouts, tools, inputs and deployment limits in English, Arabic, Korean and Brazilian Portuguese.

The merged SDK provides Agent conversation sessions through the public `Agent.chat()` API. Applications must authorize persisted session access; use separate Agents for independent concurrent conversations.

Validation (2026-11-06): **530 CLI tests** (`test_create_agent`, `test_run_agent`, `deploy/test_agent_import_security`, `test_run_crew`, `test_run_usage`, `test_create_unified`, `test_cli`, `test_api_keys`), **42 project-loader tests** and **20 core entrypoint tests** pass. Ruff, ruff-format and mypy pass. No live-model or hosted Enterprise E2E run was performed.

Experimental/unreleased: generated projects require matching CLI/core/SDK preview builds until release. Managed deployment support is in https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI-enterprise/pull/1398; production container/CDO deployment, managed API token streaming and multi-host recovery require separate verification. Manual projects remain untracked.

SDK prerequisite: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/9017
Enterprise integration: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI-enterprise/pull/1398
Linear: https://linear.app/crewai/issue/OSS-236/expose-durable-conversational-endpoints-for-standalone-agents

---

> **High Risk**
> Changes introduce a new experimental project type across CLI create/run/deploy validation and API-key handling, which is a broad surface area for regressions or security issues if misconfigured.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces experimental **standalone Agent projects** end to end: the CLI can now `crewai create agent …` with YAML/JSON/Python scaffolds, new templates, and telemetry/docs updates that call out the preview. The run path adds `run_agent` integration so `crewai run` dispatches agent projects—handling conversational TUI sessions, strict `messages` JSON inputs, dependency bootstrapping, and smarter API-key prompts with LLM endpoint context—plus deploy validation/import checks that avoid executing untrusted Python while still loading Python projects safely. Extensive CLI tests cover creation, running, API-key prompting, and validation edge cases.

title: chore(deps): bump the security-updates group across 1 directory with 2 updates
body:
Bumps the security-updates group with 2 updates in the / directory: [nltk](https://github.com/nltk/nltk) and [virtualenv](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv). Updates `nltk` from 3.10.3 to 3.10.4
Release notes

Sourced from nltk's releases.

v3.10.4

Version 3.10.4 2026-10-20

This release routes every file path, archive, download, URL fetch and external program through one sandbox that keeps reads and writes inside the trusted data directories, refuses path traversal, symlink escapes and decompression bombs, blocks requests to internal network addresses, and runs Java and other third-party tools only from trusted absolute locations with validated options and input. Pickled models now load through a restricted unpickler, XML and JSON parsing are hardened, and regular expressions, recursion and slow algorithms in the tokenizers, parsers, stemmers and corpus readers are bounded against denial-of-service input. Text that NLTK writes to the terminal, to CSV files, to the WordNet browser and to third-party tool input is sanitized against injection.

Security changes you may notice

Every refusal below raises with a message that starts with "Security Violation" and names the check, so a failure is easy to search for (PR #3877).

  • Data directories (nltk.pathsec, nltk.data): corpora, models and every other resource are read and written only inside the directories listed in nltk.data.path. A path that leaves a data root, a symlink that points out of one, and a NUL byte or encoded traversal in a resource name are refused. A data root, or a directory on the way to a resource, that another account can write to is skipped with a warning naming the directory and the remedy. Keep private data in a private directory and add it to nltk.data.path; /tmp is not a data root. Model save and load methods (perceptron, maxent, named-entity chunker, Weka, crf, hunpos, Stanford) accept destinations inside a data root only (PR #3797, #3753, #3850, #3761, #3755, #3759, #3760, #3763, #3806, #3807, #3808, #3809, #3813, #3814, #3815, #3848, #3851, #3852, #3853, #3863, #3871, #3888, #3945, #3961, #3969, #3981)
  • Downloader: downloaded package archives stay private to the installing account (0600). An install another account must read is extracted: a download made as root or outside the installing account's home extracts on its own, and nltk.download(..., extract=True) / python -m nltk.downloader --extract (or --no-extract) decide explicitly. This also unpacks the packages the index leaves zipped (wordnet, omw-1.4 ...); the extracted files are readable by every account and are found before the archive. find() names an archive it cannot read and says how to extract it instead of reporting it "not found". The downloader installs only into directories no other account can write to, treats an archive another account owns or can write to as stale and downloads it afresh, extracts only from an archive no other account could have changed since its checksum was verified, bounds the size of what it fetches, and refuses index entries and archive members that would write outside the package directory (PR #3929, #3804, #3850, #3778)
  • Pickles: nltk.data.load(..., format="pickle") reconstructs plain data only; a pickle that names any class or function is refused. Model loaders that need classes use an explicit allowlist of audited globals, so a gadget such as os.system can never be reconstructed from a model file. chat80 shelve values load the same way (PR #3794, #3754, #3757, #3802, #3817, #3823, #3824)
  • XML, JSON and YAML: nltk.xmlsec refuses any document that declares an entity or references an external one (billion-laughs, external-entity and DTD attacks) and bounds the tree depth, and every corpus XML view, the downloader index, Toolbox and internals parse through it. JSON resources load with a depth and size bound; YAML (the markdown corpus front matter and nltk.data.load(..., format="yaml")) loads through a bounded safe loader. Oversized or too deeply nested input raises ValueError naming the limit (PR #3754, #3805, #3828, #3933, #3972, #3974)
  • Regular expressions (nltk.redos): every regular expression NLTK compiles, including one you pass to RegexpTokenizer, RegexpStemmer, RegexpParser, re_show, TokenSearcher.findall, tgrep, nltk.help tag-set lookups and the concordance and nemo GUIs, now goes through nltk.redos on the regex engine. A pattern longer than 100,000 characters, nested more than 100 deep, with more than 1,000 capturing groups or an excessive repetition product is refused with nltk.redos.error, a subclass of re.error; a match that runs longer than nltk.redos.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT (5 seconds) raises TimeoutError instead of hanging. Patterns keep re syntax; match objects are the regex engine's (PR #3825, #3829, #3830, #3831, #3832, #3833, #3834, #3835, #3836, #3837, #3838, #3839, #3840, #3841, #3842, #3843, #3844, #3845, #3846, #3796, #3801, #3906, #3907, #3908, #3910)
  • Regular expressions made linear: the leading-run and re-anchoring patterns that a timeout cannot catch were rewritten or bounded in the word, Treebank, blankline, TextTiling, toktok and syllable tokenizers, the readline of corpus streams, the CoNLL SRL, TIMIT, senseval, pl196x, NKJP, Alpino, YCOE, IEER, ACE, VerbNet, reviews and Lin readers, relextract, the valuation parser, the CCG lexicon parser, dependency grammars and chomsky_normal_form, each verified on the real corpus (PR #3947, #3934, #3932, #3938, #3935, #3933, #3869, #3944, #3911, #3909, #3953, #3895)
  • Size, depth and time bounds: trees deeper than nltk.tree.MAX_TREE_DEPTH (500), WordNet and other relation walks deeper than nltk.util.MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH (500), tgrep deeper than 50, Toolbox deeper than 500, dependency graphs deeper than 200, are refused with ValueError naming the limit rather than exhausting the stack, and the stemmers, distance metrics, skipgrams, parsers and grammar transforms run in linear or bounded time with identical output for legitimate input. chart_parse stops after nltk.parse.chart.DEFAULT_MAX_TIME (5 seconds of wall-clock, needed only for feature grammars; max_time=None disables it). Tree.repr no longer recurses, so a deep accepted tree prints (PR #3827, #3885, #3895, #3767, #3784, #3917, #3958, #3960, #3977)
  • External tools and Java: a tool binary is resolved from an absolute path or a trusted search path only, never from the current directory; the binary, its directory and the model and data files handed to it must not be writable by another account (symlinked and multi-call executables such as a packaged Graphviz dot are supported). java() accepts a main class as the first argument only (no -jar, @​argfile or .java source file), validates its options against an allowlist, and loads jars only from a data root unless NLTK_ALLOW_UNSAFE_JARS=1 opts out with a warning. CoreNLP server options are allowlisted. Stanford, Malt, Senna, hunpos, Prover9, megam, TADM, Weka and crf wrappers validate their paths and the text they pipe to the tool against line and argument injection (PR #3772, #3771, #3975, #3743, #3782, #3788, #3768, #3798, #3887, #3858, #3950, #3951, #3812, #3816, #3868, #3894, #3941, #3850, #3925)
  • Network: the downloader, nltk.data.load of a URL and the CHILDES reader fetch through pathsec.urlopen, which refuses addresses that are not globally routable (loopback, private, link-local and multicast, including tunnelled and obfuscated forms), pins the validated address for the connection, allows file:// with a local authority only, and refuses a proxied fetch unless NLTK_ALLOW_PROXIED_URLOPEN=1 (or nltk.pathsec.ALLOW_PROXIED_FETCH = True) asserts the proxy is trusted. The CoreNLP client talks to its local server with requests and is not affected (PR #3847, #3810, #3750, #3850)
  • Terminal, CSV, DOT and HTML output: every print in the library goes through nltk.termsec.safe_print, which renders control characters, escape sequences and unbalanced bidi overrides from corpus text as visible \xNN escapes instead of letting them reach the terminal. The CSV files the twitter and sentiment helpers write neutralise formula-leading and control-sequence cells, AlignedSent DOT labels are escaped, the WordNet browser escapes corpus text, and nltk.data.load's verbose output no longer prints the full resource URL (PR #3914, #3915, #3937, #3946, #3931, #3930, #3856, #3902)
  • Corpus stores and encodings: the PanLex Lite and chat80 sqlite stores open read-only on a pinned descriptor with their schema screened and a statement step budget, chat80 shelves are read by a key manifest, Toolbox SFM markers are sanitised, and a resource encoding that is not a text codec (bz2_codec and friends) is refused (PR #3961, #3964, #3959, #3888, #3800, #3962)
  • Package contents: the wheel no longer ships nltk.test.unit (the attack harnesses, advisory probes and their fixtures), so pip install nltk is about half the size and import nltk.test.unit works from a source checkout or the sdist only. The doctests under nltk.test still ship (PR #3954)

Security test and CI infrastructure

  • Attack and regression harnesses, advisory probes, the sandbox conftest fixtures, the pre-commit guards (no unsandboxed open, every regex through redos, every pickle through picklesec, every print through safe_print), load-invariant CPU-time timing rules, CI matrix and runner fixes, pinned third-party downloads, and the AUTHORS update (PR #3744, #3749, #3762, #3764, #3770, #3776, #3791, #3795, #3803, #3818, #3820, #3821, #3822, #3849, #3855, #3860, #3861, #3862, #3864, #3865, #3866, #3876, #3884, #3899, #3904, #3905, #3912, #3917, #3924, #3926, #3927, #3939, #3940, #3943, #3948, #3949, #3963, #3968, #3971, #3976, #3982, #3983, #3984, #3985)

Other changes

  • Added RTL language syntactic tree visualization support (PR #3472)
  • Fix #3394: Ensure punkt_tab is downloaded when punkt is requested (PR #3505)
  • Show README.md as the PyPI long description (PR #3746)
  • Add stopwords.words("english-extended") (PR #3747)
  • Krippendorff's alpha: treat placeholder labels as missing data (#2865, #2732) (PR #3752)
  • Fix shared defaults in chat80 Concept (PR #3773)
  • Fix Java wrappers decoding str output from java() (universal_newlines) (PR #3777)
  • Prevent IndexError in Hungarian stemmer on empty string (PR #3785)
  • Isolate MTE tag filters per view (PR #3792)
  • Fix newline in ellipsis tokens in TweetTokenizer (PR #3819)
  • Isolate default WordNet reference relations (PR #3872)
  • Fix resolution paths that cancel distinct literals (PR #3878)
  • Fix UTF-8 text preprocessing in NKJP corpus reader (PR #3879)
  • Remove shadowed FeatStruct._walk stub and preserve its docstring (PR #3893)
  • Count all increasing pairs in RIBES kendall_tau (PR #3900)
  • Fix the TweetTokenizer ZWJ emoji pattern capturing adjacent whitespace (PR #3913)
  • Surface the CoreNLP server's reason for a non-2xx answer (PR #3942)
  • Omit unaligned (NULL target) pairs from Alignment strings, so IBM model output prints (PR #3967)
  • Fix DependencyGraph cycle detection, which returned False on every parsed graph (PR #3978)
  • Show, range and draw an alignment with an unaligned pair on every surface (PR #3987)

Thanks to the following contributors to 3.10.4: Zhewen Tan, Yanhaoxi, Yazan Balawneh (Cystack.ps),

Patterns keep re syntax; match objects are the regex engine's (PR #3825, #3829, #3830, #3831, #3832, #3833, #3834, #3835, #3836, #3837, #3838, #3839, #3840, #3841, #3842, #3843, #3844, #3845, #3846, #3796, #3801, #3906, #3907, #3908, #3910)
  • Regular expressions made linear: the leading-run and re-anchoring patterns that a timeout cannot catch were rewritten or bounded in the word, Treebank, blankline, TextTiling, toktok and syllable tokenizers, the readline of corpus streams, the CoNLL SRL, TIMIT, senseval, pl196x, NKJP, Alpino, YCOE, IEER, ACE, VerbNet, reviews and Lin readers, relextract, the valuation parser, the CCG lexicon parser, dependency grammars and chomsky_normal_form, each verified on the real corpus (PR #3947, #3934, #3932, #3938, #3935, #3933, #3869, #3944, #3911, #3909, #3953, #3895)
  • Size, depth and time bounds: trees deeper than nltk.tree.MAX_TREE_DEPTH (500), WordNet and other relation walks deeper than nltk.util.MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH (500), tgrep deeper than 50, Toolbox deeper than 500, dependency graphs deeper than 200, are refused with ValueError naming the limit rather than exhausting the stack, and the stemmers, distance metrics, skipgrams, parsers and grammar transforms run in linear or bounded time with identical output for legitimate input. chart_parse stops after nltk.parse.chart.DEFAULT_MAX_TIME (5 seconds of wall-clock, needed only for feature grammars; max_time=None disables it). Tree.repr no longer recurses, so a deep accepted tree prints (PR #3827, #3885, #3895, #3767, #3784, #3917, #3958, #3960, #3977)
  • External tools and Java: a tool binary is resolved from an absolute path or a trusted search path only, never from the current directory; the binary, its directory and the model and data files handed to it must not be writable by another account (symlinked and multi-call executables such as a packaged Graphviz dot are supported). java() accepts a main class as the first argument only (no -jar, @​argfile or .java source file), validates its options against an allowlist, and loads jars only from a data root unless NLTK_ALLOW_UNSAFE_JARS=1 opts out with a warning. CoreNLP server options are allowlisted. Stanford, Malt, Senna, hunpos, Prover9, megam, TADM, Weka and crf wrappers validate their paths and the text they pipe to the tool against line and argument injection (PR #3772, #3771, #3975, #3743, #3782, #3788, #3768, #3798, #3887, #3858, #3950, #3951, #3812, #3816, #3868, #3894, #3941, #3850, #3925)
  • Network: the downloader, nltk.data.load of a URL and the CHILDES reader fetch through pathsec.urlopen, which refuses addresses that are not globally routable (loopback, private, link-local and multicast, including tunnelled and obfuscated forms), pins the validated address for the connection, allows file:// with a local authority only, and refuses a proxied fetch unless NLTK_ALLOW_PROXIED_URLOPEN=1 (or nltk.pathsec.ALLOW_PROXIED_FETCH = True) asserts the proxy is trusted. The CoreNLP client talks to its local server with requests and is not affected (PR #3847, #3810, #3750, #3850)
  • Terminal, CSV, DOT and HTML output: every print in the library goes through nltk.termsec.safe_print, which renders control characters, escape sequences and unbalanced bidi overrides from corpus text as visible \xNN escapes instead of letting them reach the terminal. The CSV files the twitter and sentiment helpers write neutralise formula-leading and control-sequence cells, AlignedSent DOT labels are escaped, the WordNet browser escapes corpus text, and nltk.data.load's verbose output no longer prints the full resource URL (PR #3914, #3915, #3937, #3946, #3931, #3930, #3856, #3902)
  • Corpus stores and encodings: the PanLex Lite and chat80 sqlite stores open read-only on a pinned descriptor with their schema screened and a statement step budget, chat80 shelves are read by a key manifest, Toolbox SFM markers are sanitised, and a resource encoding that is not a text codec (bz2_codec and friends) is refused (PR #3961, #3964, #3959, #3888, #3800, #3962)
  • Package contents: the wheel no longer ships nltk.test.unit (the attack harnesses, advisory probes and their fixtures), so pip install nltk is about half the size and import nltk.test.unit works from a source checkout or the sdist only. The doctests under nltk.test still ship (PR #3954)

title: fix(llm): report token usage for LiteLLM tool-call and structured-output calls
body:
🤖 [agent on alexmarchenko-crewai's behalf]

## Related issue

None. This was reported internally: traces from deployed flows showed LLM requests but 0 tokens and $0 cost for models routed through LiteLLM.

## Summary

On the LiteLLM fallback path (for example `litellm_proxy/...`, or any model with `is_litellm=True`), two kinds of call never report token usage. Tracing still counts them as requests, but the tokens and cost come out as zero.

- **Native tool-call turns.** These are calls with no `available_functions`, which is how the agent executor makes them. They returned the tool calls without emitting `LLMCallCompletedEvent`. This happened in all four handlers: sync and async, streaming and non-streaming.
- **Structured output through Instructor** (`response_model`). The completion event was emitted with `usage=None`, and the tokens were never tracked.

The native OpenAI and Azure providers already emit a `tool_call` completion with usage before returning tool calls. This change makes the LiteLLM path do the same:

- Tool-call turns emit `LLMCallCompletedEvent(call_type=TOOL_CALL)` with usage, finish reason and response id.
- `InternalInstructor.to_pydantic_with_completion()` returns the raw completion through Instructor's `create_with_completion`. Instructor sums its retries into that completion's usage. `LLM` reports that usage on the event and tracks it. `to_pydantic()` behaves the same as before.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

Tests:

- **New:** `tests/test_llm_litellm_usage_events.py` has 5 tests, one for each fixed path: sync, async, streaming and async-streaming tool calls, plus structured output. All 5 fail on `main` and pass with this change.
- **Updated:** `test_handle_streaming_tool_calls_no_available_functions` used to assert zero `tool_call` completion events, which pinned the old behavior. Two tests faked Instructor without `create_with_completion`, and their fakes now include it.
- **Full suite:** `lib/crewai` passes, 6354 passed and 0 failed. `ruff check`, `ruff format` and `mypy` are clean on the changed files.

End-to-end check: three tiny crews running `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5` with `is_litellm=True`, counting completion events and their usage on the event bus.

| Scenario | Before (1.15.29) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Plain task | usage present | usage present |
| Task with `output_pydantic` | `usage=None` | usage present (1,178 tokens) |
| Agent with a tool | tool-call turn emits no completion event | `tool_call` completion with usage (739 tokens) |

The same scenarios on the native Anthropic client already reported usage for every call.

## Additional context

The streaming structured-output branch still reports the stream's usage rather than the follow-up Instructor call's usage. That path isn't affected by the bug above, so it's left out of this PR to keep the diff small.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Observability and event emission only; no change to model invocation semantics or tool execution behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **LiteLLM** observability so tool-only turns and Instructor structured output report real token usage on `LLMCallCompletedEvent`, matching native providers.
> 
> When the model returns **tool calls** with no `available_functions` (agent executor path), sync/async and streaming handlers now emit **`TOOL_CALL`** completions with usage, finish reason, and response id before returning. **Structured output** (`response_model`) switches to `InternalInstructor.to_pydantic_with_completion()` so usage from Instructor retries is tracked and attached to the **`LLM_CALL`** event via new `_completion_usage` helper.
> 
> Regression tests in `test_llm_litellm_usage_events.py` cover all five fixed paths.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 80b30d3a38bcd9a272d2e41312658178792a3d93. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: fix(llm): stop sending 'stop' to GPT-6 and newer models
body:
Summary

Azure and OpenAI calls to GPT-6 and newer models failed every time with a 400 error: `Unsupported parameter: 'stop' is not supported with this model`. Both providers only skipped stop for model names containing "gpt-5", so gpt-6-luna and similar models still got it.

The check now matches GPT-5 and every newer major version (gpt-[5-9] with no digit after it). Azure's gpt-35-turbo (GPT-3.5) doesn't match, so it still gets stop. Stop words are still applied on the client side, as before.

Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow change to model-name detection for omitting the `stop` request field; fixes failures on newer models and adds regression tests for gpt-35 false positives.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **400 errors** on GPT-6 and newer OpenAI/Azure models (`Unsupported parameter: 'stop'`) by broadening when CrewAI treats a model as **not supporting API stop sequences**.
> 
> **Azure** and **OpenAI** `supports_stop_words()` no longer use a literal `"gpt-5"` substring check. They now use `re.search(r"gpt-[5-9](?!\d)", …)` so GPT-5 through GPT-9 major families are excluded from sending `stop`, while names like Azure **`gpt-35-turbo`** (GPT-3.5) still support stops. When the API rejects stops, behavior is unchanged: **`stop` is omitted from the request** and stop sequences are still applied **client-side** via `_apply_stop_words`.
> 
> Tests cover **`gpt-35-turbo` / `gpt-3.5-turbo`**, newer variants (**`gpt-5.4-nano`**, **`gpt-6`**, **`gpt-6-luna`**), and existing GPT-5/o-series expectations.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 18645e31ec1817e82aa098e8e3f4b53cb4079a4c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: feat(rag): make chromadb optional
body:
## Summary

Make ChromaDB an opt-in RAG dependency so standard CrewAI installations do not install or import it unless users explicitly choose it.

## Commits

- `feat(rag): make chromadb an optional dependency` — moves ChromaDB to the `crewai[chromadb]` extra.
- `refactor(embeddings): lazy load provider exports` — prevents embedding package exports from importing ChromaDB during base imports.

title: fix: emit LLMGuardrailCompletedEvent for a malformed guardrail result
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8647

## Summary

Follow-up to #8403. `process_guardrail` converts the guardrail's return value with `GuardrailResult.from_tuple`
after the `try` block that #8403 added, so a guardrail returning the wrong shape (for example `(False, 42)` or a
three-item tuple) raised without a `LLMGuardrailCompletedEvent`. The started scope stayed on the event stack:
`Agent.kickoff` and `Crew.kickoff` logged event pairing mismatches, and later events in the same context got the
wrong parent.

The conversion now runs inside the `try`, so these errors take the same terminal path as a guardrail that raises.
The caller still gets the same exception, and a well-formed result is handled exactly as before. All four callers
(`Agent`, `LiteAgent`, and the sync and async `Task` paths) go through `process_guardrail`, so this one change
covers them.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

Added to `test_guardrail_events_on_exception.py`, next to the #8403 tests:
- `test_a_malformed_guardrail_result_still_reports_the_validation_it_started` (`non-string-error`, `three-tuple`):
  both fail on `main` with `assert 0 == 1` (no completed event) and pass with the fix.
- `test_a_valid_guardrail_result_reports_one_completed_event`: control, a well-formed `(False, "too short")` still
  emits exactly one completed event. Passes on `main` and with the fix.

The issue repro through `Agent.kickoff()` and `Crew.kickoff()` now emits both events, leaves the scope stack empty,
and logs no pairing mismatch.

- `lib/crewai/tests/`: 6349 passed, 44 skipped (Python 3.13)
- guardrail tests also pass on Python 3.10
- `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy` clean

## Additional context

None

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Small control-flow change in event emission only; behavior for valid guardrails and raised errors stays the same.
> 
> **Overview**

>

title: fix(files): run the provider listing off the loop in acleanup_provider_files
body:
## Summary

`acleanup_provider_files(..., delete_all_from_provider=True)` called `uploader.list_files()` — the sync method that hits the provider's HTTP API — directly on the event loop. Deletes were already off-loop (`adelete` under a semaphore + `gather`), but the listing step froze every other coroutine for the duration of the provider listing. The listing now runs via `asyncio.to_thread`, a one-line fix with no uploader API change (`alist_files` does not exist on the uploaders).

Closes #8641

## Change

- `lib/crewai-files/src/crewai_files/cache/cleanup.py`: `files = await asyncio.to_thread(uploader.list_files)` in the `delete_all_from_provider` branch of `acleanup_provider_files` (the sync `cleanup_provider_files` twin is unchanged).
- `lib/crewai-files/tests/test_acleanup_listing_nonblocking.py`: regression test with a stub uploader whose `list_files` sleeps 0.5 s; a ticker coroutine must keep ticking while the listing runs. Fails on `main` (ticker frozen), passes with the fix.

## Proof

- Red on `main`: `AssertionError: event loop was blocked during listing: 3 ticks` (expected ≥ 6).
- Green with the fix: `1 passed`; full `lib/crewai-files` suite: `180 passed, 4 skipped`.

## Risk

Low: behavior is identical except the listing executes in a worker thread; result ordering and error handling (`except Exception` path) are unchanged.

title: Add Trustabl agent reliability check to CI
body:
Hi! We came across crewAIInc/crewAI and like that it focuses on building an open-source framework for creating AI agents.

We ran [Trustabl](https://trustabl.ai), an open-source agent reliability scanner, on the repo and it flagged a few things that may be worth a look:

- **CrewAI agent enables built-in code execution** (`lib/crewai/tests/test_crew.py`): This Agent sets allow_code_execution=True, which makes CrewAI auto-inject a CodeInterpreterTool into the agent's tool set.

This PR adds a small GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/trustabl.yml`) so these checks run automatically:

- Runs on pushes to the default branch, on pull requests, and on demand
- Advisory only: the job uses `continue-on-error`, so it never fails your CI
- No secrets needed; findings show up in the repo's code scanning results
- Actions are pinned to commit SHAs, with read-only contents access

Some findings may be intentional. Happy to adjust the workflow, or to close this if it's not useful.

Add Trustabl to your CI · [trustabl/trustabl-action](https://github.com/trustabl/trustabl-action) · https://trustabl.ai

title: fix(tools): name the renamed integration token when it is missing
body:
After #7990, CrewAI reads the Enterprise Action Auth Token only from `CREWAI_ENTERPRISE_ACTION_AUTH_TOKEN`. Projects that still set `CREWAI_PLATFORM_INTEGRATION_TOKEN` got "No Enterprise Action Auth Token found", which reads as if no token was configured. An agent with `apps` then warned only that they "resolved to no tools", because the real error was logged at verbose level. Now the error says the old variable is set and needs renaming, and the agent's warning ends with `Cause: <the error>`.

- Covers the integration-token lookup in `crewai_tools` (used for action discovery and execution) and the warning from `Agent.get_platform_tools`.
- No compatibility fallback: the old variable is still not read, as #7990 intended. The hint has a removal note for 2.0.
- Tests: the old-variable-only case raises the rename message, both-set still uses the new token, and the warning includes the cause only when resolution raised. The new failure-path tests fail on main.
- Docs: none changed. The messages are self-explanatory.
- Out: `crewai.context.get_platform_integration_token` (MCP, skills, tracing grants) still returns `None` silently when only the old variable is set. That needs a follow-up ticket.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

> **Low Risk**
> User-facing error and warning text only; auth still reads CREWAI_ENTERPRISE_ACTION_AUTH_TOKEN with no legacy fallback.

> Improves diagnostics after the enterprise auth env var rename (#7990): users who still set **`CREWAI_PLATFORM_INTEGRATION_TOKEN`** alone no longer see a generic “token missing” error.
> 
> **`get_platform_integration_token`** in crewai-tools now raises a **`ValueError`** that names the old variable and instructs renaming it to **`CREWAI_ENTERPRISE_ACTION_AUTH_TOKEN`** (same value; no read of the legacy name). **`Agent.get_platform_tools`** appends **`Cause: <exception>`** to the existing **`UserWarning`** when platform tool resolution fails, so rename/API errors surface without verbose logging.

body:
## Related issue

None.

## Summary

Long conversational histories currently fail at the model context limit without using CrewAI's shared compaction. Reuse the BaseLLM summarizer for built-in converse, history-only, and router calls, with proactive compaction and one recovery attempt after a provider context-limit error.

Preserve the public transcript, system prompt, and latest user message. Keep internal summary text out of streamed replies. Enable handling by default through `respect_context_window`, with an opt-out supported in Python and declarative flows. Document the behavior in English, Arabic, Korean, and Brazilian Portuguese.

## Verification

- [x] Added behavioral tests for compaction, normal and streaming recovery, transcript and latest-message preservation, router and history handling, bounded retries, failures, opt-out, and declaration round-tripping.
- [x] 555 focused tests passed across conversational flows, flow definitions, shared agent utilities, and context compaction.
- [x] Ruff, formatting, and mypy passed, including repository commit hooks.
- [x] Real OpenAI calls verified proactive compaction and recovery from actual 140,065-token HTTP 400 errors against a 128,000-token window in normal and streaming turns. Preflight was bypassed only in recovery probes to exercise the provider-error path; counting, summaries, and completions called the real provider.
- [x] Two consecutive real compactions on the same LLM and Flow preserved the launch date and answered the latest question directly.

## Additional context

Compaction changes the model request; `state.messages` remains intact for display and persistence, so later turns may summarize again. Call-only custom LLM objects, legacy intent pre-classification, and custom route handlers retain their existing context handling. Local probe scripts and logs are excluded from this PR.

title: fix(security): patch deserialization, SQL injection, and path traversal vulnerabilities [SECT-601]
body:
## Security Patch — SR-2026-0127 / GHSA-wp6h-6xxh-g8fp

Fixes three security vulnerabilities:

### 1. Deserialization bypass in tool restoration (`base_tool.py`)

`_resolve_tool_dict()` used `importlib.import_module()` on attacker-controlled dotted paths from serialized checkpoint data without checking the `_trusted_deserialize()` guard. A malicious checkpoint could import and resolve arbitrary Python objects (e.g., `os.system`).

Additionally, `cache_function` strings were pre-resolved via `_resolve_dotted_path()` explicitly to bypass `SerializableCallable's` env-var guard.

**Fix:** Unregistered tool types now require `CREWAI_DESERIALIZE_CALLBACKS=1`. The `cache_function` pre-resolution block has been removed entirely — `SerializableCallable's` validator handles it with its own `_trusted_deserialize()` check.

### 2. NL2SQL read-only mode bypass via SQL comment injection (`nl2sql_tool.py`)

SQL comments (`--` and `/* */`) could hide write commands from the read-only validator:
- `/* SELECT */ DELETE FROM users` — block comment before write command
- `WITH d AS (/* read */ DELETE FROM users) SELECT 1` — block comment inside CTE body
- `-- comment\nDELETE FROM users` — line comment before write command

The `_extract_command()`, `_detect_writable_cte()`, and `_extract_main_query_after_cte()` functions only checked the first token without stripping comments first.

**Fix:** Added `_strip_sql_comments()` helper that removes both `--` line comments and `/* */` block comments while preserving string literals. Applied to all three extraction points.

### 3. Tar extraction TOCTOU race condition (`skills/main.py`)

`_safe_extractall()` validated all archive members upfront but then called `tf.extractall(dest)` which extracts everything at once. Since symlinks and files are extracted in archive order, a symlink could be extracted first and a subsequent file could follow it outside the destination directory.

**Fix:** Replaced `extractall()` with phased member-by-member extraction: directories first, then regular files, then symlinks created manually via `os.symlink()` with re-verification of targets at creation time. This eliminates the TOCTOU window entirely.

### Tests

- **Deserialization:** 3 new tests verify that `_resolve_tool_dict` blocks unregistered tool types without the env var
- **NL2SQL:** 7 new tests verify comment-based injection attempts are blocked in read-only mode
- **Tar extraction:** 2 new tests verify phased extraction ordering and symlink target verification

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes deserialization gates, SQL execution policy, and archive install paths—regressions could allow arbitrary imports, hidden writes, or path escape on older Python.
> 
> **Overview**
> Addresses three security areas: **checkpoint/tool deserialization**, **NL2SQL read-only validation**, and **skill archive extraction**.
> 
> **Tool restoration** (`base_tool.py`): Serialized `tool_type` dicts no longer import arbitrary modules unless the type is under `crewai.` / `crewai_tools.` or `CREWAI_DESERIALIZE_CALLBACKS=1`. Non-`BaseTool` targets are rejected after import. The `cache_function` pre-resolution bypass is removed; the default cache path is stripped so restore works without the opt-in. **JSON projects** eagerly resolve `tool_type` via `_resolve_tool_class` so project-defined tools register before Pydantic hydration.
> 
> **NL2SQL** (`nl2sql_tool.py`): Read-only mode **rejects any statement containing** `--`, `/*`, or (MySQL/MariaDB only) `#`, instead of parsing/stripping comments—avoiding bypasses via quoting and dialect quirks. With `allow_dml=True`, commented statements are treated as writes for commit detection.
> 
> **Tar fallback** (`_safe_extractall` in CLI skills + skill cache): On Python without `tarfile` `filter="data"`, symlink and hardlink members are **blocked entirely** (with a Python upgrade hint); only files and directories pass path checks before `extractall`. Tests cover link chains, hardlink-to-symlink cases, and traversal member names.
>

title: SECT-602: fix path traversal in output_file via template interpolation
body:
## Security Fix — GHSA-hq26-r99g-pvv4 (SR-2026-0128)

### Vulnerability

`output_file` paths are validated at model construction time via a Pydantic field validator, but `interpolate_inputs_and_add_conversation_history()` rewrites `output_file` with caller-controlled template inputs **after** validation. An attacker can craft inputs like `{"topic": "../../etc/cron.d"}` to escape the intended output directory and overwrite arbitrary files writable by the process.

### Fix (3 layers)

1. **Extract validation into `_validate_output_file_path()`** — reusable static method with an `allow_templates` flag. The field validator calls it with `allow_templates=True` (permits `{var}` syntax). Post-interpolation calls use `allow_templates=False` (rejects unresolved templates too).

2. **Re-validate after interpolation** — `interpolate_inputs_and_add_conversation_history()` now calls `_validate_output_file_path()` on the interpolated result, catching any `..`, shell chars, or expansion attempts injected via template variables.

3. **Defense-in-depth in `_save_file()`** — after resolving the path, verifies the resolved path is within `Path.cwd()`. This is the last line of defense even if upstream validation is somehow bypassed.

### Tests

- Path traversal via interpolation → `ValueError`
- Shell injection via interpolation → `ValueError`  
- Legitimate interpolation → works correctly
- `_save_file` rejects paths outside cwd → `ValueError`
- All existing `output_file` validation tests still pass

### Linear

https://linear.app/crewai/issue/SECT-602

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Closes arbitrary file write via interpolated `output_file` paths; behavior changes for previously exploitable caller inputs while tightening path rules on Windows-style roots.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Security fix (GHSA-hq26-r99g-pvv4):** `Task.output_file` was only validated at construction, so caller-controlled template inputs could inject `..`, shell metacharacters, or absolute paths after `interpolate_inputs_and_add_conversation_history()`.
> 
> Validation is centralized in **`_validate_output_file_path()`** with an `allow_templates` flag: construction keeps allowing `{var}` placeholders; post-interpolation runs with templates disallowed. After interpolation, paths are re-checked and compared via **`_path_anchor()`** (using `PureWindowsPath`) so inputs cannot increase how “rooted” the path is relative to the developer’s template. **`output_file` is updated only after validation succeeds**, so a failed run cannot leave a poisoned path for a later empty-input interpolation.
> 
> New tests cover traversal, shell injection, absolute/UNC/drive-relative escalation, smuggled `{…}` syntax, and stale-path behavior; legitimate templated writes (including absolute developer templates) remain supported.
>

title: fix(crew): drop checkpoint resume state when copying a crew
body:
Fixes #8616

## Summary

Saving a checkpoint writes the live crew's runtime state into its public checkpoint fields, and a completed run leaves `task.output` set. `Crew.copy()` carried all of that into the copy, so the copy **resumed the old run instead of executing**: `_get_execution_start_index` saw the checkpoint pointer plus the stale outputs, returned `len(tasks)`, and every task was skipped; `checkpoint_inputs` additionally shadowed the new inputs. After one checkpointed run, `kickoff_for_each()` and `test()` (both internally `self.copy()`) silently returned the checkpointed run's results with zero execution.

`Crew.copy()` now excludes `checkpoint_kickoff_event_id` / `checkpoint_inputs` / `checkpoint_train`; `Task.copy()` excludes `output` / `checkpoint_original_description` / `checkpoint_original_expected_output`.

## Verification

New `tests/test_crew_copy_resume_state.py`:
- `test_copy_drops_checkpoint_resume_pointers`, `test_copy_task_drops_previous_run_output`, `test_copy_would_execute_its_tasks_from_the_start` — all fail on main (the copy inherits the resume pointer and stale outputs; its execution start index equals `len(tasks)`, i.e. all tasks skipped) and pass with this change
- `test_plain_copy_still_carries_configuration` — control pinning that ordinary configuration (name, max_rpm, task description) still survives the copy; green on both
- Regressions: `test_checkpoint.py` + `test_crew_thread_safety.py` 76 passed; the copy/train/kickoff_for_each selection and the task suites match clean main exactly (their API-key-dependent failures are identical with and without this change)

## Risk

Low — `copy()` has three internal callers (train, kickoff_for_each, test), all of which immediately kick off a fresh run. Resume goes through `Crew.from_checkpoint`, not `copy()`, so no resume path loses state.

🤖 Generated with ZCode (AI agent) on behalf of Wilson0511

Co-Authored-By: ZCode <agent@zcode.dev>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Scoped to copy() used only for fresh runs; checkpoint restore still uses from_checkpoint(), not copy().
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a bug where **`Crew.copy()`** (used by `kickoff_for_each`, `test`, and `train`) copied **checkpoint resume state** and **finished task outputs** from a prior run. The copy then behaved like a resume: `_get_execution_start_index` treated all tasks as done and skipped execution, and stale `checkpoint_inputs` could override new kickoff inputs.
> 
> **`Crew.copy()`** now omits `checkpoint_kickoff_event_id`, `checkpoint_inputs`, and `checkpoint_train`. **`Task.copy()`** omits `output` and the checkpoint original description/expected-output fields so cloned tasks start clean.

The drain tests checked "still subscribed" after a `pilot.pause()` that could outlast the 50ms grace, then expected the unsubscribe within a fixed 80ms; `wait_for_consent` accepted the consent screen before it had any buttons, because `all()` of nothing is True. title: fix(events): stop rich live panel repainting into redirected logs
body:
Rich treats any `FORCE_COLOR` value (even `FORCE_COLOR=0`) and `TTY_COMPATIBLE=1` as a terminal without checking `isatty`. So with stdout redirected to a file, the streaming answer panel was appended on every chunk, every 100 ms auto-refresh, and every other print during the stream (one 22 KB answer wrote about 10 MB, and a sandboxed run reached 1.8 GB). Now, when stdout is not a TTY and not Jupyter, `ConsoleFormatter` does not start a `Live` at all: it keeps the latest panel and prints it once when the stream completes, fails or is paused for HITL.

- Scope: `ConsoleFormatter.handle_llm_stream_chunk`, `handle_llm_stream_completed` and `pause_live_updates`. This covers sync and async LLM calls alike because both emit `LLMStreamChunkEvent`.
- Compat: no public signature, event or telemetry value changes. On a real TTY and in Jupyter the animated panel is unchanged. A stdout replacement without `isatty` (a tee or log shim) counts as not a terminal.
- Tests: under `FORCE_COLOR=1`/`0` and `TTY_COMPATIBLE=1` on a file, the final panel and the tool-arguments panel each appear once with colour kept. That also holds while other `print`/`console.print` calls interleave with chunks, while the stream stalls, on a HITL pause, and for a file without `isatty`. A TTY still repaints per chunk. 9 of the new cases fail on main.
- Docs: none; nothing user-facing to configure.
- Out: the redirected log still holds only the last 20 lines of a streamed answer (pre-existing, same on main). No Windows or real-PTY/Jupyter run, and no handling of a nested `Live` owned by user code. Each needs a Linear ticket if wanted.

title: fix(agent): load from_repository set inside an agent's config
body:
`Agent.validate_from_repository` only read a top-level `from_repository` and ran before `config` was flattened, so an `agents.yaml` entry with `from_repository` either failed validation (role/goal/backstory missing) or, with those set locally, silently skipped the fetch and dropped the repository's tools, llm and settings. The validator now flattens a copy of `config` first, so the repository agent loads and precedence is keyword argument > config > repository.

- Scope: `Agent(config=...)`, which covers `@CrewBase` agents.yaml; JSON crews and the keyword form already fetched.
- Behaviour change: a YAML entry with `from_repository` now fetches, so it needs `crewai login` (or the hosted client hook) and raises `AuthError` when logged out, `AgentRepositoryError` when the agent is missing.
- Behaviour change: `Agent(from_repository=x, config={...})` now lets config fields beat the repository (it was the reverse), matching the "local fields override the repository" rule in `crew_definition.py`.
- Tests: config fetch, precedence, kwarg-vs-config repository, logged-out `AuthError`, 404, no fetch without the key, caller dict not mutated, and a `@CrewBase` agents.yaml end to end; 7 of these fail on main.
- No docs touched: `docs/edge` has no page that documents `from_repository`.
- Out: `json_loader`'s required-field check still reads only top-level keys, so a JSON agent with `config: {from_repository: ...}` and no role is still rejected (needs a Linear ticket); no real AMP fetch was exercised.

title: fix(cli): show amp's reason on a 401 and let the run app's deploy log in again
body:

A 401 now prints AMP's own reason (or the raw body when it is not JSON, e.g. a proxy page) plus a `crewai login` hint and raises `AuthenticationRequiredError(1)`; the run app's Deploy then offers the login once and retries once, so a stale token deploys and a 401 right after a fresh login stops with AMP's reason on screen.

- Scope: every `_validate_response` caller (deploy, tool publish, skill publish, triggers); only `run_crew._chain_deploy` catches the error, so only the run app logs in again.
- Compat: those commands now exit 1 on a 401 instead of 0, matching the missing-token case in #8590; 403/422/other non-2xx output and exit codes are unchanged, and the saved token is not cleared.
- Telemetry: no value added or renamed, but `deploy_login_prompted` now also fires after a 401; warehouse readers can tell these apart by the `http_status=401` Crew Deployment Failed span in the same project.
- Tests: 401 with a JSON reason, a non-JSON body and no reason, for deploy/tools/skills/triggers; a 403 is not a login problem; `_chain_deploy` retries once and never loops. No docs touched.
- Related: independent of #8593 (the login timeout for the same ticket); they merge cleanly in either order. It conflicts with #8590 in `lib/cli/tests/test_crew_run_tui.py` only; whichever lands second resolves it.

title: fix(memory): respect scope delimiter boundary in LanceDBStorage.delete (#8558)
body:
### Summary

Fixes #8558.

In `LanceDBStorage.delete`, scope matching previously matched records without enforcing scope hierarchy delimiter boundaries and inadvertently included `OR scope = '/'` in the query condition. This caused:
- Deleting with a scope prefix (e.g. `scope_prefix="user"`) to delete root-scope records (`scope="/"`)
- Deleting with a scope prefix to match sibling scopes (e.g. `user_analytics`, `users`, or `/user_settings`)
- Empty or whitespace `scope_prefix` strings to wipe all records.

### Changes
- Enforce scope hierarchy boundary checks: a record belongs to `scope_prefix` if and only if `record.scope == scope_prefix or record.scope.startswith(scope_prefix.rstrip("/") + "/")`
- Eliminate accidental deletion of root-scope records when deleting a sub-scope
- Safely handle empty/whitespace `scope_prefix` without wiping all records
- Added unit tests in `test_lancedb_filter_escaping.py` verifying boundary isolation, sibling scope preservation, sub-scope root preservation, and category-filtered scope boundaries.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes memory deletion semantics and fixes a bug that could wipe wrong scopes or all data on empty prefix; behavior is more correct but callers relying on the old over-broad matching may see fewer rows deleted.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Fixes incorrect scope matching in `LanceDBStorage.delete`** so deletes only touch records in the intended scope hierarchy.
> 
> Deletion no longer uses prefix `LIKE` with an extra `OR scope = '/'`, which could remove root records and scopes that only share a string prefix (e.g. `user` vs `user_analytics` or `users`). New helpers `_scope_matches_prefix` and `_scope_prefix_delete_filter` require an exact scope match or a child path after `prefix/`, with SQL escaping preserved.
> 
> **`delete` behavior updates:** empty or whitespace-only `scope_prefix` returns **0** instead of deleting everything; the `record_ids` path can also honor `scope_prefix` and `older_than`; category/metadata deletes filter rows with `_scope_matches_prefix` after scan.
> 
> Tests cover delimiter boundaries, root preservation, and category-filtered deletes.
>

Fixes #8563.

### Description
In `LanceDBStorage.delete()`:
- Previously, when \ecord_ids\ was passed alongside `older_than` or `scope_prefix` (without categories or metadata filters), \ecord_ids\ bypassed age and scope checks, deleting records regardless of their timestamp or scope.
- When `categories` or `metadata_filter` was passed alongside \ecord_ids\, the row-scanning loop ignored \ecord_ids\, causing records outside the specified ID set to be deleted.

### Changes
- Properly intersect \ecord_ids\ with `older_than`, `scope_prefix`, `categories`, and `metadata_filter` criteria so only records matching all active criteria are deleted.
- Return 0 immediately when \ecord_ids is not None and not record_ids\.
- Add unit tests in `lib/crewai/tests/memory/test_lancedb_delete.py` verifying isolated and combined filter behaviors.

title: fix(memory): handle timezone-aware older_than in storage delete (#8565)
body:
### Summary

Fixes #8565 by normalizing timezone-aware `older_than` datetime arguments to naive UTC before comparison and filtering in storage backends.

### Problem

`MemoryRecord.created_at` values are stored and evaluated as naive UTC datetimes. When callers passed a timezone-aware `older_than` datetime (e.g., `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`):
- In LanceDB, in-memory filtering against `record.created_at >= older_than` raised `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`.
- In Qdrant Edge storage, the `TypeError` occurred during shard deletion and was caught in `delete()`, resulting in 0 records being deleted silently.
- Additionally, lexicographical string comparisons against ISO-formatted strings produced unexpected results for datetimes with non-UTC timezone offsets.

### Solution

Normalize `older_than` to naive UTC in `delete()` prior to comparisons across storage backends (`LanceDBStorage` and `QdrantEdgeStorage`):

```python
if older_than is not None and older_than.tzinfo is not None:
    older_than = older_than.astimezone(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
```

### Verification

Added test suites in `lib/crewai/tests/memory/test_lancedb_delete.py` and `lib/crewai/tests/memory/test_qdrant_edge_storage.py` testing `delete()` with:
- `older_than=None`
- Offset-naive datetime
- Offset-aware datetime (UTC)
- Offset-aware datetime with positive/negative timezone offsets
All test suites passed with a 100% pass rate.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Targeted bug fix in memory retention delete paths; naive-datetime behavior is unchanged and coverage was added for timezone variants.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes memory **`delete(older_than=...)`** when callers pass timezone-aware datetimes (e.g. `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`), which previously broke or mis-deleted records because stored `created_at` values are naive UTC.
> 
> **LanceDB** and **Qdrant Edge** now convert aware `older_than` to naive UTC at the start of `delete()` (and again in Qdrant’s shard helper) via `astimezone(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)`, so in-memory comparisons and ISO string filters align with stored timestamps.
> 
> Adds parametrized tests for naive, UTC-aware, and offset-aware `older_than`, with and without category filters, in `test_lancedb_delete.py` and `test_qdrant_edge_storage.py`.

title: fix: filter categories server-side in qdrant edge search
body:
Fixes #8571

## Problem

`QdrantEdgeStorage.search()` applies `categories`/`metadata_filter` **after** the ANN fetch, with only a `limit * 3` oversample. When more than `limit * 3` non-matching records rank above the matching ones (a dense scope full of same-vicinity noise is the common case — e.g. all memories embedded from one document), the matching records are silently missed: the fetch returns only noise, the post-filter discards it, and the caller gets an empty or truncated result.

`categories` is stored as a Keyword-array payload field, so it can be matched server-side inside the query `Filter` (before the ANN limit). `metadata_filter` remains a payload post-filter (arbitrary key/value pairs are not pre-indexed) and keeps the oversample.

## Solution

In `search()` (`lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/storage/qdrant_edge_storage.py`):

- build a `FieldCondition(key="categories", match=MatchAny(any=list(categories)))` and merge it into the scope `Filter`'s `must` list when `categories` is given, so category matching happens server-side before the fetch limit;
- oversample only for `metadata_filter` (`fetch_limit = limit * 3 if metadata_filter else limit`), since categories now arrive pre-filtered;
- keep the client-side post-filters unchanged as a defense in depth (they are a no-op on server-filtered results).

## Testing

New regression tests in `lib/crewai/tests/memory/test_qdrant_search_categories.py` (offline `QdrantEdgeStorage` on a tmp path, skipped when `qdrant_edge` is not installed):

- `test_matches_below_ann_fetch_limit_are_found` — 8 near "other" records + 2 far "target" records, `search(categories=["target"], limit=2)` returns both targets (fails on `main`: empty result);
- `test_categories_limit_respected` — 5 matching records, `limit=2` returns exactly the 2 best-scored matches;
- `test_metadata_filter_with_categories_still_applies` — categories (server-side) combined with `metadata_filter` (post-filter) returns only records matching both.

Full `tests/memory/` suite: 190 passed; the only failure on this machine is the pre-existing environment-dependent `test_qdrant_edge_storage.py::test_orphaned_shard_cleanup`, which fails identically on unmodified `main`.

---

**AI assistance disclosure:** this bug report, analysis, fix and tests were prepared with the assistance of an AI agent (Claude Code) under human review. Please apply the `llm-generated` label if that is project policy for AI-assisted contributions.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Targeted retrieval bug fix with regression tests; behavior change only improves category-filtered search correctness, with no auth or persistence changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **silent misses** when `QdrantEdgeStorage.search()` is called with `categories`: category matching now happens in the Qdrant query `Filter` (via `MatchAny` on the indexed `categories` payload) **before** the ANN `limit`, instead of only as a client post-filter on an oversampled `limit * 3` fetch.
>

title: fix: enforce guardrail result/error exclusivity with model validator
body:
Fixes #8569

## Problem

`GuardrailResult.validate_result_error_exclusivity` is a `@field_validator("result", "error")`, but in pydantic v2 `info.data` only contains **previously validated** fields (declaration order: `success`, `result`, `error`). Validating `result` can never see `error`, so the `success=True` branch of the exclusivity rule is dead code:

```python
GuardrailResult(success=True, result="answer", error="boom")  # validates silently
```

The `success=False` direction only fires by accident (by the time `error` is validated, `result` is already in `values`). The documented contract — result on success, error on failure, never both — is unenforced precisely where a misbehaving guardrail would produce both.

## Solution

Replace the per-field validator with a `@model_validator(mode="after")` that checks exclusivity on the fully constructed instance (`lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/guardrail.py`). Both error messages and the falsy-value behavior (empty strings never triggered the rule before, and still don't) are preserved. `GuardrailResult.from_tuple` only ever sets one side, so no production call site is affected.

## Testing

New regression tests in `lib/crewai/tests/utilities/test_guardrail_result_exclusivity.py`:

- `test_success_true_with_both_result_and_error_rejected` — the dead branch, now enforced (fails on `main`: no error raised);
- `test_success_false_with_both_result_and_error_rejected` — was enforced only by accident, now intentional;
- `test_success_true_with_result_only_accepted` / `test_success_false_with_error_only_accepted` — the legitimate shapes still validate;
- `test_from_tuple_still_works_for_both_directions` — the production constructor is unaffected;
- `test_empty_strings_do_not_trigger_exclusivity` — falsy-value behavior preserved.

`tests/utilities/` (excluding the three file-store test modules that crash natively on Windows, unrelated to this change): 541 passed, 2 failed — both pre-existing Anthropic/VCR environment failures that reproduce identically on unmodified `main`.

---

**AI assistance disclosure:** this bug report, analysis, fix and tests were prepared with the assistance of an AI agent (Claude Code) under human review. Please apply the `llm-generated` label if that is project policy for AI-assisted contributions.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> **Low Risk**
> Validation-only change on `GuardrailResult`; the main execution path uses `from_tuple`, which already sets only one side.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Fixes invalid `GuardrailResult` shapes that previously slipped past validation.** The result/error exclusivity check moves from a Pydantic `@field_validator` on `result` and `error` to a `@model_validator(mode="after")`, because v2 `info.data` only includes fields validated earlier in declaration order—so `success=True` with both `result` and `error` could validate silently.

title: fix: guard storage listing failures in encoding flow analyze
body:
Fixes #8567

## Problem

`EncodingFlow.parallel_analyze()` calls `storage.list_scopes()` and `storage.list_categories()` unguarded. Both results only feed **suggestion lists** for the LLM field-resolution prompts, yet a transient storage read failure aborts the whole save pipeline: the listener raises, `memory.remember()` re-raises, and the memory is never persisted.

The sibling step `parallel_find_similar` already wraps every per-item `storage.search()` in `try/except` ("treating item as new"); the recall-side counterpart of this asymmetry was fixed in #8557.

## Solution

In `parallel_analyze` (`lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/encoding_flow.py`), wrap each listing in `try/except` with a warning log and a degraded fallback, mirroring the sibling step's pattern:

- `list_scopes` failure → `existing_scopes = ["/"]` (root scope only);
- `list_categories` failure → `existing_categories = []` (no category suggestions).

The two calls are guarded independently, so a scope-listing failure does not prevent category suggestions from being fetched.

## Testing

New regression tests in `lib/crewai/tests/memory/test_encoding_flow_analyze_fallback.py` (all offline, MagicMock storage + fake embedder):

- `test_scope_listing_failure_still_analyzes` — item with missing fields is still analyzed and planned for insert (fails on `main`: RuntimeError);
- `test_category_listing_failure_still_analyzes` — same for the categories listing (fails on `main`);
- `test_both_listing_failures_still_analyzes` — both listings fail, item still gets defaults and a plan (fails on `main`);
- `test_kickoff_survives_listing_failure` — end-to-end: `flow.kickoff()` completes, `storage.save()` is called, `result_record` is produced (fails on `main`).

Full `tests/memory/` suite: 190 passed; the only failure on this machine is the pre-existing environment-dependent `test_qdrant_edge_storage.py::test_orphaned_shard_cleanup`, which fails identically on unmodified `main`.

title: fix(prompts): use the right task slice with custom templates
body:
Fixes #8560

## Problem

`Prompts.task_execution()` selects one of three task slices — `task` (ReAct), `native_task` (native function calling), `task_no_tools` (no tools) — and appends it to the prompt components. With custom `system_template` / `prompt_template`, `_build_prompt` filters the system parts with `if component != "task"` (exact string match only) and hardcodes `I18N_DEFAULT.slice("task")` into the `{{ .Prompt }}` slot. Result for non-ReAct agents:

- the mode-specific task slice leaks into `{{ .System }}` (duplicated task context);
- `{{ .Prompt }}` always receives the ReAct slice — *"use the tools available ... Thought:"* — including for **native-function-calling** agents (wrong response format) and **tool-less** agents (told to use tools they don't have).

## Solution

In `_build_prompt` (`lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/prompts.py`), detect which of the three task slices is present in `components`, exclude it from the `{{ .System }}` parts, and substitute that slice into `{{ .Prompt }}`. The classic ReAct path (custom templates + non-native tools) produces byte-identical output to before; only the native and no-tools modes are corrected.

## Testing

New regression tests in `lib/crewai/tests/utilities/test_prompts_custom_templates.py`:

- `test_native_tool_calling_uses_native_task_slice_in_prompt_slot` — `{{ .Prompt }}` carries the clean `Current Task: {input}` slice; no ReAct instructions; task text not duplicated into the system section (fails on `main`);
- `test_no_tools_uses_task_no_tools_slice_in_prompt_slot` — `{{ .Prompt }}` carries `Provide your complete response:` and no "use the tools available" (fails on `main`);
- `test_react_tools_keep_classic_task_slice_in_prompt_slot` — the ReAct output is unchanged (guards the no-regression case);
- `test_system_section_holds_persona_not_task` — for both tool modes the system section holds only persona text.

Existing agent suites that exercise `Prompts` (`tests/agents/test_agent.py`, `test_agent_inject_date.py`) still pass.

---

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> **Low Risk**
> Prompt assembly only; corrects wrong instructions for native and no-tool agents without changing the default ReAct custom-template output.

> **Overview**

title: fix(lite-agent): reset guardrail retry count per kickoff

---

## Description

`kickoff` reset `_iterations`, `tools_results` and `_tool_failures` per execution but not `_guardrail_retry_count`, so a reused agent instance inherited the previous run's consumed budget: after one run used (or exhausted) its guardrail retries, the next kickoff raised on its **first** guardrail failure instead of getting its own fresh `guardrail_max_retries` budget (or silently got fewer retries than configured).

## Changes

- `lib/crewai/src/crewai/lite_agent.py`: `self._guardrail_retry_count = 0` added to the per-execution reset block in `kickoff`.

## Tests

- `lib/crewai/tests/agents/test_lite_agent_guardrail_retry_reset.py` (new, fully offline):
  - `test_retry_counter_resets_between_kickoffs` — two consecutive kickoffs each consume their own 3-attempt budget (fails on main: the second run raises after a single attempt)
  - `test_exhausted_budget_does_not_leak_into_next_kickoff` — after one kickoff exhausts its retries, the next kickoff still gets 4 attempts (fails on main: it gets 1)

`run_crew_tool` is the LLM-callable tool behind `crewai chat` (declared `-> str`, passed to `chat_llm.call(available_functions=...)`). When `crew.kickoff` failed it called `sys.exit(1)`:

title: fix(lite-agent): stop re-emitting execution started on guardrail retries

---

## Description

`LiteAgent._execute_core` emitted `LiteAgentExecutionStartedEvent` at the top and then retried guardrail failures via **recursion into itself**, so every retry re-emitted the started event. With `guardrail_max_retries=N` a kickoff emitted N+1 started events with a single terminal event (completed on eventual success, error on exhausted retries), breaking the one-started-plus-one-terminal contract. Trace listeners open one scope per started event, so every guardrail retry leaked an open execution scope.

The recursive call also dropped the per-kickoff `response_format`, so retries silently fell back to `self.response_format`.

## Changes

- `lib/crewai/src/crewai/lite_agent.py`: the attempt body moved to a private `_execute_attempt`; `_execute_core` now emits the started event once and delegates, and the guardrail retry re-enters `_execute_attempt` directly (forwarding `response_format`). One started + one terminal event per kickoff on all paths; retry-count and message semantics unchanged.

## Tests

- `lib/crewai/tests/agents/test_lite_agent_guardrail_event_pairing.py` (new, fully offline):
  - `test_guardrail_retry_emits_single_started_and_completed` — 2 retries then pass yields exactly 1 started + 1 completed (fails on main: 3 started)
  - `test_guardrail_exhausted_retries_pair_started_with_error` — exhausted retries yield 1 started + 1 error (fails on main: N+1 started)

title: fix(flow): cancel sibling methods when a batch fails
body:
Two batch-execution spots in the flow runtime use a bare `asyncio.gather`, which propagates the first exception and leaves the remaining coroutines running in the background after the flow has already failed:

- the plain listener batch in `FlowRuntime._execute_listeners` (several listeners triggered by one method, no racing group);
- the parallel start-method batch in `kickoff_async` (multiple unconditional `@start()` methods).

Once `kickoff_async` raises, in-flight siblings keep executing — LLM calls, tool calls, event emissions — while the caller already holds the exception, and their outcomes are never retrieved (a second failure disappears silently). This is the same defect class already fixed for crews in #8523 and for the racing-listener batch in #8529; this PR covers the remaining bare gathers in the flow runtime.

title: fix(events): render panels when stdout can't encode emoji
body:
`ConsoleFormatter` prints every event panel through a rich `Console` writing to `sys.stdout`, and nearly every panel title carries emoji (`🌊 Flow Started`, `✅/❌`, `🔧` …). On Windows with redirected/piped output and `PYTHONIOENCODING`/`PYTHONUTF8` unset, `sys.stdout` encodes with the ANSI code page (cp936/GBK, cp1252, …), which cannot encode those emoji. Rich deliberately re-raises the `UnicodeEncodeError`, so on main every handler that prints a panel raises into the event bus and gets reported as `[CrewAIEventsBus] Sync handler error ...` — verbose users on those setups get a wall of handler errors and no panels at all.

Related: #7556 / #7557 handle the same failure mode for the trace-batch finalize panel's own `Console()`. This PR fixes the main `ConsoleFormatter` output path.

## Changes

- `lib/crewai/src/crewai/events/utils/console_formatter.py`:
  - new module-private `_EncodingSafeStdout`: a delegating `file` for the formatter's `Console` that resolves `sys.stdout` at write time and, if a write raises `UnicodeEncodeError`, retries the same chunk with unencodable characters replaced (`errors="replace"`). UTF-8-capable streams keep emoji untouched; delegation keeps rich's dynamic-stdout behavior (works under pytest capture).
  - `ConsoleFormatter.__init__` now constructs `Console(width=None, file=...)` with that wrapper.

## Tests

- `lib/crewai/tests/utilities/test_console_formatter_encoding.py` (new):
  - `test_emoji_panels_render_on_non_utf8_stdout` — GBK-strict stdout; emoji panels must render with replacements instead of raising (fails on main with `UnicodeEncodeError: 'gbk' codec can't encode character '\U0001f30a'`)
  - `test_ascii_panel_unchanged_on_non_utf8_stdout` — guard: ASCII panels print the same text on a GBK stream
  - `test_emoji_kept_intact_on_utf8_stdout` — guard: UTF-8 streams keep the emoji

## Verification

- New tests: 1 fails on main → 3 pass with the fix
- `pytest lib/crewai/tests/utilities lib/crewai/tests/events lib/crewai/tests/test_flow.py` (excluding known local libmagic-crashing files): 813 passed; the only 2 failures (`test_anthropic_research_workflow_generates_steps`, `test_summarize_direct_anthropic`) fail identically on unmodified main (local environment)
- `ruff check --no-fix` / `ruff format --check` / strict `mypy` on changed files: clean

## Note

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude) and reviewed by me. Per the contributing guidelines it should carry the `llm-generated` label — I can't add labels myself, so could a maintainer please add it. Thanks!
