title: fix(files): honor an injected aioboto3 session in BedrockFileUploader
body:
Fixes #8520

## Summary

`_get_async_client` wrote its auto-created session to a phantom `self._session` attribute that `__init__` never defines and returned it unconditionally, so:

- a caller passing `async_client` (exposed by the factory's `BedrockOpts`/`AllOptions`) always crashed with `AttributeError: ... no attribute '_session'`, wrapped by `aupload`'s classifier into a misleading `TransientUploadError` that the resolver then retried three times;
- the constructor parameter was dead even on the auto-create path.

The created session is now stored in `self._async_client` and the injected value is used as-is, mirroring the sync twin `_get_client`. The `__init__` docstring now says the parameter is an aioboto3 **Session** (which is what `aupload`/`adelete` require, since they call `session.client("s3", ...)` on it).

## Verification

New `tests/test_bedrock_async_client.py`:
- `test_aupload_uses_injected_async_session` / `test_adelete_uses_injected_async_session` — fail on main with the phantom-attribute error, pass with this change; a stub session records the S3 calls it received
- `test_aupload_creates_session_when_none_injected` — control for the auto-create path (fake `aioboto3` module via `sys.modules`), passes on both
- Tests are hermetic: no boto3/aioboto3 install needed (TransferConfig seam stubbed; the files test env doesn't ship boto3)
- Full `crewai-files` suite locally: 179 passed, 4 skipped, no regressions; repo-pinned `ruff check`/`format --check` clean

## Risk

Low — behavior only changes for callers that pass `async_client`, who previously always crashed; the auto-create path returns the same Session it always did.

🤖 Generated with ZCode (AI agent) on behalf of Wilson0511

Co-Authored-By: ZCode <agent@zcode.dev>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Scoped to Bedrock async S3 upload/delete; fixes previously broken injection with no change to default lazy-session behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`BedrockFileUploader`** async setup so `async_client` (an **aioboto3 `Session`**) is stored and returned from `_get_async_client`, matching the sync `_get_client` pattern. Previously, lazy creation wrote to a non-existent `self._session` and always returned it, so **`aupload`/`adelete` failed** when a session was injected (often surfaced as misleading **`TransientUploadError` retries**) and the constructor argument was effectively unused.
> 
> The **`async_client` docstring** now documents that it is a Session, created on first use when omitted. **New tests** cover injected-session upload/delete and lazy session creation with stubbed aioboto3 (no real AWS deps).
>

title: build(deps): bump setuptools from 83.0.0 to 84.1.0 in the security-updates group across 1 directory
body:
Bumps the security-updates group with 1 update in the / directory: [setuptools](https://github.com/pypa/setuptools). Updates `setuptools` from 83.0.0 to 84.1.0
Changelog

Sourced from setuptools's changelog.

v84.1.0

Features

  • setuptools.archive_util now raises the new UnsafeMember exception when an archive member would be extracted outside of the extraction directory, where previously such a member was silently skipped. Aborting makes a malicious or malformed archive visible to the caller instead of yielding a quietly incomplete extraction, and matches the behavior of the standard library's tarfile extraction filters.

Bugfixes

  • Wheel.install_as_egg no longer creates namespace package directories outside of the destination egg directory. Entries in a wheel's namespace_packages.txt were split on . and passed straight to os.path.join, so an entry that was absolute, drive-qualified, or UNC discarded the destination and placed an __init__.py at a path chosen by the wheel. Namespace entries are now validated as dotted module names on every platform -- see GHSA-xmj3-9gf7-h52w.

    This code path is reached only by the deprecated setup_requires mechanism when setup() is invoked outside a PEP 517 frontend; the setuptools build backend never reaches it.

  • setuptools.archive_util no longer extracts archive members outside of the requested extraction directory. Both the tar and zip formats specify / as the only path separator, but the guard against .. components split member names on / alone, so a name such as ..\escaped.txt was treated as a single component and then resolved as a traversal by the filesystem on Windows. Member names containing a backslash, a drive letter, or a UNC prefix are now rejected on every platform, as are members whose resolved destination falls outside the extraction directory -- see GHSA-grgh-hr87-3jpw.

v84.0.0

Features

  • Newline-separated keywords and platformspypa/setuptools#4887old specification <https://peps.python.org/pep-0345/>_ separated items with spaces and the current one uses commas. (#4887)
  • Extensionpypa/distutils#373#5022)
  • The C compiler modules now emit log messages through their own compilers.C.* loggers instead of the distutils root logger, part of decoupling the compilers package from distutils. The logger names are normalized to a stable compilers.C.* prefix so they remain constant as the package migrates toward a standalone compilers.C distribution. (#5266)
  • The C compilers gained a Compiler.call method -- a thin wrapper over subprocess.check_call (with macOS deployment-target env injection) that is the modern replacement for Compiler.spawn. The compilers no longer depend on distutils.spawn, distutils.dir_util, distutils.file_util, distutils._modified, or distutils.util.execute/split_quoted: the generic newer/newer_group and split_quoted helpers are vendored into the compilers package, and Compiler.mkpath/move_file/execute are implemented directly on the standard library (os.makedirs/shutil.move). The methods are retained for backward compatibility. (#5267)
  • The compilers no longer depend on distutils.util, distutils.version, distutils.compat, or distutils._macos_compat. The platform-identification helpers (get_platform/get_host_platform/is_mingw) now live in distutils.compilers.platform.detect and the macOS deployment-target logic and compiler_fixup in distutils.compilers.platform.macos; CygwinCCompiler.gcc_version returns a packaging.version.Version. distutils.util re-exports the platform/macOS helpers from their new homes for backward compatibility rather than keeping duplicate copies. (sysconfig lookups still route through distutils pending its own decoupling.) (#5268)
  • The compilers now read their build configuration from the standard library's sysconfig instead of distutils.sysconfig. Per-compiler customization -- previously distutils.sysconfig.customize_compiler -- has moved into Compiler.configure_system(): a no-op on the base class, with UnixCCompiler applying the compiler/flag/archiver settings CPython recorded in sysconfig (and the usual CC/CFLAGS/LDSHARED/… environment overrides). distutils.sysconfig.customize_compiler is retained as a thin wrapper that calls compiler.configure_system(). (#5269)

... (truncated)

title: fix(flow): tool actions honor the tool's tool_failure_policy
body:
Fixes #8425
Stacked on #8424 (same area, `ToolAction.run`); only the second commit is new.

## Problem

`ToolAction.run` (PR #8367) raised `ToolExecutionFailedError` on every detected `ToolFailure`, ignoring `BaseTool.tool_failure_policy` — whose contract is "Overrides the agent's and task's tool_failure_policy for this tool only". A tool explicitly configured WARN (or IGNORE) still killed the whole flow, and because the raise bypassed `handle_tool_failure` entirely, not a single `ToolFailureDetectedEvent` reached the event bus — zero observability for flow tool failures.

The agent execution path already resolves the policy (`resolve_tool_failure_policy` / `handle_tool_failure`); the same tool should not silently change failure semantics depending on whether an agent or a flow calls it.

## Change

`_actions.py` (`ToolAction.run`): when the tool declares an explicit `tool_failure_policy`, route the detected failure through `handle_tool_failure(failure, tool_name=..., tool_args=..., tool=self.tool)`:

- **WARN** — records the failure, emits `ToolFailureDetectedEvent`, flow continues with the soft-failure output;
- **IGNORE** — silent, flow continues;
- **RAISE** — aborts.

A tool with no policy set keeps flow actions' fail-hard default, preserving #8367's behavior for unconfigured tools.

## Verification

- New `tests/test_flow_tool_action_failure_policy.py::test_warn_policy_tool_does_not_kill_the_flow`: fails on `main` (`ToolExecutionFailedError` raised, zero events) and passes with the fix; `test_raise_policy_tool_still_aborts_the_flow` pins RAISE.
- `tests/test_flow_from_definition.py` (includes #8367's own suite): 173 passed; `tests/test_flow_tool_action_usage.py`: 2 passed.
- `mypy` clean; `ruff` clean on the new test file.

## Risk

Low: only tools that explicitly set `tool_failure_policy` change behavior — in the direction their own configuration asks for.

🤖 Generated with [ZCode](https://github.com/) (AI agent) on behalf of @Wilson0511

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Behavior changes only for tools that explicitly set `tool_failure_policy`; unconfigured tools and RAISE semantics stay the same.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Flow tool steps now respect each tool's explicit `tool_failure_policy`**, aligning flow tool actions with the agent execution path instead of always aborting on a detected `ToolFailure`.
> 
> When a flow tool action sees a soft failure, it routes through `handle_tool_failure` if the tool sets `tool_failure_policy` (WARN continues and emits `ToolFailureDetectedEvent`, IGNORE is silent, RAISE still aborts). Tools **without** an explicit policy keep the previous fail-hard behavior (`ToolExecutionFailedError`).
> 
> New tests cover WARN (flow completes, event fires) and RAISE (still raises).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9a0013798378988c828f2e475a1de174d667c5b4. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(flow): tool actions get a fresh usage budget per kickoff
body:
Fixes #8423

## Problem

Tool actions build their tool instances once per flow object (`_flow_post_init`) and reuse them across kickoffs, but nothing reset `current_usage_count` at the kickoff boundary. A `max_usage_count` budget exhausted in an earlier kickoff therefore made **every later kickoff of the same flow object fail**: `BaseTool.run` answered with `ToolFailure(USAGE_LIMIT)` and `ToolAction.run` (PR #8367) turned that into a fatal `ToolExecutionFailedError`.

The agent path already zeroes the counter every time tools are prepared (`parse_tools`); the flow runtime had no equivalent.

## Change

- `_actions.py` (`ToolAction.__init__`): register the built tool on the flow instance (`_tool_action_tools`) so kickoffs can find it.
- `runtime/__init__.py` (`Flow._reset_tool_action_usage_budgets`): new helper calling `tool.reset_usage_count()` for every registered tool, invoked at the top of `kickoff_async`'s execution path — the single seam every run goes through (`kickoff`, `kickoff_async`, `astream`, checkpoint resume).

## Verification

- New `tests/test_flow_tool_action_usage.py::test_tool_action_usage_budget_resets_between_kickoffs`: fails on `main`, passes with the fix.
- `test_tool_action_usage_budget_still_enforced_within_a_kickoff` pins that the budget remains per-kickoff, not per-call (an `each:` loop invoking a `max_usage_count=1` tool twice still fails mid-run).
- `tests/test_flow_from_definition.py` (includes PR #8367's own suite): 173 passed.
- `mypy` clean on the touched module; `ruff` output unchanged vs `main`.

## Risk

Low: the reset only touches tools built by flow tool actions, and the budget still applies within a single kickoff.

🤖 Generated with [ZCode](https://github.com/) (AI agent) on behalf of @Wilson0511

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow change at the kickoff boundary for flow tool actions only; does not alter agent tool prep or relax limits within a single kickoff.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes reused flow tool instances carrying **`current_usage_count`** across multiple **`kickoff`** calls on the same **`Flow`** object, which could permanently trip **`max_usage_count`** after an earlier run.
> 
> **`ToolAction`** now registers each built tool on the flow via **`_tool_action_tools`**. **`Flow._reset_tool_action_usage_budgets()`** calls **`reset_usage_count()`** on those tools at the start of **`kickoff_async`** (covering sync kickoff and streaming paths). Per-kickoff limits still apply inside a single run (e.g. **`each:`** loops).

> Adds **`test_flow_tool_action_usage.py`** for multi-kickoff reset and in-run enforcement.

title: fix: Crew.test emits its start event before setup so a failed setup pairs
body:
Fixes #8419

## Change

`Crew.test` emits `CrewTestStartedEvent` before `create_llm` (`eval_llm` now carries the requested spec, which the field's `str | Any | None` type already allows) instead of after it, so a setup failure's `CrewTestFailedEvent` has its opener on the scope stack.

## Why

`crew_test_failed` is scope-ending. The start event was emitted only after `create_llm` succeeded, so a create_llm failure (bad model spec, missing key) emitted an unpaired Failed that popped the caller's enclosing event scope and corrupted later event parentage — the same theft shape as the a2a delegation fix (#8407), in the test harness path.

## Proof

- `test_crew.py::test_crew_test_setup_failure_pairs_events` (new): with `create_llm` raising, `test()` emits Started then a Failed whose `started_event_id` pairs with it. Red before: no Started at all, Failed unpaired.
- `test_crew.py -k 'test_crew or replay'`: 136 passed, 1 skipped, plus the known env-only `test_crew_kickoff_streaming_usage_metrics` failing identically on clean main. The existing success-path test (`test_crew_testing_function`) still passes.

## Risk

Low. Success-path payload change is `eval_llm` carrying the requested spec instead of the built instance; no in-repo listener reads the field (telemetry has no crew_test handler).

🤖 Generated with [ZCode](https://github.com/) (AI agent) on behalf of @Wilson0511

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Event ordering and a minor started-event payload change on the success path; no in-repo consumers depend on `eval_llm` being the built instance.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`Crew.test()`** now emits **`CrewTestStartedEvent`** before evaluation setup (including `create_llm`), so a setup failure can emit a **`CrewTestFailedEvent`** that pairs with that start instead of leaving the failed event unpaired and corrupting the event scope stack.
> 
> On the success path, **`eval_llm`** on the started event carries the requested model spec rather than the constructed LLM instance. A new test asserts that when `create_llm` raises, started and failed events are both emitted and **`failed.started_event_id`** matches the test’s own start event.

Crew.test emits CrewTestStartedEvent before create_llm (eval_llm now

title: fix: replay emits CrewKickoffFailedEvent when the replayed run fails
body:
Fixes #8417

## Change

`Crew.replay`'s execution tail wraps `_execute_tasks` in try/except, emitting `CrewKickoffFailedEvent(started_event_id=self._kickoff_event_id)` before re-raising — mirroring `kickoff()`'s except-clause.

## Why

#8366 taught replay() to emit `CrewKickoffStartedEvent` so the success path pairs, but the failure path had no terminal: a task exception raised straight out of replay left the start event dangling — no Failed event for listeners, and a leaked `crew_kickoff_started` frame on the event-scope stack that parented every later event in the same context (the next kickoff's start event inherited the leaked frame as `parent_event_id`). Same pairing class as #8402 and #8406; this is the failure-path gap left by #8366 itself.

## Proof

- `test_replay_failure_emits_kickoff_failed_event` (new): a failing replay emits a Failed event scoped to the replay's own start id (red: no Failed event at all).
- `test_replay_failure_does_not_leak_kickoff_scope_into_next_kickoff` (new): after a failed replay, the next kickoff's start event has `parent_event_id is None` (red: parented to the leaked replay scope).
- `test_crew.py -k 'replay or kickoff_event'`: 16 passed; full `test_crew.py`: 137 passed, 1 skipped — unchanged from main apart from the two new tests.

## Risk

Low. Purely additive terminal event on a path that previously raised immediately; success path unchanged.

title: fix: emit LLMGuardrailCompletedEvent when a guardrail raises
body:
Fixes #8402

## Change

`process_guardrail` now emits `LLMGuardrailCompletedEvent(success=False, error="<Type>: <msg>")` and re-raises when the guardrail callable raises a non-`HookAborted` exception, mirroring the existing `HookAborted` branch (which keeps its exact legacy error string).

## Why

`LLMGuardrailStartedEvent` is emitted before the call; an ordinary exception left it without a terminal event. The tracing listener's `evaluate guardrail` span then stayed open until `TelemetrySession.finish_spans()` closed it as `Span orphaned — execution ended before completion event`, discarding the real error from the trace. Denies already keep the pairing (`test_a_denied_guardrail_still_reports_the_validation_it_started`); an exception ends the validation just as decisively and owes the same terminal event.

## Proof

- `tests/test_guardrail_events_on_exception.py` (new): a raising guardrail produces exactly one started + one completed(`success=False`) event, and the exception still reaches the caller unchanged. Red before the fix: the completed list is empty.
- `tests/hooks/test_hook_abort_propagation.py` + `tests/test_task_guardrails.py`: 48 passed — deny path and task retry behavior unchanged.

title: fix: private memories without a source no longer leak to every recall
body:
Fixes #8399

### The bug

The privacy filters in both recall paths test `not r.private or r.source == source`. For a private record saved without a source (`remember(private=True)` → `source=None`), the second clause reduces to `None == None` — True — so the record is returned to **every** default caller (`source=None`, `include_private=False`). The privacy flag is void for source-less records, on both the shallow path (`unified_memory.py`) and the deep RecallFlow path (`recall_flow.py`).

### The fix

Both filters now require a real, matching source before a private record is visible:

```python
if not r.private or (source is not None and r.source == source)
```

Legitimate access is unchanged: a private record with a real source stays visible to that source, and `include_private=True` still sees everything (both covered by tests that pass on main and after the fix).

### Tests

- `test_private_record_without_source_does_not_leak` (shallow + deep, parametrized): a private `source=None` record is excluded from unprivileged recalls while a public record in the same scope stays visible — fails on main for both paths.
- `test_private_record_still_visible_to_its_source_and_when_included`: the owning source and `include_private=True` still see the record — passes on main (the tightening breaks no legitimate access).

Full memory suite: 166 passed, 0 failed.

🤖 Generated with [ZCode](https://github.com/) (AI agent) on behalf of @Wilson0511

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> This changes memory privacy enforcement on recall paths; incorrect filtering could hide legitimate private data or still leak secrets, though new tests target the reported leak.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Fixes a privacy leak** where private memories stored with `source=None` were returned to every default `recall()` (`source=None`, `include_private=False`) because the filter treated `None == None` as a match.
> 
> The recall privacy filter in **`unified_memory.py`** (shallow path) and **`recall_flow.py`** (deep RecallFlow) now only exposes a private record when the caller has a **non-null** `source` that equals the record’s `source`: `not r.private or (source is not None and r.source == source)`.
> 
> **Tests** add coverage for shallow and deep recall (no leak for `private=True` + `source=None`, public records still visible) and confirm owning sources and `include_private=True` still work.
>

title: feat(tools): add Mekong x402 pay-per-call tool family
body:
# PR: Add Mekong x402 tools (pay-per-call APIs, no API key)

**Title:** `feat(tools): add Mekong x402 pay-per-call tool family`

**Target repo:** `crewAIInc/crewAI` → `lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/tools/mekong_x402_tool/`
**Files:** `__init__.py`, `mekong_x402_tool.py`, `schemas.py`, `README.md`

---

## What

7 native CrewAI tools for the [Mekong x402 fleet](https://api.mekongtradeintel.com/tools/) —
37 pay-per-call APIs on Base (USDC):

- `MekongTaskRouterTool` — **FREE** task router: describe a task in plain language → top-3 endpoints + curls
- `MekongWebSearchTool` — live web search ($0.01)
- `MekongTokenPriceTool` — price/mcap/liquidity ($0.001)
- `MekongAIVerdictTool` — token safety verdict ($0.01)
- `MekongEnrichTool` — company enrichment ($0.02)
- `MekongSTTTool` — speech-to-text ($0.05)
- `MekongBriefTool` — news+trends+sentiment bundle ($0.05)

## Why this belongs in crewai-tools

- **Zero-config for the agent operator:** no API keys, no signup, no env vars.
  Every endpoint has a free daily trial quota per IP — the tools work out of the box.
- **Honest paid path:** when the trial is exhausted the tool raises
  `MekongPaymentRequired` with the exact price, `payTo`, asset, network and the
  3-step x402 flow. Never a silent charge, never a fake success.
- **Independently verifiable:** https://api.mekongtradeintel.com/tools/verify —
  one-command script checking 402 paywall shape, CDP `/x402/validate` preflight
  and on-chain settlement from the outside.

## Tested

- All 7 tools instantiate; free router tool run live against production
  (`task="Is this token a honeypot?"` → `rugcheck` top-1, correct).
- 402 path unit-tested with mocked responses (raises with pay instructions).
- Follows repo conventions: `BaseTool` + `args_schema` pydantic models in
  `schemas.py`, `_run(**kwargs)`, per-tool README.

## Notes for reviewers

- No `env_vars`: there is deliberately nothing to configure — that is the point
  of x402 (the wallet is the credential).
- The fleet is operated by Mekong Trade Intelligence; endpoints are plain HTTPS
  + x402 v2 (`exact` scheme, USDC on Base `eip155:8453`).
- Happy to split into smaller PRs per tool if preferred.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces runtime dependency on a third-party paid API and financial/token-safety surfaces; payment is not auto-charged but operators must understand 402/x402 behavior when trials expire.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a new **`mekong_x402_tool`** package under `crewai-tools` with seven `BaseTool` implementations that call the Mekong x402 fleet over HTTPS—no API keys or env vars.
> 
> A shared **`_call`** helper POSTs to `api.mekongtradeintel.com`, parses JSON responses, and on HTTP **402** raises **`MekongPaymentRequired`** with USDC-on-Base x402 pay steps instead of failing silently. **`MekongEnrichTool`** uses GET for the happy path but reuses that 402 handling when the trial quota is exhausted.
> 
> Each tool has Pydantic **`args_schema`** models in `schemas.py` and formats API output as agent-friendly strings (search bullets, token stats, briefings, etc.). **`MekongTaskRouterTool`** hits `/recommend/` and is documented as free endpoint discovery. A package **`README`** documents pricing, usage, and independent verification of the paywall.
>

title: fix(knowledge): read Excel cells as written in ExcelKnowledgeSource
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8375

## Summary

`ExcelKnowledgeSource` let pandas infer a dtype for every column, so the text it chunked and embedded differed from the workbook:

- `12` became `12.0` in a column with a blank cell.
- `01234`, stored as text, became `1234`.
- Cells that say `N/A` or `NULL` were emptied, because both are pandas default NA values.

Each sheet is now read with `dtype=str, keep_default_na=False`, so a cell's text is what the workbook holds. Empty cells still come out empty, and the CSV layout per sheet is unchanged.

```
main:     A1,12.0,1234,     A2,,2134,
this PR:  A1,12,01234,N/A   A2,,02134,NULL
```

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

- `test_excel_knowledge_source_keeps_cells_as_written` builds the workbook from the issue and asserts the sheet text. It fails on `main` and passes here.
- `tests/knowledge/`: 53 passed. The two `docling` tests fail with and without this change, because `docling` is not installed locally.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` (repo config) are clean on the changed source file.

## Additional context

None.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized change to Excel parsing for knowledge ingestion; improves fidelity with a small behavioral shift for existing workbooks that relied on pandas dtype inference.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Excel knowledge ingestion** now preserves each cell’s displayed text when sheets are converted to CSV for chunking and embedding.
> 
> `ExcelKnowledgeSource._load_content` passes `dtype=str` and `keep_default_na=False` to `pd.read_excel`, so integers stay `12` instead of `12.0`, leading-zero text like `01234` is not normalized, and literal `N/A` / `NULL` strings are not treated as missing values. Empty cells still export as blank fields; per-sheet CSV shape is unchanged.
> 
> A regression test builds a workbook with those edge cases and asserts the exact CSV lines produced from the sheet content.
>

title: fix(crew): let a hierarchical crew run more than once
body:
Fixes #8368

## Summary

A hierarchical crew only works on its first run. A second `kickoff()`/`akickoff()`, `copy()` after a run,
`kickoff_for_each()` after a run, and every `train(n_iterations > 1)` hit one of two problems:

- With `manager_llm`, the manager built on the first run keeps its delegation tools, so `_create_manager_agent`
  raises `Manager agent should not have tools` on the next run. It now rejects only tools that are not
  `BaseAgentTool` delegation tools, so a `manager_agent` given real tools still raises as before.
- With `manager_agent`, the first run leaves the manager assigned to the task, and `_update_manager_tools` then
  offered the manager only itself as a coworker. It now skips that case and delegates to the crew's agents, as
  on the first run. A task assigned to a worker still delegates to that worker only.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

`test_hierarchical_crew_delegates_to_workers_on_every_kickoff` runs the same crew twice for `manager_llm` and
`manager_agent`, through `kickoff()` and `akickoff()`, and checks the worker is called on each run. On `main`
all four cases fail: `manager_llm` with `Manager agent should not have tools`, `manager_agent` with
`assert 1 == 2` (the worker is not called on run 2).

- `lib/crewai/tests/`: 6201 passed, 44 skipped (Python 3.13)
- Hierarchical/manager tests in `test_crew.py` also pass on Python 3.10
- `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy` clean

## Additional context

Previously reported in #2131 (training) and #1851; both were closed without a fix. #4782 and #5037 changed
`_update_manager_tools` so a task with an assigned worker delegates to every agent; this PR keeps the current
behavior for assigned workers and only fixes the case where the "assigned" agent is the manager itself.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes hierarchical manager validation and delegation tool wiring on reused crews; behavior is narrow but affects core orchestration paths (multi-kickoff, train, copy).
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **repeat kickoffs** for hierarchical crews (`kickoff`/`akickoff`, `copy`, `train`, `kickoff_for_each`) that previously failed or stopped delegating after the first run.
> 
> For **`manager_llm`**, the manager agent is reused with delegation tools still attached; `_create_manager_agent` now only errors when the manager has **non-delegation** tools (anything that is not a `BaseAgentTool`), so injected coworker delegation tools are allowed while user-supplied tools on a custom `manager_agent` still raise.
> 
> For **`manager_agent`**, a prior run can leave the manager on `task.agent`; `_update_manager_tools` now treats that as “no assigned worker” and injects delegation to **`self.agents`** again instead of delegating only to the manager. Tasks still assigned to a real worker delegate to that worker only.
> 
> Adds **`test_hierarchical_crew_delegates_to_workers_on_every_kickoff`** (scripted LLM, two runs, `manager_llm` vs `manager_agent`, sync vs async) asserting the worker is invoked on every run.

title: feat(flow): run an integration app action directly with call: tool
body:
## Summary

A flow step can now run one integration app action directly, with no agent:

    do:
      call: tool
      ref: google_gmail/send_email
      with: {to: "${state.email}", subject: "Daily digest", body: "${outputs.summarize}"}

`ref` takes the same selector an agent lists in `apps`, so users write one string in both places. A class ref always contains `:` and an app selector always have a `/`. Add `@<connection>` to pick a connection.

The app tool is built through the existing `_resolve_platform_tools`, so `with` is checked against the action's real JSON Schema. A selector with no action (`gmail`), or one that resolves to anything other than exactly one tool, fails at load with an error that names the ref.

**Behavior change:** a `call: tool` step now raises `ToolExecutionFailedError` when its tool returns `ToolFailure`. Before, the failure became the step's output, so later steps took a failed send for a success. Platform tools report every API error this way, and code tools that return `ToolFailure` are affected too.

## Verification

- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally
- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior

- New tests cover: an app action with and without `@<connection>`, a missing action, zero tools returned, and a tool that returns `ToolFailure`. All 5 failed on `main` first.

## Additional context

- The app action is fetched when the flow loads, as agent apps already are. A platform outage fails the flow at load, not at the step.

title: fix: emit CrewKickoffStartedEvent in replay so completion pairs correctly
body:
Fixes #8365

### The bug

`replay()` never emits a `CrewKickoffStartedEvent` (only `prepare_kickoff` does, and replay skips it), but its execution tail still emits `CrewKickoffCompletedEvent(started_event_id=self._kickoff_event_id)`. On every replay this produces:

1. `[CrewAIEventsBus] Warning: Ending event 'crew_kickoff_completed' emitted with empty scope stack. Missing starting event?`
2. A completion event referencing the **original kickoff's** start id — two completions pointing at one start, corrupting event pairing/trace causality for listeners.

### The fix

Mirror `prepare_kickoff` in `replay()`: after `_interpolate_inputs`, emit `CrewKickoffStartedEvent(crew_name=self.name, inputs=replay_inputs)`, store its id in `self._kickoff_event_id`, and await the emit future the same way the kickoff path does. The completion event (built from `_kickoff_event_id` in `_create_crew_output`) then pairs with the replay's own start.

### Test

`test_replay_emits_paired_kickoff_events` — after `kickoff()`, `replay()` must surface its own `CrewKickoffStartedEvent` (fresh event id, distinct from the kickoff's) and leave `_kickoff_event_id` pointing at it. Fails on main; passes with the fix. All 14 existing replay tests, the event-bus suites, and the rest of `test_crew.py` stay green (135 passed; the single usage-metrics failure reproduces identically on unmodified main — environment-only, litellm unavailable).

title: fix: re-raise HookAborted from the ReAct text tool path
body:
### What

`AgentExecutor.execute_tool_action` (the ReAct text-based tool route) now re-raises `HookAborted` instead of letting the generic `except Exception` handler fold it into an `"Observation: Error executing tool: ..."` recovery message for the LLM. Added an `except HookAborted: raise` clause ahead of the generic handler, mirroring the existing `ToolExecutionFailedError` passthrough in the same function.

### Why

`_invoke_hook` (`hooks/dispatch.py`) re-raises only `HookAborted` and fails open on every other exception — `HookAborted` is the documented way to veto a tool call (`raise HookAborted("deletion not allowed")` in the `@on` docstring). The native tool-call path (`execute_native_tool`), the parallel todo executor, and LiteAgent all treat it as a deliberate stop and re-raise. Only the ReAct text path downgraded the abort into a tool-error observation, letting the agent keep iterating (and re-invoke the vetoed tool) after a policy abort, with inconsistent behavior between the two tool-call modes.

### How verified

- New `lib/crewai/tests/agents/test_react_tool_hook_contract.py`:
  - a `POST_TOOL_CALL` hook raising `HookAborted` now propagates out of `execute_tool_action` (fails on `main` with `DID NOT RAISE`);
  - a plain `RuntimeError` from tool execution still takes the observation recovery path and returns `"tool_completed"`.
- `lib/crewai/tests/agents/test_native_tool_hook_contract.py` and `lib/crewai/tests/tools/test_tool_failure.py`: 122 passed.
- `lib/crewai/tests/agents/test_agent_executor.py`: same 12 pre-existing failures before/after (verified via stash); 109 passed.
- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` clean.

Fixes #8362

> Small, targeted exception-handling change aligned with other tool paths; behavior only changes when hooks intentionally abort via HookAborted.

title: fix(agents): run async native tools on the kickoff caller's event loop
body:
Fixes #8904.

Follow-up to #7630 (the closed #7634 was the pre-#8192 fix for the same family).

## The bug (reproduced on `main`)

After #8192, every sync Flow method runs in a worker thread (`asyncio.to_thread`, flow runtime `_execute_method`). An async native tool's coroutine therefore goes through the bare `asyncio.run()` inside `Tool.run` — on a **fresh, unrelated event loop per call**. Anything bound to the kickoff caller's loop fails deterministically:

```
RuntimeError: Task ... got Future <Future pending> attached to a different loop
```

Minimal repro on unpatched `main`: a Crew with one `@tool async def`; the tool awaits a `Future` created on the `kickoff_async` caller's loop after `asyncio.run(crew.kickoff_async())` → the tool result the LLM sees is `Error executing tool: ... attached to a different loop`. Same shape for any caller-loop-bound resource (`httpx.AsyncClient` created before kickoff, sockets).

## The fix

- The async kickoffs capture the caller's event loop into a **ContextVar** (`Crew.kickoff_async` non-stream branch, `AgentExecutor.invoke_async`). `Crew.kickoff_async` is `await asyncio.to_thread(self.kickoff, ...)`, so capturing **before** the thread boundary is what makes the loop visible inside every worker lane — ContextVars propagate through `to_thread` and the Flow runtime's `copy_context` (including the `ThreadPoolExecutor` in `execute_native_tool`).
- `agent_utils.run_native_tool_result(...)` executes the tool: when a caller loop is present **and** the tool has a working async implementation, bridge `tool.arun(**args)` onto the caller loop via `run_coroutine_threadsafe(...).result()` (the worker thread blocks; the coroutine runs with caller-loop affinity). Otherwise the exact historical sync behavior — the `available_functions` mapping stays authoritative, so test doubles and cache wrappers are untouched.
- Async-capability detection: `Tool`-wrapped functions are async iff the wrapped function is a coroutine function (`Tool` always overrides `_arun`, even for sync funcs); class-based `BaseTool`s qualify when their type overrides the `NotImplementedError`-raising `BaseTool._arun`.

## Tests

New `lib/crewai/tests/agents/test_native_async_tool_loop_affinity.py`:

- worker-thread bridge onto a caller-loop `Future` (unit, with and without caller loop),
- full `Crew` + scripted-LLM `kickoff_async` path asserting the caller-loop Future **resolves** instead of the cross-loop error.

## Verification

- `ruff check` clean on all touched files.
- A/B vs pristine `main`: `pytest lib/crewai/tests/agents -k "native or agent_executor or invoke"` — **identical failure sets** (3 pre-existing `TestDeferredNativeToolResults` / `TestResponseFormatWithKickoff` failures reproduce on pristine `main` in this environment; 172 pass on both), plus 4 new green tests.
- With the patch, the repro above returns `got:expected-item` instead of the error.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core tool execution and cross-thread asyncio bridging on every async kickoff; fallbacks and tests limit blast radius but blocking **`future.result()`** in worker threads can stall the caller loop if async tools block.
> 
> **Overview**

title: feat(cli): every crewai eval keeps the evaluation's full data in the project
body:
## Why

An evaluation's report opens for one five-minute sitting after it is first read, and the verdict `crewai eval` waits for counts as that read. A coding agent that wants a check's quotes, the outputs or the trace after its edits runs `crewai eval export` and gets "has been read already. Evaluate the run again for a fresh report."

## What changes

Right after the verdict, `crewai eval` saves the evaluation's export into the project and says where:

```
Goal gate: PASSED · goal 5/5 · tasks 5/5 · tools not measured · agents 3/5
…brief…
Its full data is saved in .crewai/evaluations/22dd9d88-…/ — start with report.md.
```

The folder holds `report.md`, `run/checks.md` (every check, with the judge's words and quotes), `run/outputs.md` and `run/trace.json`, beside a `.gitignore` of `*`.

- **Saved whole, or said otherwise.** A marker (`.crewai-eval-saved`) is written last, only when every file was. It, not `report.md`, means "saved". AMP can't send it: the marker's name is reserved like `.gitignore`, so a payload carrying one is skipped like an unsafe path. A save cut short, or one that skipped a file, says "Part of its data was saved…", leaves no marker, and is tried again on the next read.
- **Graded again with nothing changed:** it's the same evaluation, so it points at what it saved and doesn't ask AMP again. By then the sitting may have closed.
- **A short wait.** The save asks AMP with its own timeout (20 s to read), not export's two minutes, since the verdict is already printed and CI waits on the command.
- **Only inside a project** (a `pyproject.toml` here). `crewai eval --run ID` run from anywhere else saves nothing.
- **The ten newest are kept.** Only a folder this command saved whole is ever removed: named by an evaluation id, a real folder (never a link or a junction), with the marker in it. Nothing is removed when `.crewai/` or `.crewai/evaluations/` is a link.
- **Never at the verdict's cost.** A service that doesn't export yet (404) says nothing. Any other failure is one dim line, with AMP's own words when it sent some. The exit code stays the gate's.
- **Run app:** an evaluation the run app grades on its own screen (a JSON crew or flow run at a terminal) isn't saved; `crewai eval export` still covers it. Every evaluation `crewai eval` itself waits for is saved, including the one it runs after the run app's Evaluate.

Waiting for the verdict already opens the sitting (crew-optimize's `show` calls `open_sitting!`), so saving right after it doesn't shorten anyone's window.

**The export writer** now raises `ExportWriteError` instead of exiting. `crewai eval export` turns it into the same message as before. It also writes into a nested folder the same way it wrote into one: each folder opened inside the one before it, never through a link. The path writer (Windows) refuses a link anywhere on the folder's way before making anything through it, and checks the resolved path against the whole relative path.

## Tests

`test_eval_crew.py`:
- the verdict leaves the full data and its `.gitignore` in `.crewai/evaluations/<id>/`;
- a 404 says nothing and writes nothing;
- a connection error or a 500 is one line, and a failed gate still exits 1;
- only the ten newest are kept, oldest first, and a folder that isn't an evaluation stays;
- outside a project nothing is saved or asked;
- graded again, it points at what it saved without asking AMP;
- a refusal shows AMP's own sentence;
- the save passes its short timeout;
- a skipped file is "part of its data", with no marker, and the next read exports again;
- a write that fails after `report.md` leaves no marker, and the next read saves it whole;
- pruning leaves a UUID-named folder without the marker;
- a link at `.crewai` or at `.crewai/evaluations`, with either writer, keeps every file out of where it leads.
- a marker in AMP's payload, with one file skipped, leaves no marker, and the next read exports again.

The existing `crewai eval export` tests (45) pass unchanged. `lib/cli` eval, run-app and run tests: 630 passed; the 2 failures also fail on main. ruff and mypy are clean.

Checked live against production: a fresh evaluation saved its data, and grading the unchanged project again pointed at the same folder.

title: feat(cli): with no terminal, crewai eval sends the crew's own output to a log
body:
## Why

A coding agent reads every line `crewai eval` prints, and pays for it. When `crewai eval` runs the crew itself, the crew's panels, final answer and tool calls came first. In a measured run that was 341 of 378 lines, all before the verdict, and an agent that cuts long output can lose the verdict and the brief at the end.

## What changes

When nobody reads the output as it prints (stdout isn't a terminal, the same check that decides the brief), what the crew prints while it runs goes to `.crewai/last_run.log`. The agent sees this, then the verdict and brief as before:

```
The project changed since its last traced run: running the crew again to evaluate what it does now.
The crew's output goes to .crewai/last_run.log while it runs.
The crew ran in 42s; its output is in .crewai/last_run.log.
Evaluating run 33599001-…
Goal gate: PASSED · goal 5/5 · tasks 5/5 · tools not measured · agents 3/5
```

The same crew now prints 40 lines instead of 378, with the 587 lines of run output in the log.

- **A run that leaves no trace to evaluate** shows its last 40 lines, which usually hold the error, and the "not traced" sentence says they are above.
- **At a terminal** nothing changes.

**The log** holds final answers, tool output and tracebacks that can carry a credential. It's opened owner-only (0600) and never through a link, and a log an earlier run left is emptied and tightened. It's kept after the verdict on purpose, since it's how an agent reads why a run failed, and the next run overwrites it.

**How.** It moves this process's stdout and stderr (descriptors 1 and 2) while the crew runs. Both originals are saved before either moves. A move that fails halfway puts back what it moved. Putting them back after the run goes stream by stream, never raises, and never hides the run's own error. Every child inherits them, so each way a project runs is covered without touching any of them: `uv run`, the JSON crew runner, declarative flows. On Windows the standard handles are pointed there too. Anything that keeps the output from moving leaves it on screen; a quiet log is a nicety, never a failed run. `.crewai/` is already left out of the project-changed check, so the log never triggers a re-run.

## Tests

`test_eval_crew.py`, using real descriptor writes, as a child process's output arrives:
- with no terminal, the run's stdout and stderr land in the log, not on screen, and the verdict still prints;
- a run that left no trace shows only its last 40 lines, the error included;
- at a terminal, the run prints where it always did and no log is written;
- a terminal stdin with a captured stdout still keeps the transcript off what the agent reads;
- the log is 0600, even one an earlier run left at 0644, and a link at its place leaves the output on screen;
- a move that fails after the first `dup2` puts stdout back before the block runs;
- a put-back that fails on stdout still restores stderr, and the run's own error surfaces.

`lib/cli` eval, run-app and run tests: 584 passed. The 2 failures also fail on main (`test_missing_crewai_package_shows_full_install_hint`, `test_json_runner_imports_with_older_project_env_crewai_core`). ruff and mypy are clean.

Checked live on a fresh JSON crew project: 40 lines, with the run's 587 in the log.

title: fix(agents): restore task description when replanning fails
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8306

## Summary

`AgentExecutor._trigger_replan` temporarily swaps `task.description` for the replan prompt and restores it after `handle_agent_reasoning()`. The restore wasn't in a `finally`, so when the planner call raised (an LLM error, a plan failing `ReasoningPlan` validation, or `HookAborted`), the task kept the replan prompt as its description permanently. That text also showed up in `task.output.description` and carried into later runs.

The fix moves the restore into a `finally`, so the original description comes back whether or not the replan succeeds. Nothing else changes: the existing `except` still records `Replan failed: ...` and keeps the old todos.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

- Added `TestPlanGenerationIsolation::test_failed_replan_restores_task_description`. It makes the planner raise and asserts the description is unchanged and the failure is recorded. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `uv run ruff check`, `uv run ruff format --check` and `uv run mypy` pass on the changed files.
- The replan-related tests in `test_agent_executor.py`, `test_agent_reasoning.py` and `tests/hooks/test_hook_abort_propagation.py` pass. On Windows, some unrelated tests in these files fail locally with and without this change (event-loop and network-disabled errors), so I'm relying on CI for the full suite.

## Additional context

AI-assisted (Claude Code).

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow lifecycle fix around temporary task.description mutation during replan; existing error handling and todo preservation are unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a bug where **failed replans could permanently overwrite `task.description`**. During `_trigger_replan`, the executor temporarily sets `task.description` to the enhanced replan prompt; restoring the original text now runs in a **`finally` block** so LLM errors, plan validation failures, or `HookAborted` no longer leave the replan text on the shared task (and in downstream `task.output`).
> 
> Adds **`test_failed_replan_restores_task_description`**, which forces the planner to raise and checks the description is unchanged while `state.last_replan_reason` records the failure.

title: fix(memory): preserve records when update serialization fails
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8302

## Summary

Updating a LanceDB memory with metadata containing a `datetime` or `set` raises a JSON serialization error after the original record has already been deleted. Serialize the replacement row and prepare its vector before deleting the stored version, so serialization failures leave the saved memory intact.

Add regression tests for both invalid metadata types and a successful replacement. Existing serialization errors are preserved. The delete/add sequence is still nontransactional for storage-write failures.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Regression tests fail before the fix and pass afterward

- Before the fix: 2 failing preservation cases, 1 passing successful-update case.
- Python 3.13 with all locked extras: 163 memory tests passed, excluding the unrelated Qdrant backend test file.
- Python 3.10 with all locked extras: 181 memory tests passed; the existing Qdrant `test_orphaned_shard_cleanup` failed on Windows because `os.kill(pid, 0)` raised WinError 87.
- Tests use real temporary LanceDB databases. The local launcher disabled telemetry, stubbed the unrelated authentication-token lookup, and allowed localhost through the network guard for Windows asyncio.
- Repository-wide Ruff lint and format checks passed; the new test file also passed explicit Ruff checks despite the default test exclusion.
- Configured commit hooks passed, including changed-source mypy and Commitizen. The commit has a verified GPG signature and a DCO sign-off matching its author.
- `uv lock --check --offline --python 3.10` passed without lockfile changes.
- All configured pre-push hooks passed under the repository-pinned Python 3.13 environment: Ruff, Ruff format, changed-source mypy, pip-audit, and Commitizen branch checks. The audit found no known vulnerabilities, with 5 ignored by the existing repository policy.
- Full-workspace mypy could not be verified locally: a check targeting Linux terminated with a Windows access violation. Upstream CI is still needed for the complete Linux test/type-check matrix.


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Small reordering in LanceDB `update()` with targeted regression tests; behavior improves on error paths without changing successful updates.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a data-loss bug in **LanceDB** `update()`: the old row was deleted before the replacement was serialized to JSON, so invalid metadata (e.g. `datetime` or `set`) raised `TypeError` after the stored memory was already removed.
> 
> The update path now builds the row (including vector normalization) **before** the delete/add writes, so serialization errors fail without touching the existing record. Regression tests cover failed updates (record unchanged, count stays 1) and successful replacements.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ed437a347d379c9ca1981294b8a2e825a3779663. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(cli): crewai eval says why before it asks, and its help says when it asks
body:
Two things found while checking `crewai eval` end to end on main before the next release.

**Why before asking.** At a terminal, the first time tracing is turned on, `crewai eval` showed crewAI's trace consent screen with nothing before it, though no crew had run yet:

```
╭──── Execution Traces ────╮
│ 🔍 Detailed execution traces are available! …
Share this execution trace with CrewAI? [y/N] (20s timeout):
```

It now says first why the crew runs and where its trace goes, then asks:

```
No traced run of this crew yet. To evaluate it, the crew runs now and its trace goes to CrewAI AMP, which grades it.
```

There's one line for each reason the crew runs: no traced run yet, the project changed, or the run wasn't traced. After a yes, the run line isn't repeated. Without a terminal nothing changes: no screen and no extra line.

**Help text.** `crewai eval --help` still said "Nothing is asked, with or without a terminal". It now says:
- a person at a terminal is asked the first time tracing is turned on;
- with no terminal nothing is asked, and the command says it turned tracing on;
- a project that turned tracing off is asked at a terminal, and told how to turn it on without one.

**Tests.** `test_at_a_terminal_tracing_is_turned_on_only_after_the_consent_screen` now checks that the reason prints before the screen and not again after it. `lib/cli` eval, run-app and run tests: 533 passed. The 2 failures (`test_missing_crewai_package_shows_full_install_hint`, `test_json_runner_imports_with_older_project_env_crewai_core`) fail on main too. ruff and mypy are clean.

Checked live at a terminal on a fresh project: the line prints, then the screen; "n" runs nothing.

title: fix(mcp): pass every tool result content block to the agent
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8299

## Summary

MCP tool results reached the agent with only `result.content[0]`. The rest of the blocks were dropped, and a non-text first block arrived as its pydantic repr with base64 data. The same logic was copied in `MCPClient._call_tool_impl`, `MCPToolWrapper._execute_tool` and `MCPNativeTool._extract_content`.

This adds one helper, `crewai.mcp.content.content_blocks_to_text`, and uses it in all three places:

- text blocks and embedded text resources keep their text, joined with newlines;
- image, audio, blob and link blocks become `[type: uri or mimeType]`, e.g. `[image: image/png]`, `[resource: file:///report.pdf]`;
- a single text block returns exactly what it returned before.

The helper narrows with `isinstance` on the `mcp.types` content classes. It imports them inside the function, the way `MCPToolWrapper._execute_tool` already imports the SDK, so importing `mcp_native_tool` / `mcp_tool_wrapper` still does not load the MCP SDK. Anything that is not an SDK content block falls back to `str()`, as before. The helper is not re-exported from `crewai.mcp`.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

`lib/crewai/tests/mcp/test_tool_result_content.py` runs each of the three call sites against a 3-text-block result and a text + image + blob result, plus one direct test for audio, resource link and embedded text resource. No network: the MCP session and transport are mocked. With the call sites reverted to main, 6 of the 7 tests fail (the three-text-block cases with `assert 'first' == 'first\nsecond\nthird'`, the mixed-content cases because the placeholders are missing); the remaining one only exercises the new helper.

Run locally on Python 3.13.16 and 3.10.19:

```text
uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/mcp lib/crewai/tests/tools/test_tool_failure.py lib/crewai/tests/telemetry/test_wharf_runner.py   # 204 passed on both
uv run ruff check lib/
uv run ruff format --check lib/
uv run mypy lib/   # Python 3.10 env from `uv sync --all-groups --all-extras`, as in CI: no issues found in 948 source files
```

End to end with a stdio FastMCP server through `Agent(mcps=[MCPServerStdio(...)])` (script in the issue), Python 3.10.19 and 3.13.16:

```text
before: RESULT three_blocks: 'first'
after:  RESULT three_blocks: 'first\nsecond\nthird'
before: RESULT chart: "type='image' data='iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAA' mimeType='image/png' annotations=None meta=None"
after:  RESULT chart: '[image: image/png]\nRevenue grew 12% in Q3.'
```

## Additional context

- Behavior change: a result whose only block is non-text used to return the block's repr (with base64 for images); it now returns the placeholder. An embedded text resource now returns its text instead of the repr. The same string is what `MCPClient.call_tool()` returns, what `MCPToolExecutionCompletedEvent.result` / `MCPToolExecutionFailedEvent.error` carry, and the `ToolFailure` message for `isError` results, so those no longer get the base64 repr either.
- `MCPServerAdapter` in crewai-tools is not changed here. It keeps all text blocks but returns them as a Python list repr, so the two integrations still format results differently. Aligning them would change the adapter's output, so I left it out to keep this PR small and can open a follow-up if you want them to match.
- Overlap with open PRs: #7643 edits the same lines in `MCPToolWrapper._execute_tool`; whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase (`content = content_blocks_to_text(result.content)`). #6744 already conflicts with main in `client.py`; this PR adds no new conflict hunks there, and the helper lives in `mcp/content.py` rather than the `mcp/_utils.py` that #6744 adds. #7448 and #7756 merge cleanly with this branch.
- Earlier attempt: #5226 fixed only the `MCPClient` copy and was closed for having no linked issue.
- AI disclosure: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) wrote the fix, the tests and this description, and ran the checks above. I reviewed the diff and the drafts, and Claude Code opened this PR on my behalf. Please add the `llm-generated` label; I don't have permission to add labels.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes agent-visible MCP tool output across all integration paths; behavior shifts for multi-block and non-text-first results, though scope is limited to result formatting.
> 
> **Overview**
> MCP tool results no longer expose only the first `content` block to agents. A shared **`content_blocks_to_text`** helper joins **all** blocks into one newline-separated string and replaces duplicated extraction in **`MCPClient`**, **`MCPNativeTool`**, and **`MCPToolWrapper`**.
> 
> **Text** and embedded text resources keep their text; **image, audio, blob, and link** blocks become short placeholders (e.g. `[image: image/png]`) without base64 payload. Single text-block results stay the same; non-text-only results change from pydantic reprs to placeholders. The same string flows through tool return values, MCP execution events, and error/`ToolFailure` messages.
> 
> Tests cover all three call paths plus direct helper behavior for mixed block types.
>

title: feat(cli): rewrite the scaffolded AGENTS.md and fail PRs that teach coding agents less
body:
The AGENTS.md that `crewai create` ships was 11K tokens of reference that coding agents mostly didn't act on: they rarely logged in, traced a run or ran `crewai eval`, and GPT models without CrewAI knowledge got a quarter of basic questions wrong with it. It is now a 5K-token working guide to building with CrewAI and AMP together (check the login, trace, evaluate with `crewai eval`, deploy), with the features it no longer details kept as a short index. A PR that changes it is now checked against main's file before it can teach agents less.

- Scope: `lib/cli/src/crewai_cli/templates/AGENTS.md` (crew, JSON crew and flow scaffolds), its guard tests in `lib/cli/tests/test_create_crew.py`, and `devtools agents-md-eval` with a 223-question bank.
- CI: `.github/workflows/agents-md.yml` (guards, on `pull_request`) and `agents-md-eval.yml` (eval, on `pull_request_target`, this repo's branches). Guards pin the required references, a 5,000-token budget, imports and docs paths; the eval asks Claude Code (Haiku, Sonnet) and Codex (gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol) every question with both files and fails on a drop over 10%. It runs the base branch's workflow and code and reads the PR's files as data, with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the `agents-md-eval` environment, so it first runs after this merges.
- Teaches `crewai eval` as it is on main since #8270: it runs and traces the crew itself, logged in or out, so agents don't stop to log in first.
- Compatibility: only newly scaffolded projects get the file; existing projects keep theirs. No public API change.
- Out: logged-out `crewai eval` inside Claude Code's sandbox (its handoff file lands outside the project, the write is refused) needs its own fix and a ticket; AMP's evaluation brief still says `crewai run` then `crewai eval`; the declarative-flow AGENTS.md is unchanged; no nightly behaviour runs or LLM-judge audit yet.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes what every newly scaffolded project tells coding agents and adds CI that spends API keys via pull_request_target; runtime APIs are unchanged but doc/CI regressions could block or mis-score template PRs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces the **`crewai create` AGENTS.md template** with a shorter, workflow-first guide (~5K token budget): session setup on AMP, **`crewai eval`** as definition of done, deploy cautions, and a compact **Reference** index instead of the old long API cookbook.
> 
> Adds **quality gates** for template edits: **`agents-md.yml`** runs pytest guards (required feature mentions, banned outdated advice, CLI command parsing, imports/docs links, token budget) and **`agents-md-eval.yml`** runs **`devtools agents-md-eval`** on PRs that touch the template—comparing base vs head with Claude Code and Codex against a **223-item question bank** (`agents_md_items.json`), failing if any model drops more than **10%**. Scaffold tests are updated to match the new copy and env var names (e.g. **`CREWAI_ENTERPRISE_ACTION_AUTH_TOKEN`**).

title: fix(cli): keep runtime input prompts on stderr
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8296


## Summary

`prompt_for_inputs` writes its headers to stderr but sends field prompts to stdout. A caller that prints the returned inputs as JSON therefore produces an unparseable stdout stream despite exiting successfully.

Pass `err=True` to Click and redirect stdout only during the prompt call. The redirect is needed on Windows because Click 8.4.2 passes the final prompt character to `input()` on stdout even with `err=True`. The context restores the caller's stdout on success or abort; value coercion and result output run outside it. This preserves the existing prompt text, styling and returned values. The redirection is process-wide during synchronous input collection, not thread-local.

Add three subprocess regressions using real Click: one field, multiple fields with integer coercion and non-ASCII text, and EOF abort. They assert exact result-only stdout, prompt text on stderr, and stdout restoration. One existing assertion is only reflowed by Ruff.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

Native Windows, Python 3.12.8, Click 8.4.2, dependencies from the current lockfile (`uv sync --locked --package crewai --group dev`). With the final regression file:

- Unchanged implementation: **3 failed, 8 passed**.
- Fixed input-prompt suite: **11 passed**.
- Existing JSON-crew input-resolution controls: **4 passed, 48 deselected**.

Run from the repo root with telemetry disabled:

```text
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest lib/cli/tests/test_input_prompt.py -q -n 0 -p no:randomly -p no:cacheprovider
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest lib/cli/tests/test_run_crew.py -k resolve_crew_inputs -q -n 0 -p no:randomly -p no:cacheprovider
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m ruff check --no-fix lib/cli/src/crewai_cli/input_prompt.py
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m ruff format --check --no-force-exclude lib/cli/src/crewai_cli/input_prompt.py lib/cli/tests/test_input_prompt.py
.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m mypy lib/cli/src/crewai_cli/input_prompt.py
git diff --check
```

Ruff source lint, formatting for both changed files, targeted mypy and whitespace checks pass. The repository's Ruff lint configuration excludes CLI tests, so source lint does not claim whole-test-file lint coverage.

No model/API calls, complete `crewai run` execution, full monorepo tests, terminal UI session, hosted CI or Linux/macOS validation is claimed. The subprocess tests exercise the shared helper's actual Click I/O, not the complete CLI's output contract.

## Additional context

This is independent of the custom-prompt BOM fix in #8260. No dependency or public signature changes.

AI assistance: Codex reviewed contribution rules and related work, reproduced the stream contamination and the Windows last-character behavior, prepared the patch/regressions, ran the checks, and drafted this description. Please apply `llm-generated`; this external account cannot add repository labels.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Scoped to CLI interactive prompting I/O routing with regression tests; no API or auth/data-path changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **stdout pollution** during interactive runtime input collection in `prompt_for_inputs`: field prompts now go to **stderr** (with `err=True` on `click.prompt`), matching headers and hints, so callers can print JSON results on stdout without mixing in prompt text.
> 
> On **Windows**, Click can still write the last prompt character to stdout even with `err=True`; the change wraps each `click.prompt` in **`redirect_stdout(sys.stderr)`** only for that call, then returns to normal stdout for coercion and caller output.
> 
> Adds **subprocess integration tests** that drive real Click prompts (single/multi field, coercion, non-ASCII, EOF abort) and assert prompt chrome on stderr and **result-only** stdout.

title: feat(flow): add opt-in per-turn conversation tracing
body:
## Related issue

Conversation tracing DX improvement; no linked issue.

## Summary

Conversational callers currently manage a session-wide trace with `defer_trace_finalization` and `finalize_session_traces()`. Add `ConversationConfig(trace_scope="turn")` so each `handle_turn()` or `stream_turn()` finishes its own trace while persisted history remains resumable under the same session ID.

- Propagate `gen_ai.conversation.id` across opted-in turn traces, including restored Flow instances and nested LLM work. Hosts can supply their durable public conversation ID through the existing telemetry attributes hook.
- Preserve existing defaults, legacy deferral flags, trace grouping, and LLM correlation values when the new scope is omitted. Existing `finalize_session_traces()` calls remain supported and are safe no-ops in turn scope. An explicit scope takes precedence over the legacy flag.
- Document the TUI, direct-call, streaming, export, consent, and compatibility lifecycles; sync Arabic, Korean, and Portuguese translations.

- Return pending human feedback without emitting `conversation_turn_completed`; keep the existing linked HITL segments under the same execution UUID and document that pause boundary.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally
- Tracing, Enterprise compatibility, conversational Flow, declarative Flow, and shim suites: **969 passed, 1 skipped**.
- TUI conversation checks: **2 passed**.
- Ruff lint/format, mypy, commit hooks, and `git diff --check` passed; Python/YAML documentation examples parse in all four locales.
- Live local Plus/Wharf check: restored a persisted conversation in a fresh Python process, appended another turn with `trace_scope="turn"`, and verified all spans completed `OK` with the same conversation ID.

- HITL follow-up: tracing, conversational Flow, and human-feedback suites covered **886 passing cases, 1 skipped**; the two optional-provider cases passed after installing the locked Anthropic SDK.

## Additional context

This is an additive opt-in, not a default switch or a deprecation. Scope resolves independently of persistence: completing a turn's trace does not end its conversation. Enterprise still needs to adopt the SDK option and forward its stable public conversation ID; Plus/Wharf conversation grouping is separate work.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes conversational tracing lifecycle and OpenTelemetry attributes when `trace_scope="turn"` is enabled; defaults are unchanged but telemetry consumers and Enterprise hosts must understand per-turn export and `gen_ai.conversation.id` grouping.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds an **opt-in** `ConversationConfig(trace_scope="turn")` (and declarative `conversational.trace_scope`) so each `handle_turn()` / `stream_turn()` closes its own trace while chat history stays resumable on the same `session_id`. Omitting `trace_scope` keeps today’s deferred session batch and `finalize_session_traces()` behavior.
> 
> **Runtime:** `_should_defer_trace_finalization()` honors explicit `"turn"` vs `"session"` over `defer_trace_finalization`. Turn-scoped flows stamp spans with **`gen_ai.conversation.id`** (session id or host override via `telemetry_session` attributes). `handle_turn` / `stream_turn` can return **`HumanFeedbackPending`** without completing the turn trace semantics documented for HITL.
> 
> **Docs:** English, Arabic, Korean, and Portuguese conversational-flow guides now center turn-scoped examples (no mandatory `finalize_session_traces()` in snippets) and expand tracing lifecycle, export, TUI/streaming, and compatibility notes.
> 
> **Tests:** New coverage for per-turn finish/resume, failures, HITL pause/resume linking, host conversation id, and unchanged legacy session tracing.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7559ba0795a4983f10274b959c3d25b9b01b216d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(llms): use auto tool choice for a single Anthropic tool
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8233

## Summary

A single tool plus `available_functions` made the Anthropic provider send `tool_choice: {"type": "tool", "name": ...}`. That forces the model to call the tool. `available_functions` only means CrewAI can execute the tool, and Claude Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, and Mythos 5.1 reject that forced choice with a 400.

This path now sends `tool_choice: {"type": "auto"}` for every model. The tool stays in the request, and the model can call it or answer in text. Structured-output calls that force the `structured_output` tool are unchanged.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

`test_single_tool_with_available_functions_uses_auto_choice` and `test_tool_search_single_tool_skips_search_and_uses_auto_choice` passed. Pre-commit (ruff, ruff-format, mypy) passed.

## Additional context

#8234 and #8241 fix the same 400 with a model denylist and keep forcing the tool on older Claude models. This drops the force entirely, so new models that reject named `tool_choice` do not need another denylist entry.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes default Anthropic tool-calling behavior for single-tool + available_functions across all models (models may skip the tool and answer in text), though it fixes API failures on newer Claude versions.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes Anthropic API **400 errors** on newer Claude models when CrewAI sent a **forced named** `tool_choice` for the common case of **one agent tool** plus `available_functions`.
> 
> **`_prepare_completion_params`** no longer sets `tool_choice` to `{"type": "tool", "name": ...}` in that scenario. It now sends **`{"type": "auto"}`** so the tool stays available but the model can call it or reply in plain text—matching that `available_functions` only means CrewAI can execute the tool, not that the model must use it. Comments note rejection on Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, and Mythos 5.1. **Structured-output** paths that force the `structured_output` tool are **unchanged**.
> 
> Tests were renamed/updated for single-tool + `tool_search`, and **`test_single_tool_with_available_functions_uses_auto_choice`** was added for Claude Sonnet 5.5.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit adcb8cc17a0b9977d9f2657b9b38c9e69e2a2e59. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: Fix JSONLoader escaping non-ASCII text when rendering JSON documents
body:
Fixes #8276

## Description

JSONLoader renders parsed JSON back to text with json.dumps, which escapes every non-ASCII character as a \uXXXX sequence by default (ensure_ascii=True). RAG documents loaded from JSON containing accents, CJK text, or emoji come out unreadable, and that escaped text is what gets embedded and sent to the model.

## Root Cause

The three json.dumps calls in JSONLoader._parse_json rely on the default ensure_ascii=True, so characters outside ASCII are rendered as escape sequences instead of the original text.

## Changes

- Pass ensure_ascii=False to the three json.dumps calls in lib/crewai-tools/src/crewai_tools/rag/loaders/json_loader.py (dict, list, and scalar branches).
- Update test_json_loader_bom.py: an internal BOM now survives as a real character instead of an escaped sequence.
- Add tests/rag/test_json_loader_unicode.py covering dict and list payloads with accented and CJK text, asserting the readable characters are preserved and no \u escape sequences appear.

## Verification

- The new unicode tests fail on current main and pass with this change.
- The updated BOM test passes.
- The full lib/crewai-tools rag test suite passes locally (149 tests).

Per the contributing guide, this PR was prepared with AI assistance. Please apply the llm-generated label, since I cannot set labels as an outside contributor.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized change to JSON text serialization in the RAG loader with added tests; no auth, security, or API surface changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> **JSONLoader** now renders parsed JSON back to text with readable Unicode instead of `\uXXXX` escapes, so RAG documents from JSON with accents, CJK, or emoji embed human-readable content.
> 
> `_parse_json` passes **`ensure_ascii=False`** on all `json.dumps` paths (dict, list, scalar), then normalizes output with a UTF-8 **`backslashreplace`** round-trip so lone surrogate escapes stay safe while valid Unicode (including emoji from surrogate pairs) stays readable.
> 
> Tests were updated for an internal BOM appearing as a real `\ufeff` character, and new coverage asserts non-ASCII preservation plus lone vs paired surrogate behavior.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit de043990d626b94da1302126f27bfffe099ba6b6. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: refactor(llm): make context compaction a BaseLLM capability
body:
## Summary

Make context compaction available through `BaseLLM.summarize_messages`, route all runtime triggers through that method, and reduce the compaction implementation to a direct, token-budgeted chunk-and-summarize flow.

## Commits

- `b0362d69f` adds the `BaseLLM` context-compaction entry point.
- `e208e1f8d` moves compaction helpers into the LLM context-window module.
- `0a98536a0` uses the active LLM token estimator for summary chunks.
- `a93a4ad8f` removes the legacy stateful message summarizer.
- `dd0bbb3e7` removes the old summarization wrapper.
- `07832e57c` migrates summarization coverage to the new entry point.
- `43f173d21` shares safe multimodal message-text handling.
- `72ccd9c7f` adjusts the former compaction retry budget.
- `837379d5f` adds the initial chunk-planning implementation.
- `e4b497232` simplifies compaction planning and caps parallel summary calls at four.
- `1669b20e8` centralizes message rendering helpers.
- `67b997e3e` moves shared compaction message helpers into `message_utils`.
- `7c858c4ca` removes tool-call grouping from chunking.
- `6425b9efd` replaces binary-search splitting with proportional splitting.
- `6ae00bbe2` shares the summary-prompt builder through `message_utils`.
- `525f04e02` partitions system and work messages in one pass.
- `ebb408ca3` clarifies the single-message chunking flow.
- `ba7dcfd5c` uses a conservative 75% message-split budget.
- `033edd92e` removes nested summary compaction.
- `451b63c07` removes the summary retry heuristic.

## Verification

- [x] `uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/llms/test_context_window.py -q`
- [x] Ruff, formatting, mypy, and diff checks

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Compaction logic was rewritten and moved off agent_utils; behavior changes (token-based chunking, no char-per-token retry ladder) could affect long conversations and custom LLMs that lack accurate token counting.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Context compaction** is now a **`BaseLLM.summarize_messages`** capability; preflight and overflow paths in `agent_utils` call **`llm.summarize_messages`** instead of the removed **`SummarizeMessages`** class and standalone **`summarize_messages`** helper.
> 
> The new flow lives in **`llms/context_window.py`**: preserve system messages and user attachments, **chunk** history using the active model’s **`get_input_tokens_count`** on the real summary prompt, **split** oversized text with a **75%** budget, summarize chunks **in parallel (max 4)**, and replace non-system history with one summary message. Shared rendering moves to **`utilities/message_utils.py`** (`message_content_text`, `format_message_for_llm`, `build_summary_prompt`, etc.), with imports updated across agents, executor, and LLM code.
> 
> **Verbose compaction** panels now show **token counts** before and after (and % reduction). Tests shift to **`test_context_window.py`** and **`patch.object(llm, "summarize_messages")`**; large legacy summarizer suites are dropped or trimmed from integration tests.
>
