title: feat(tools): add Azure DocumentDB vector search integration
body:
## Related issue

Fixes crewAIInc/crewAI#7302


## Summary

Adds a dedicated Azure DocumentDB integration so CrewAI agents can retrieve documents without custom database retrieval code or MongoDB Atlas-specific assumptions.

- Introduces `AzureDocumentDBVectorSearchTool`, `AzureDocumentDBVectorSearchConfig`, and `AzureDocumentDBToolSchema`.
- Implements native vector search using `$search.cosmosSearch`, with configurable result limits, metadata filters, similarity scores, and embedding output.
- Supports batched document ingestion with metadata, generated or supplied IDs, and OpenAI/Azure OpenAI embeddings.
- Provides an explicit IVF index creation helper.
- Adds renewable Microsoft Entra ID authentication for DocumentDB and Azure OpenAI, including credential injection and automatic token renewal.
- Adds the `azure-documentdb` optional dependency, public exports, tool metadata, and lockfile updates.
- Documents resource setup, authentication, indexing, ingestion, CrewAI Agent usage, and local/live testing.
- Leaves the existing MongoDB integration unchanged.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

### Automated tests

With local Podman and live Azure test environment variables configured, the following command passed: **52 tests passed**.

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest lib\crewai-tools\tests\tools\test_azure_documentdb_vector_search_tool.py lib\crewai-tools\tests\tools\test_azure_documentdb_vector_search_e2e.py lib\crewai-tools\tests\tools\test_mongodb_vector_search_tool.py lib\crewai-tools\tests\test_generate_tool_specs.py -o addopts='' -n 0 -q --tb=short
```

Coverage includes:
- Configuration and input validation, batching, IDs, metadata, and JSON serialization.
- Entra token callbacks, token renewal, credential ownership, and error propagation.
- Existing MongoDB behavior and tool specification discovery.
- Two E2E tests against the official DocumentDB local image running in Podman.
- A live E2E test against Azure DocumentDB and Azure OpenAI using Entra ID authentication.

Live testing verified real `text-embedding-3-small` embeddings with API version `2023-05-15`, document ingestion, IVF indexing, ranked retrieval, metadata filtering, and score/embedding output. 

### Quality checks

Each command below passed:

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\ruff.exe check lib\crewai-tools\src\crewai_tools\tools\azure_documentdb_vector_search_tool
.venv\Scripts\ruff.exe check --no-force-exclude lib\crewai-tools\tests\tools\test_azure_documentdb_vector_search_tool.py lib\crewai-tools\tests\tools\test_azure_documentdb_vector_search_e2e.py
.venv\Scripts\ruff.exe format --check lib\crewai-tools\src\crewai_tools\tools\azure_documentdb_vector_search_tool
.venv\Scripts\ruff.exe format --check --no-force-exclude lib\crewai-tools\tests\tools\test_azure_documentdb_vector_search_tool.py lib\crewai-tools\tests\tools\test_azure_documentdb_vector_search_e2e.py
.venv\Scripts\mypy.exe --follow-imports=silent lib\crewai-tools\src\crewai_tools\tools\azure_documentdb_vector_search_tool
uv lock --check --offline --python 3.12
git diff --check
```

Also verified that the public package imports without the optional PyMongo and Azure Identity dependencies installed.

The full repository suite and Python-version matrix were not run locally; these remain for CI.

## Additional context

- Install with `pip install "crewai-tools[azure-documentdb]"`.
- Index creation is explicit; the tool does not automatically drop or rebuild existing indexes.
- Local and live E2E tests are opt-in and skipped unless their connection environment variables are configured.
- Podman test containers and the temporary forwarding tunnel were removed after verification.
- No credentials or resource-specific endpoints are committed.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> New optional integration touches external databases, embeddings, and Entra/OIDC auth, but it is additive with broad test coverage and no changes to existing MongoDB behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`AzureDocumentDBVectorSearchTool`** so agents can ingest and query Azure DocumentDB with native **`$search.cosmosSearch`** vector search (not MongoDB Atlas `$vectorSearch`). Install via **`crewai-tools[azure-documentdb]`** (`pymongo`, `azure-identity`).
> 
> The tool embeds with OpenAI or Azure OpenAI, supports batched **`add_texts`**, explicit IVF index creation, configurable limits/metadata filters, and JSON results with optional scores or embeddings. **Microsoft Entra ID** is supported for DocumentDB OIDC connections and keyless Azure OpenAI via injectable or auto-created credentials.
>

title: feat(flow): add exact historical state lookup by row id
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8139

## Summary

`SQLiteFlowPersistence` keeps every saved state in the `flow_states` table, but `load_state` only returns the latest one, so there is no way to read an earlier snapshot. This PR adds a read-only lookup that returns one historical state by its row id, scoped to its flow UUID.

- Adds `SQLiteFlowPersistence.load_state_from_history(flow_uuid, record_id)`, which returns `dict[str, Any] | None` like `load_state`.
- The query matches on both the row id and the flow UUID with bound parameters, so a row saved by another flow is never returned.
- It follows the connection handling and JSON decoding of `load_state` and leaves `load_state` unchanged. A missing row returns None, and so does a stored state that is not a JSON object, as in `load_state`.
- The method is SQLite only. I did not add it to the `FlowPersistence` base class, so custom persistence backends are unaffected.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

Four tests in `lib/crewai/tests/test_flow_persistence.py` cover the acceptance criteria. They check that a lookup returns the exact nested state of an older row rather than the latest one, that a missing row id or unknown flow UUID returns None, that interleaved saves from two flows never resolve under the other flow's UUID, and that `load_state` still returns the latest state after a lookup. The tests write states through `save_state` and read row ids with a small SQL helper, since there is no public API for row ids on main yet.

```bash
uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/ -x -q
```

The full suite passed with 6151 passed and 44 skipped. I wrote each test before the code it covers and saw it fail first. For the tests that passed once the method existed, I broke the code on purpose to confirm they catch the bug: dropping the id condition, dropping the flow UUID condition, and making the lookup save a new row each made the matching test fail.

`ruff check lib/`, `ruff format --check lib/` and `mypy lib/` pass. On Python 3.10, the persistence tests and mypy on `flow/persistence` also pass.

## Additional context

This builds on main independently of #8253, which implements the history listing from #8138. The row id here is the same value as the `id` field of that PR's `FlowStateHistoryRecord`, so a caller can list the history and then look up a row. The method is SQLite only and has no read-only module-level variant like `read_flow_state_history`. Either could follow once #8253 settles if that is useful for the CLI in #8140. I left out docs because the current docs do not cover `load_state` either.

`record_id` is not validated beyond its type hint. Any id that does not exist for the flow returns None.

Happy to adjust the name or scope. This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude Code), and I reviewed and tested every change. Could a maintainer please add the `llm-generated` label?

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Isolated SQLite read path with parameterized queries; no changes to save paths, base persistence API, or latest-state loading.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`SQLiteFlowPersistence.load_state_from_history(flow_uuid, record_id)`**, a read-only API to fetch a specific earlier snapshot from `flow_states` by table row id (not the flow’s latest via `load_state`). Lookups require both row id and flow UUID; missing or mismatched rows return `None`, and non-object JSON is treated like `load_state`. **`load_state` is unchanged** and the method is **not** added to the `FlowPersistence` base class.
>

title: feat(cli): crewai eval runs the crew itself, so a coding agent gets a verdict from one command
body:
## Why

Most `crewai eval` attempts stop before an evaluation begins, because the project has no traced run. From the feature-usage telemetry since Sept 25 (two test-suite "projects" left out):
- **117 projects** stopped as "untraced" at least once;
- **97 of them had no terminal**, mostly coding agents (37 under Claude Code, 60 under an agent or script it couldn't name);
- **67 of those 99 no-terminal projects never got any further**, 31 hit the same stop again, and only 8 later started an evaluation from `crewai eval`.

With no terminal the command could only print three steps: set `CREWAI_TRACING_ENABLED=true`, `crewai run`, `crewai eval`. Without a login those steps couldn't work, because an unattended anonymous run never uploads its trace. And after an agent edited the crew, `crewai eval` graded the old run.

## What changes

**`crewai eval` runs the crew when there's nothing current to grade.**
- **When:** there is no traced run, or the project's files changed since the last one. The command then runs the crew and evaluates that run.
- **Running the command is the request.** The grade is read off the run's trace, so once tracing is on nothing more is asked. The command says what it's doing in one line: "No traced run of this crew yet: running it now to evaluate it."
- **Tracing is turned on once.** If nobody has turned tracing on (no `CREWAI_TRACING_ENABLED=true`, no stored consent), the first such evaluation turns it on for the project by writing `CREWAI_TRACING_ENABLED=true` to `.env` and setting it for the run. After that the project traces, and nothing more is asked or said.
  - **at a terminal,** the person is asked first, on crewAI's existing trace consent screen (`prompt_user_for_trace_viewing(sharing=True)`: "Share this execution trace with CrewAI? [y/N]", 20 s). A yes turns tracing on and runs the crew; a no, or no answer in time, runs nothing (exit 0, `eval_stopped:declined`);
  - **with no terminal** (a coding agent, a script), the yes is taken from the command and tracing is turned on with one calm sentence: "Tracing is now on for this project: its runs' traces are sent to CrewAI AMP, which grades them." The sentence also shows in the run app.
- **Never toward an AMP the command doesn't trust.** The crew runs only when its trace would go to an AMP this machine is set up for: an origin trusted before the project's `.env` was loaded, over HTTPS or loopback. Toward any other AMP, the crew isn't run, nobody is asked, nothing is written, and the command stops with `eval_stopped:untrusted_amp`, saying to set that AMP up (`crewai enterprise configure <url>`) or remove `CREWAI_PLUS_URL`. This holds whatever the tracing setting and whether or not the machine is logged in yet:
  - a project's crewai older than the handshake sends this machine's login to whatever AMP its `.env` names whenever the run traces, `tracing=True` in code included, which the CLI can't see;
  - tracing turned on toward that AMP before any login exists would carry the login there on the first run after `crewai login`.
- **Except when the project turned tracing off** (`CREWAI_TRACING_ENABLED=false` or `0`, in its `.env` or the environment). That's the project's no, and nothing overrules it:
  - **at a terminal,** the command asks to turn tracing on. A yes writes `CREWAI_TRACING_ENABLED=true` to `.env` and runs the crew; a no runs nothing (exit 0, `eval_stopped:declined`);
  - **with no terminal,** it stops and says how to turn it on (exit 1, `eval_stopped:tracing_off`), which a coding agent can then do itself.
- **"Changed" means** a file under the project modified more than 60 s after the last run's record. Files written in that minute count as the run's own (e.g. a `main.py` that saves the result after the crew returns). Ignored:
  - hidden folders (`.venv`, `.git`, `.crewai`, caches), but `.env` counts;
  - `__pycache__`, `node_modules`, `venv`/`env`, `build`/`dist`, `*.egg-info`, `*.pyc`, `*.log`;
  - `crewai-eval-*` export folders and `eval.jsonc`, which the evaluation writes.

  A record with no timestamp is graded as it is. `--run ID` never runs the crew.
- **Deleted files count too.** Each evaluation keeps the list of the project's files (`.crewai/eval_project_state.json`, path, mtime and size), and the next one compares against it, so an added, removed or rewritten file is a change. The list is taken after the command's own `project_id` write, so that write is never seen as an edit. A run recorded by a plain `crewai run` that no evaluation has seen uses the mtime rule above.

**crewAI approves the upload of that one run (`crewai_core.eval_handshake`).**
- This reuses the run app's existing handshake. A random token goes in `CREWAI_EVAL_AWAITING_RUN`, and it counts only while a file of that name exists in the user's crewAI data folder. A project's `.env` can set the variable but can't create the file, so it can't claim the approval; a test pins that. On POSIX that folder comes from the account's home in the account database, never `HOME` or `XDG_DATA_HOME`, so a `.env` can't redirect it either.
- **The saved login only goes to an AMP `crewai eval` trusted.** The token file also carries the AMP origins the command trusted before loading the project's `.env`. For a run the command started, the saved login goes only to one of those, over HTTPS or loopback; an AMP the `.env` chose gets an anonymous grant.
  - Evaluate's re-run passes this machine's AMPs, because its process has already loaded the `.env`.
  - Every path that loads a project's `.env` (`run_crew.load_project_env`) keeps the token the process started with, and never takes one from the `.env`.
- `tracing_asked_for()` and `should_enable_tracing()` treat an awaited run as asked for. An explicit `CREWAI_TRACING_ENABLED=false` is checked first and still wins, as does `tracing=False` in code.
- The run app keeps its own copy of the variable's name and the folder rather than importing them, because the JSON crew runner runs this CLI's code against a project's crewai-core, which may be older. A test pins the two copies to the same values.

**The run app's Evaluate on an untraced run** closes the app and runs the crew again, traced, through `crewai eval`'s own path (`run_crew._chain_traced_rerun`), instead of the "turn tracing on" notice. If tracing isn't on yet, a modal asks first: the app's trace consent screen (`TraceConsentScreen`) when nobody ever turned it on, `TurnTracingOnScreen` when the project turned it off. A yes turns it on in `.env` and runs again; a no leaves everything as it was. Toward an untrusted AMP, nothing is asked or written: the app says why and stays open.
- **The re-run is the run that was watched.** It carries that run's definition, the inputs it used (prompted ones included) and its trained-agents file. Conversational flows handle Evaluate the same way.
- **`tracing=False` on the crew or flow:** Evaluate says why the run can't be evaluated and runs nothing, and the app never says the trace is sent.

**`OTEL_SDK_DISABLED` no longer turns tracing off.** It's the telemetry opt-out, a separate setting; tracing has its own (`CREWAI_TRACING_ENABLED`, `tracing=`).
- `execution._tracing_disabled` no longer reads it.
- The trace session's own `TracerProvider` records even with the OpenTelemetry SDK switched off (`session._trace_provider`). Without this, the SDK hands out tracers that record nothing. A provider a host passes in is left alone.
- Two existing tests used it as a way to stop a trace; they now cover the real switches.
- The telemetry docs (en, ar, ko, pt-BR) say so: it disables OpenTelemetry instrumentation and CrewAI's telemetry, not AMP tracing.

**Usage counts:**
- `eval_ran_crew:{no_traced_run,project_changed,run_again}` — why the crew ran;
- `eval_finished:{passed,failed,inconclusive,unknown}` — so "reached a result" is counted, not inferred;
- `eval_stopped:untraced_after_run` replaces the catch-all `untraced`, and `eval_stopped:tracing_off` / `declined` count a project that turned tracing off.

The CLI tests also stop sending usage counts: two test-suite "projects" had put 344 `untraced` events into the real data.

## Tests

- **`test_eval_crew.py`:**
  - a coding agent with no terminal, logged in or not, gets its verdict from `crewai eval` alone: the crew runs traced and approved, no `.env` is written, and the run is graded;
  - at a terminal, tracing is turned on only after a yes on the consent screen, a no runs nothing, and a project already tracing isn't asked; after a yes, the run app evaluates without another question;
  - with no terminal, tracing is turned on with the note, and the consent screen is never shown;
  - a changed project re-runs (five kinds of change);
  - what tools leave around the project is no change (ten kinds);
  - the 60 s window, a record with no timestamp, and `run_again`;
  - tracing is turned back off after the run;
  - a project that turned tracing off is asked first at a terminal (yes turns it on, no runs nothing) and told how with no terminal;
  - what counts as turned off (`.env` over the environment);
  - each new count.
- **`test_crew_run_tui.py`:**
  - Evaluate on an untraced run closes the app and asks for the re-run when tracing is on, and asks first on the right screen when it was never turned on or was turned off;
  - an awaited run is approved with no screen;
  - the run app's token is the one crewAI's tracing reads.
- **`test_run_crew.py` / `test_run_declarative_flow.py`:** the app's hand-off calls `eval_crew(run_again=True)`.
- **`test_deferred_trace_transitions.py`:**
  - a run `crewai eval` started uploads with no terminal, under test, or with messages suppressed;
  - an explicit `CREWAI_TRACING_ENABLED=false` keeps even that run untraced;
  - with `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true` a traced run, anonymous or logged in, is still recorded and uploaded, and the session's provider records spans;
  - the variable alone, as a `.env` could set it, uploads nothing.
- **`crewai-core` `test_eval_handshake.py`.**

Results:
- the touched CLI test files pass;
- `lib/crewai`, the whole suite: 6143 passed. The 10 failures (checkpoint and SQLite tests) are the same on `main`;
- `crewai-core`: 97 passed;
- ruff, ruff format and mypy are clean.

Some CLI tests fail locally with and without this change: the same 38, most of them because `lancedb` isn't installed here, plus `test_create_crew` ×4, `test_run_crew` ×2 and `tools/test_main` ×4. This PR doesn't touch them. Two run-app tests from #7963 used to leave `.crewai/last_eval.json` in the repo; they now run in their own folder.

## Not in this PR

- A project whose crewAI predates the version that records runs for evaluation still ends at "its trace did not reach CrewAI AMP"; the message now says that may be why.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes authentication/tracing upload rules, `.env` loading, and when credentials are sent to AMP—security-sensitive—but with explicit trust checks and extensive tests; behavioral shift for `crewai eval` and `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED` users.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`crewai eval` is now a one-shot path from “no traced run” to an AMP verdict**, especially for headless coding agents. When there is nothing current to grade (no last traced run, project files changed since the last evaluation, or the TUI’s Evaluate on an untraced run), the CLI runs the crew first, enables tracing when needed, and grades that run—running the command counts as consent to trace/upload in non-interactive mode; at a terminal, the existing trace consent screen or a click confirm applies first.
> 
> **New `crewai_core.eval_handshake`** ties CLI and runtime: a short-lived token file (not forgeable via `.env`) marks eval-started runs, carries trusted AMP origins decided before project `.env` load, and lets tracing skip interactive prompts while still respecting `CREWAI_TRACING_ENABLED=false` and `tracing=False`. **`load_project_env`** preserves the eval token; untrusted `CREWAI_PLUS_URL` blocks running/turning tracing on toward that AMP.
> 
> **Tracing vs telemetry:** `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED` no longer disables AMP tracing (`CREWAI_TRACING_ENABLED` / `tracing=` instead); trace sessions use a provider that can record despite the SDK global disable. Docs (en/ar/ko/pt-BR) clarify this split.
> 
> **TUI:** Evaluate on untraced runs prompts to turn tracing on (or reuses consent), then chains `_chain_traced_rerun` → `eval_crew(run_again=True)` with the same definition/inputs. Expanded telemetry stop/finish reasons and broad test coverage.
>

title: fix: treat checkpoint paths literally in glob patterns
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8268

## Summary

`JsonProvider.prune()` and the checkpoint CLI passed the checkpoint location (and branch) to `glob.glob()` as part of the pattern, so glob characters in the path selected a different directory. For `runs[1]`, pruning deleted the checkpoints in `runs1` and kept its own.

This escapes the directory part with `glob.escape()` in `JsonProvider.prune()` and in the five JSON patterns of `crewai_cli/checkpoint_cli.py` (list, info for the latest checkpoint and by ID, prune, and the prune dry run). The `*.json` and `**/*.json` parts are still patterns, so paths without glob characters work as before.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

- `test_prune_treats_directory_and_branch_as_literal_paths` in `lib/crewai/tests/test_checkpoint.py` covers brackets in the location, the branch and a nested branch, with `max_keep` 0 and 1 (6 cases).
- `test_json_location_with_glob_characters` and `test_location_with_glob_characters` in `lib/crewai/tests/test_checkpoint_cli.py` cover list, info, prune and the prune dry run.
- The new tests fail on `main` and pass with this change. `lib/crewai/tests/test_checkpoint.py` and `lib/crewai/tests/test_checkpoint_cli.py`: 99 passed on `main`, 107 passed with this change. To keep my local credentials and telemetry out of the run, I mocked the auth token lookup and disabled telemetry.
- The checkpoint tests in `lib/cli/tests` (`test_checkpoint_telemetry.py`, `test_model_catalog.py`): 65 passed.
- I also ran `crewai checkpoint list`, `prune --dry-run` and `prune` on a `runs[1]` directory next to `runs1`: with this change, they only read and delete the checkpoints in `runs[1]`.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` on the changed source files: passed. I did not run the full test suite.

## Additional context

This PR was prepared with AI assistance. I can't add labels, so could a maintainer please add `llm-generated`?

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Prune and CLI glob behavior changes for paths with `[]`, `*`, or `?`; fixes wrong-directory deletes but could affect anyone relying on accidental glob matching.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes incorrect checkpoint discovery and deletion when checkpoint **location** or **branch** paths contain glob metacharacters (e.g. `runs[1]`).
> 
> **`JsonProvider.prune()`** and the checkpoint CLI JSON helpers now wrap the directory segment with **`glob.escape()`** before calling `glob.glob()`, while `**/*.json` / `*.json` remain wildcards. That stops paths like `runs[1]` from matching sibling `runs1` during list, info (latest and by ID), prune, and prune dry-run.

> Adds regression tests for bracket-heavy locations/branches in **`test_checkpoint.py`** and **`test_checkpoint_cli.py`**.

title: fix(logging): restore configured logger level on exit and errors (#8214)
body:
## Description
Closes #8214.

### Problem
`suppress_logging()` did not restore a logger's configured level if an exception was raised inside the context block. Furthermore, using `getEffectiveLevel()` incorrectly converted `NOTSET` (0) to the effective parent level, permanently severing parent inheritance upon exit.

### Changes
1. Save `logger.level` rather than `logger.getEffectiveLevel()` to preserve `NOTSET` inheritance.
2. Wrap execution and stdout/stderr redirection in a `try...finally` block to ensure the original configured level is restored on all exits, errors, and interruptions.
3. Added unit tests in `lib/crewai/tests/test_logger_utils.py` verifying level restoration on exceptions and `NOTSET` inheritance preservation.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Small, localized change to a logging utility with new unit tests; no auth, data, or security surface.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`suppress_logging()`** so logger configuration is always restored after the context exits, including when ChromaDB (or other wrapped code) raises inside the block.
> 
> **Restoration logic:** saves **`logger.level`** instead of **`getEffectiveLevel()`**, so a child logger left at **`NOTSET`** is put back correctly and keeps inheriting from its parent instead of being stuck at the parent’s effective level.
> 
> **Safety:** wraps the redirect/suppress block in **`try`/`finally`** so **`setLevel(original_level)`** runs on normal exit, exceptions, and interruptions.
> 
> Adds **`test_logger_utils.py`** with tests for level restore on exception and **`NOTSET`** inheritance after exit.
>

title: fix(cli): run JSON crews headless when there is no terminal
body:
`crewai run` on a JSON crew, the default `crewai create crew` project, always opened the interactive run screen unless `CREWAI_DMN` was set. Without a terminal (a coding agent's shell, CI, piped input) the screen stayed open after the crew finished, so the command never exited. JSON crews now follow the rule declarative flows already use: the screen opens only in an interactive terminal, and otherwise the crew runs on plain output and the command exits.

- Scope: `_run_json_crew` gates the screen on `is_interactive()` (stdin is a terminal and `CREWAI_DMN` is unset) instead of on `CREWAI_DMN` alone.
- Unchanged: an interactive terminal still gets the screen, and `CREWAI_DMN` still forces the plain run.
- Tests: with no terminal the crew runs plain, prints its result, and the screen never starts (this fails on main). A terminal still opens the screen; the existing screen tests now simulate one. End to end, `crewai run < /dev/null` on a scaffolded JSON crew exits 0 in 28 s, and hangs until killed on main.
- Found by the AGENTS.md eval: coding agents running a JSON crew with either AGENTS.md had to kill `crewai run`, or read results with `crewai log-tasks-outputs`.
- Out: Python conversational flows (`_run_conversational_flow_tui`) still open the chat screen without a terminal check. Needs a ticket.

title: Fix suppress_logging not restoring logger level
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8214

## Summary

`suppress_logging()` never restored the logger level when the body raised (missing `try/finally`), and it saved `getEffectiveLevel()` instead of `logger.level`, so a `NOTSET` logger stopped inheriting its parent's level after the context exited.

title: fix(llms): skip forced tool choice on claude models that reject it
body:
Claude Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 reject tool_choice "tool"/"any" with a 400. The Anthropic provider forced the tool when a call had exactly one tool and available_functions, which broke crewai chat and the reasoning step on those models. Leave tool_choice unset for them so the API applies "auto"; every other model sends the same request as before.

## Related issue

Fixes #8233 

## Summary

Claude Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 reject a forced `tool_choice`
("tool"/"any") with a 400. The Anthropic provider forces the tool when a call has exactly
one tool plus `available_functions`, which `crewai chat` and the reasoning step do.

`_supports_forced_tool_choice` is a denylist of those models, matched as substrings like
`_supports_native_structured_outputs`. For them, `tool_choice` is left unset so the API
applies "auto". Every other model sends an identical request, and token counting follows
the same params. The agent loop never passes `available_functions`, so normal crew runs
are unaffected.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

New tests: single tool not forced on the four models, still forced on `claude-sonnet-5`,
and Sonnet/Opus 5.5 added to the native structured-output tests. The new tests fail with
the fix reverted. `tests/llms/anthropic` + `tests/agents/test_agent_reasoning.py`: 140
passed; pre-commit (ruff, ruff-format, mypy) clean.

## Additional context

Bedrock has the same restriction on its forced `structured_output` tool; that is covered
by #7726, so this PR leaves the Bedrock provider untouched.

**Disclosure:** This PR utilized LLMs for review and linting as well as ideation for test coverage. I can't apply labels from a fork so could a maintainer please add it? I scoped the change, checked it against open PRs (Bedrock fix for similar change is left to #7726) and ran the tests myself.

title: feat: add offline jev routing and guardrail evaluation runner
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8124

## Summary

Adds an offline evaluation runner for TypeSafe Jev routing (Choice) and guardrail (Noul) decisions at `scripts/jev_evaluation_runner.py`, next to the other runners in `scripts/` (moved there per review).

- `load_dataset(path)` loads labeled records from `.jsonl` or `.json`. Errors name the line or index of the bad record.
- `evaluate(records, min_confidence=..., noul_threshold=...)` classifies each record as decided, abstained or failed and returns a pydantic report:
  - routing accuracy (correct ÷ all route records), coverage and abstention rate;
  - guardrail false accepts and false rejects, each with its denominator;
  - recorded token usage and latency, summed or averaged only over the records that report them;
  - each record's outcome and the reason for it.
- `collect_live_decisions(records, client=...)` is the opt-in live mode. The caller passes a TypeSafe client created with their own credentials. Each successful call is timed; client errors and malformed answers (wrong answer type, bad usage or probabilities) are stored on the record as failures instead of stopping the run.
- Offline mode runs from the command line and prints the report as JSON; invalid input exits with a usage error:

```bash
uv run python scripts/jev_evaluation_runner.py data.jsonl --min-confidence 0.7 --noul-threshold 0.8
```

Usage, the dataset format and the metric definitions are in the script's docstring.

Semantics:
- Failed records (missing, malformed or errored decisions) are never counted as correct or accepted, and are left out of the false-accept and false-reject denominators. These are decision-quality metrics, not a replay of a runtime guardrail that rejects on failure.
- Both thresholds are inclusive (`>=`).
- Choice confidence and Noul probability are separate fields and are never converted into each other.
- Missing token counts stay missing instead of becoming 0.

No changes to existing code, `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`. The script doesn't import `typesafe_sdk`; live questions use the SDK's dict form.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

```bash
uv run ruff check lib/ scripts/jev_evaluation_runner.py
uv run ruff format --check scripts/jev_evaluation_runner.py lib/crewai/tests/test_jev_evaluation_runner.py
uv run mypy scripts/jev_evaluation_runner.py
cd lib/crewai && uv run pytest tests/test_jev_evaluation_runner.py -q  # 68 passed on Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13
```

The tests load the script by path, the same way `test_wharf_runner.py` does. They cover metric denominators, threshold boundaries (below, equal and above), missing and invalid decisions, invalid inputs, usage and latency, the CLI, and live mode with a fake client, including malformed responses. They need no network or credentials. As a mutation check, I broke the threshold comparisons and the denominator logic on purpose to confirm the tests catch each change. I also ran live collection against a real `SystemOneResponse` from typesafe-sdk 0.7.5 (no network) to confirm the answer fields match.

## Additional context

- AI disclosure: this PR was written with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code), and I reviewed and tested every line. I can't apply labels as a first-time contributor. Could a maintainer please add `llm-generated`?
- Open choices: the location is settled (`scripts/`, per review). The record field names and how failures and abstentions are counted are described on #8124 (cc @ketpatil77 @PRINCE2-AI); I'll adjust to whatever is decided.
- Size: about 1,250 lines, roughly half of them tests. I'm happy to split live collection into a follow-up PR if that's easier to review.
- Not run against the live TypeSafe API, since that needs credentials and live mode is opt-in.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Additive script and tests only; no changes to runtime CrewAI paths or dependencies beyond existing Pydantic usage.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **`scripts/jev_evaluation_runner.py`**, a standalone offline evaluator for TypeSafe Jev **Choice** routing and **Noul** guardrail decisions, plus a large pytest suite in **`lib/crewai/tests/test_jev_evaluation_runner.py`** that loads the script via `importlib` (no `typesafe_sdk` import).
> 
> The runner loads labeled **route** / **guardrail** records from **`.jsonl` or `.json`**, classifies each row (correct/incorrect/abstained vs accepted/rejected/**failed**), and emits a **Pydantic JSON report** with routing accuracy/coverage/abstention, guardrail false-accept/false-reject rates (failed rows excluded from those denominators), optional token usage and latency aggregates, and per-record outcomes with reasons. **Inclusive** `min_confidence` and `noul_threshold` apply; Choice and Noul scores are never mixed.
> 
> **`collect_live_decisions`** optionally fills missing decisions by calling a injectable **`system_one`** client (errors recorded on the record, collection continues). A **CLI** (`main`) evaluates a dataset file and prints the report; invalid input exits with usage errors.
> 
> Tests cover metric math, threshold edges, malformed datasets/decisions, CLI output, and live collection with a fake client.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 83c13e964655f5f1bebdb3dc9f3c29a226f1cf82. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: feat(memory): add backend record lifecycle and pagination tests
body:
## Related issue

Fixes #8135

Part of #8120.

## Summary

LanceDB and Qdrant Edge each had their own tests, so nothing checked that they behave the same way under the `StorageBackend` contract. `test_storage_backend_contract.py` runs one suite against both backends, using real stores in `tmp_path` and fixed vectors. Runtime code is unchanged.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Test round-tripping records and that update replaces the intended ID without corrupting other records.
  - `TestSaveAndGet` checks that every field survives `save` → `get_record`: id, content, scope, categories, metadata, importance, timestamps, source and private.
  - `TestUpdate` checks that the target ID changes while the other records, `count` and `list_records` stay the same.
- [x] Test newest-first list ordering with distinct timestamps and deterministic limit/offset cases.
  - In `TestListRecords`, records are one minute apart and saved out of order, so storage insertion order can't make the tests pass.
  - Limit/offset cases cover the first and middle pages, a partial last page, a limit larger than the total, offsets at and past the end, and scoped listing.
- [x] Test empty-store and missing-record behavior according to the StorageBackend contract.
  - `TestEmptyStore` checks that `count`, `list_records` and `get_record` return `0`, `[]` and `None` on a fresh store.
  - `test_missing_id_returns_none_on_populated_store` checks the same `None` on a store that has data.
- [x] Reuse backend-specific setup fixtures; do not build another fake storage engine or test framework.
  - The `storage` fixture builds the real `LanceDBStorage` and `QdrantEdgeStorage` the same way the existing tests do (`tmp_path`, `vector_dim=4`, the same `qdrant_edge` skip), using plain pytest parametrization.
  - It repeats that setup rather than sharing it, because `tests/memory/` has no `conftest.py`. Moving the fixtures into one would mean editing `test_qdrant_edge_storage.py`, which #7745, #7708, #7690 and #7687 also change.
- [x] Respect existing active fixes such as fix(memory): return newest records first in LanceDBStorage list_records #7418; new runtime defects need a separate reproduced issue.
  - Runtime code is unchanged. The LanceDB first-page and middle-page cases were `xfail(strict=True)` while `list_records` applied the limit before sorting (#7394). #7418 has now merged, so the markers are removed and both cases run as normal tests.
  - No new runtime defects were found.

## Verification

- [x] Tests added or updated for the changed behavior
- [x] Relevant tests and quality checks pass locally

- `uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/memory/test_storage_backend_contract.py`: 32 passed, stable under random ordering.
- `uv run pytest lib/crewai/tests/memory/`: 226 passed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format` (with `--no-force-exclude`, since tests are excluded in the config) and `mypy --strict` on the new file: clean.

## Additional context

Qdrant Edge scales stored embeddings to unit length for cosine distance, so the round-trip test doesn't compare vectors. The contract doesn't promise exact vectors from `get_record`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Test-only addition with no production code changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`test_storage_backend_contract.py`**, a parametrized pytest suite that runs the same scenarios against **`LanceDBStorage`** and **`QdrantEdgeStorage`** so divergences in the **`StorageBackend`** contract show up as failures instead of backend-only surprises.
> 
> Coverage includes empty-store behavior, save/get round-trips (all fields except embeddings for Qdrant normalization), batch save, **`update`** isolation, scoped **`count`**, and **`list_records`** ordering (newest-first with out-of-order inserts), pagination edge cases, and scope-prefixed listing. **No runtime changes.**
>
